4378.title: The years shortened and the order altered — the enemy thinks to change times and laws
4378.summary_md: The deepest corruption in Enoch's vision is not famine or sword but violence done to the reckoning itself: *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2). The lights are dragged into it, *And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.* (1 Enoch 80:6), and Enoch had already said where the fault would sit when the count went wrong: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). This is the little horn's signature in Daniel's night vision: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). The enemy's aim is the appointed times themselves. If he can shorten the year and shift the order of the stations, the feasts drift and the people keep the wrong days. Isaiah shows the cost when a people lets the ordinance be moved: *The earth also is defiled under the inhabitants thereof; because they have transgressed the laws, changed the ordinance, broken the everlasting covenant.* (Isaiah 24:5). The Creator wrote the reckoning into the lights, *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), so to alter the year is to assault creation's own covenant. The Torah is not the curse here; breaking the order is.
4378.note: 80:10-11 do not exist; the live 80:2 ('the years shall be shortened'), 80:6 and 82:5 carry the thought. Canon kept. Title adjusted.

4379.title: Not at their time — the feasts lost when the reckoning is lost
4379.summary_md: When the order is perverted it lands on the appointed times. Uriel says the moon herself will be thrown off, *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), and that the reckoning will be hidden from the very people who need it: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). The feasts are not human inventions to be set by convenience. They are Yahuah's (God's) own, fixed in their seasons: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* (Leviticus 23:2), *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* (Leviticus 23:4). Those seasons hang on the luminaries the Creator appointed: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). Jubilees foretells the same drift and names what Enoch's vision only shows, that losing the three hundred and sixty-four days is what loses the feasts: *For this reason the years will come upon them when they will disturb (the order), and make an abominable (day) the day of testimony, and an unclean day a feast day, and they will confound all the days, the holy with the unclean, and the unclean day with the holy; for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and feasts and jubilees. For this reason I command and testify to you that you may testify to them; for after your death your children will disturb (them), so that they will not make the year three hundred and sixty-four days only, and for this reason they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.* (Jubilees 6:37). The Creator's reckoning of whole solar days is the standard, and to lose it is to lose His feasts.
4379.note: 80:12 ('err as to the new moons, sabbaths, festivals, jubilees') is not in Charles — those words are Jubilees 6:37, which the summary already quoted. Re-formed on the live 80:4 and 80:7 with Jubilees carrying the feast list. Title adjusted since the live Enoch verse does not name the feasts.

4380.title: The fruits withheld and evil multiplied — the ground answers a broken order
4380.summary_md: When the order is perverted, the ground itself answers: *And in those times the fruits of the earth shall be backward, And shall not grow in their time, And the fruits of the trees shall be withheld in their time.* (1 Enoch 80:3). The rain goes with the fruit, *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2), and the chapter ends in judgment: *And evil shall be multiplied upon them, And punishment shall come upon them So as to destroy all.’* (1 Enoch 80:8). This is covenant cause and effect. Defile the everlasting covenant and the earth withers: *The earth mourneth and fadeth away, the world languisheth and fadeth away, the haughty people of the earth do languish.* (Isaiah 24:4). The drought and the famine are not arbitrary. The same hand that set the lights for the harvest seasons withholds the increase when men forsake His reckoning, and the remedy is never to abandon the order but to return to it.
4380.note: 80:6 'consumed by the sword' is invented; the live 80:2, 80:3 and 80:8 carry the withheld fruit and the judgment. Isaiah 24:4 kept; the sword sentence dropped with the quote. Title adjusted.

4382.title: Declare everything to thy son — the tablets read and handed down
4382.summary_md: Having read the heavenly tablets, Enoch is sent home with a commission to teach: *And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: ‘Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), for He is their Creator.* (1 Enoch 81:5). He is given one year to do it: *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). He kept the charge, and the next chapter opens with him doing it: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father’s hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1). This is the Shema's own charge to pass the way down the generations: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* (Deuteronomy 6:6); *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* (Deuteronomy 6:7). The Psalm says why the handing down matters, *That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children:* (Psalms 78:6), and the wisdom books say where the writing finally has to land: *Let not mercy and truth forsake thee: bind them about thy neck; write them upon the table of thine heart:* (Proverbs 3:3). The way is kept by being handed down, not invented.
4382.note: Both Enoch quotes were invented (the 'scribe of righteousness' call is not in ch. 81); re-formed on the live 81:5-6 and 82:1. Deuteronomy 6:6-7 and Proverbs 3:3 kept; Psalm 78:6 added from the verse index. Title adjusted.

4383.title: The righteous with the righteous, the apostate with the apostate — the year of testimony
4383.summary_md: Before Enoch is taken, the holy ones tell him how the testimony he leaves will divide the generations after him: *Let thy heart be strong, For the good shall announce righteousness to the good; The righteous with the righteous shall rejoice, And shall offer congratulation to one another.* (1 Enoch 81:7), *But the sinners shall die with the sinners, And the apostate go down with the apostate.* (1 Enoch 81:8). And they warn him that in the meantime the righteous will suffer for what others do: *And those who practise righteousness shall die on account of the deeds of men, And be taken away on account of the doings of the godless.’* (1 Enoch 81:9). This is the first Psalm's two ways laid out before a single generation has walked them: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalm 1:1), *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). The reckoning Enoch was about to hand to Methuselah is what the next chapter says the sinners will refuse: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). So the sorting is by the way a man walks and not by the house he was born in, and the one who keeps what Enoch wrote down walks with the righteous. The commandments were written to be kept, not altered, and the generation that forgets them goes down together.
4383.note: 81:6-7 ('perverse generation... alter the times') do not exist in ch. 81 — that wording is Jubilees 6:37. The live 81:7-9 carry the righteous-with-the-righteous / sinners-with-sinners sorting; re-formed there with 82:5 for the reckoning. Psalm 1:1 kept, 1:6 added from the index; Daniel 7:25, Genesis 1:14 and the Jubilees quotes dropped as they no longer answer the live verse. New title.

4384.title: Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness — no book of unrighteousness written
4384.summary_md: When Enoch has read the book of all the deeds of mankind, the first thing out of his mouth is a blessing on the one whose record is clean: *And after that I said: ‘Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness and goodness, Concerning whom there is no book of unrighteousness written, And against whom no day of judgement shall be found.’* (1 Enoch 81:4). The chapter closes with Enoch coming home the same way, *And in those days they ceased to speak to me, and I came to my people, blessing Yahuah (Lord) of the world.* (1 Enoch 81:10), and the blessing is spelled out in the next chapter for those who keep the reckoning as the sun keeps it: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). To walk in the reckoning is to keep the appointed times by the lights, the feasts that belong to the Creator and not to men: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts.* (Leviticus 23:2). This is the two-ways blessing of the first Psalm: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalm 1:1). And the voice John heard says the same thing Enoch said over the tablets: *And I heard a voice from heaven saying unto me, Write, Blessed are the dead which die in Yahusha (Lord) from henceforth: Yea, saith the Spirit, that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them.* (Revelation 14:13). The blessing is on the walk, written in a book, and it ain't new.
4384.note: All four Enoch quotes were invented; the live 81:4 ('Blessed is the man who dies in righteousness'), 81:10 and 82:4 carry the blessing. Leviticus 23:2 and Psalm 1:1 kept; Revelation 14:13 added from the index. Title adjusted.

4385.title: Men at fault in the reckoning — the four days they refuse to count
4385.summary_md: Enoch names exactly where the reckoning goes wrong in the hands of men: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5). The four days men drop are not optional; they are part of the year as the Creator counts it: *For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:6). Uriel had shown Enoch what that fault grows into in the days of the sinners, when the very stars are made to look as if they had changed: *And many chiefs of the stars shall transgress the order (prescribed). And these shall alter their orbits and tasks, And not appear at the seasons prescribed to them.* (1 Enoch 80:6). This is the same enemy Daniel names, the horn that *shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time* (Daniel 7:25). The lights were never men's to alter: *Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalm 104:19). To bow to the host of heaven instead of reading the order their Maker set is the idolatry the Torah forbade: *And lest thou lift up thine eyes unto heaven, and when thou seest the sun, and the moon, and the stars, even all the host of heaven, shouldest be driven to worship them, and serve them, which Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) hath divided unto all nations under the whole heaven* (Deuteronomy 4:19). Jubilees names the same falling away from the reckoning: *they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh* (Jubilees 6:37). The times and the laws stand; only the sinners think to change them.
4385.note: The 82:3 quote was invented (its wording is Jubilees 6:37, already quoted); re-formed on the live 82:5-6 and 80:6. Canon and Jubilees kept. Title adjusted.

4386.title: Blessed are all the righteous who walk in the reckoning of their days
4386.summary_md: Against the perversion of the count stands a blessing on those who hold the order: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4). Enoch says the wisdom that carries this reckoning is sweeter than food to the ones who take it in: *And those who understand it shall not sleep, But shall listen with the ear that they may learn this wisdom, And it shall please those that eat thereof better than good food.* (1 Enoch 82:3). This is the blessing of the first Psalm, hung on the man whose reckoning is the Creator's: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful* (Psalm 1:1), *But his delight is in the law of Yahuah (LORD); and in his law doth he meditate day and night* (Psalm 1:2). The days are reckoned by the sun because the appointed times are the Creator's own appointments and not man's: *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons* (Leviticus 23:4). To walk in the reckoning is to keep the feasts in their seasons. The Torah stands, and the keeping of it is covenant blessing and never a curse.
4386.note: Both Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:4 and 82:3 carry the blessing on the reckoning. Psalm 1:1-2 and Leviticus 23:4 kept. Title adjusted to the live words.

4387.title: The reckoning recorded for ever — the luminaries, months and festivals shown by Uriel
4387.summary_md: Enoch hands Methuselah an order that was recorded in heaven before any man counted a day: *For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:6). He is careful to say where the account came from and who stands over the lights: *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7). The lights keep their law because their Maker set them to it: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalm 104:19). Jubilees writes the same fixed measure onto the heavenly tables and binds Yashar'el (Israel) to it: *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts...* (Jubilees 6:32). The year of three hundred and sixty-four whole days is the Creator's covenant order. Man preserves it; he does not author it.
4387.note: Both Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:6-7 (the anchor span) carry the recorded reckoning and Uriel over the host. Canon and Jubilees kept. Title adjusted.

4388.title: The leaders who watch the seasons and festivals — the four who divide the year
4388.summary_md: Enoch sets out the ranks that govern the year, and he says plainly what they are for: *And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.* (1 Enoch 82:9), *And these are the names of those who lead them, who watch that they enter at their times, in their orders, in their seasons, in their months, in their periods of dominion, and in their positions.* (1 Enoch 82:10). The four who complete the year come first: *Their four leaders who divide the four parts of the year enter first; and after them the twelve leaders of the orders who divide the months; and for the three hundred and sixty (days) there are heads over thousands who divide the days; and for the four intercalary days there are the leaders which sunder the four parts of the year.* (1 Enoch 82:11), and they are named: *And these are the names of the leaders who divide the four parts of the year which are ordained: Mîlkî’êl, Hel’emmêlêk, and Mêl’êjal, and Nârêl.* (1 Enoch 82:13). The seasons and festivals these leaders watch over are exactly what Leviticus names as the Creator's own: *Speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel), and say unto them, Concerning the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), which ye shall proclaim to be holy convocations, even these are my feasts* (Leviticus 23:2), fixed by the lights of the fourth day: *...and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14). Jubilees ties the same heavenly tables to the feast of weeks as a perpetual renewing of the covenant: *For this reason it is ordained and written on the heavenly tables, that they should celebrate the feast of weeks in this month once a year, to renew the covenant every year...* (Jubilees 6:17). The leaders keep the festivals in their seasons because keeping the appointed times is how the covenant is renewed, and it ain't new.
4388.note: All three Enoch quotes were invented; the live 82:9-11 and 82:13 carry the leaders, seasons and festivals and the four names. Leviticus, Genesis and Jubilees kept.

4712.title: The heaven cast down, the earth swallowed — the deluge foreseen
4712.summary_md: Enoch's first dream-vision is the Flood seen from heaven's side: *And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.* (1 Enoch 83:4). He wakes crying out, and his grandfather tells him what he has seen: *And I recounted to him the whole vision which I had seen, and he said unto me: ‘A terrible thing hast thou seen, my son, and of grave moment is thy dream-vision as to the secrets of all the sin of the earth: it must sink into the abyss and be destroyed with a great destruction.* (1 Enoch 83:7). This is Genesis read from above. The sin that brings it is the very violence Yahuah (God) names to Noah: *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence* (Genesis 6:11), so that *Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth* (Genesis 6:13). The swallowing abyss of the vision is the very mechanism of the deluge, *the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened* (Genesis 7:11), until *every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground... and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23). Enoch's own book had already carried the word to Noah before the water came: *’Go to Noah and tell him in my name “Hide thyself!” and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The seed-war of Genesis 6 closes in water, and it ain't new.
4712.note: 83:5 re-pointed to the live 83:4; the 83:7 quote was invented and replaced with the live 83:7 (Mahalalel's reading of the dream). 10:2 stood. Canon kept.

4713.title: The heaven collapsed and fell to the earth — the heavens undone
4713.summary_md: The first thing Enoch sees in the dream is the sky itself coming down: *And regarding them I prayed to Yahuah (Lord). I had laid me down in the house of my grandfather Mahalalel, (when) I saw in a vision how the heaven collapsed and was borne off and fell to the earth.* (1 Enoch 83:3), and the earth under it giving way: *And when it fell to the earth I saw how the earth was swallowed up in a great abyss, and mountains were suspended on mountains, and hills sank down on hills, and high trees were rent from their stems, and hurled down and sunk in the abyss.* (1 Enoch 83:4). The prophets and the Revelation see the same unmaking of the heavens on the day of Yahuah (God). Isaiah: *And all the host of heaven shall be dissolved, and the heavens shall be rolled together as a scroll: and all their host shall fall down, as the leaf falleth off from the vine, and as a falling fig from the fig tree* (Isaiah 34:4). The sixth seal answers it: *And the heaven departed as a scroll when it is rolled together; and every mountain and island were moved out of their places* (Revelation 6:14), and the mountains Enoch saw suspended on mountains are those mountains moved out of their places. Peter binds the flood of water to the coming judgment by fire as one pattern: *Whereby the world that then was, being overflowed with water, perished* (2 Peter 3:6), so that now *the heavens and the earth, which are now, by the same word are kept in store, reserved unto fire against the day of judgment* (2 Peter 3:7). The first dissolution is the picture of the last. The same Word that drowned the old order keeps the present one for the day Enoch's vision foreshadows.
4713.note: 83:10 'rolled up like a scroll' is invented; the live 83:3-4 carry the heaven collapsing and the earth swallowed. Isaiah 34:4, Revelation 6:14 and 2 Peter kept. Title adjusted to the live words.

4714.title: Enoch the intercessor — that a remnant may remain on the earth
4714.summary_md: Mahalalel does not let the dream end in terror. He sends his grandson to pray: *And now, my son, arise and make petition to Yahuah (Lord) of glory, since thou art a believer, that a remnant may remain on the earth, and that He may not destroy the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 83:8), and Enoch does it and writes the prayer down for those who come after: *After that I arose and prayed and implored and besought, and wrote down my prayer for the generations of the world, and I will show everything to thee, my son Methuselah.* (1 Enoch 83:10). The prayer itself asks not for the wicked but for a seed: *And now, O Elohim (God) and Yahuah (Lord) and Great King, I implore and beseech Thee to fulfil my prayer, To leave me a posterity on earth, And not destroy all the flesh of man, And make the earth without inhabitant, So that there should be an eternal destruction.* (1 Enoch 84:5). Enoch stands in the office every true prophet fills afterward, the man who stands in the breach. Abraham bargains the same way before Sodom: *And Abraham drew near, and said, Wilt thou also destroy the righteous with the wicked?* (Genesis 18:23). Moses turns wrath at Sinai: *Turn from thy fierce wrath, and repent of this evil against thy people* (Exodus 32:12). Amos cries the prophet's plea for the small remnant, *O Yahuah (Lord) GOD, cease, I beseech thee: by whom shall Jacob arise? for he is small* (Amos 7:5), and *Yahuah (LORD) repented for this: This also shall not be* (Amos 7:6). Enoch is the first in that line, and the mercy of the Torah and the standing in the gap of the prophets are already here.
4714.note: The three Enoch quotes were invented; the live 83:8, 83:10 and 84:5 carry the petition for a remnant. Canon kept. Title adjusted.

4715.title: The days of Noah — the Flood as the pattern of the coming judgment
4715.summary_md: Enoch wakes from the vision crying out, *And thereupon a word fell into my mouth, and I lifted up (my voice) to cry aloud, and said: ‘The earth is destroyed.’* (1 Enoch 83:5), and his grandfather tells him it is no idle dream but the sin of the earth coming to its end: *My son, from heaven all this will come upon the earth, and upon the earth there will be great destruction.* (1 Enoch 83:9). That is the Flood set as the pattern for the end, and Yahusha (Jesus) makes the deluge the very figure of His coming: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:37), for *they knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:39). The title stands plainly there, the coming of the Son of Adam, the same Son Enoch's own Parables name. Peter draws the same line and presses it toward holiness: *Seeing then that all these things shall be dissolved, what manner of persons ought ye to be in all holy conversation and godliness* (2 Peter 3:11). And when the Flood has done its work the covenant mercy turns: *And Elohim (God) remembered Noah, and every living thing, and all the cattle that was with him in the ark: and Elohim (God) made a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters asswaged* (Genesis 8:1), the remembering that answers the petition Mahalalel sent Enoch to make, that a remnant might remain. The judgment is real, but it falls on a corrupt and violent generation; the righteous are remembered and kept, and the Torah is never the curse in it.
4715.note: 83:6 quote was invented; the live 83:5 and 83:9 carry Enoch's cry and the destruction from heaven. Matthew 24, 2 Peter 3:11, Genesis 8:1 kept.

4716.title: Thy dominion throughout all generations — the everlasting throne
4716.summary_md: Enoch opens his prayer by exalting the King over a reign that has no end: *‘Blessed be Thou, O Yahuah (Lord), King, Great and mighty in Thy greatness, Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the heaven, King of kings and Elohim (God) of the whole world. And Thy power and kingship and greatness abide for ever and ever, And throughout all generations Thy dominion; And all the heavens are Thy throne for ever, And the whole earth Thy footstool for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 84:2). This is the same confession Nebuchadnezzar is forced to make when his reason returns, *I blessed the El Elyon (most High), and I praised and honoured him that liveth for ever, whose dominion is an everlasting dominion, and his kingdom is from generation to generation* (Daniel 4:34), and *none can stay his hand, or say unto him, What doest thou?* (Daniel 4:35). The Psalmist sings the same crown: *Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.* (Psalm 145:13). Isaiah is shown the throne behind Enoch's words, *I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple.* (Isaiah 6:1), and the elders at the end echo the everlasting King: *We give thee thanks, O Yahuah Elohim (Lord God) Almighty, which art, and wast, and art to come; because thou hast taken to thee thy great power, and hast reigned.* (Revelation 11:17). The throne Enoch blesses is the same throne the four angels named when they first carried the cry against the Watchers up to heaven: *And they said to Yahuah (Lord) of the ages: ‘Lord of lords, Elohim (God) of gods, King of kings, and Elohim (God) of the ages, the throne of Thy glory (standeth) unto all the generations of the ages, and Thy name holy and glorious and blessed unto all the ages!* (1 Enoch 9:4). The sovereignty is total and ordered and cannot be shaken, and that is the ground on which a remnant can safely be asked for.
4716.note: 84:2 was a paraphrase; replaced with the live 84:2 in full. 9:4 re-quoted from the live text. Canon kept, with the stray single quotes around the canon quotes removed.

4717.title: Nothing hidden from Thee — the eyes on the throne
4717.summary_md: Enoch presses past the throne to the eyes of the One on it: *For Thou hast made and Thou rulest all things, And nothing is too hard for Thee, Wisdom departs not from the place of Thy throne, Nor turns away from Thy presence. And Thou knowest and seest and hearest everything, And there is nothing hidden from Thee [for Thou seest everything].* (1 Enoch 84:3). He is praying in the words the four angels used when they first brought the Watchers' deeds before the throne: *Thou hast made all things, and power over all things hast Thou: and all things are naked and open in Thy sight, and Thou seest all things, and nothing can hide itself from Thee.* (1 Enoch 9:5). Hebrews lifts that line almost word for word into the canon: *Neither is there any creature that is not manifest in his sight: but all things are naked and opened unto the eyes of him with whom we have to do.* (Hebrews 4:13). David knew there is no hiding from the same gaze, *Whither shall I go from thy spirit? or whither shall I flee from thy presence?* (Psalm 139:7), and the same enthroned eyes try the sons of men: *Yahuah (LORD) is in his holy temple, the LORD'S throne is in heaven: his eyes behold, his eyelids try, the children of men.* (Psalm 11:4). Nothing of the Watchers' secret arts is hidden from Him, which is exactly why Enoch can go on in the next breath to name their trespass and trust the verdict: *And now the angels of Thy heavens are guilty of trespass, And upon the flesh of men abideth Thy wrath until the great day of judgement.* (1 Enoch 84:4).
4717.note: 84:3 was quoted in 9:5's words and 84:8 does not exist; re-formed on the live 84:3 with 9:5 as its echo and 84:4 closing it. Hebrews 4:13, Psalms 139:7 and 11:4 kept. Title adjusted.

4719.title: Leave me a posterity on earth — the plea for a seed and the remnant left
4719.summary_md: Enoch's blessing turns to intercession, and he does not ask for a blanket reprieve. He asks for a seed: *And now, O Elohim (God) and Yahuah (Lord) and Great King, I implore and beseech Thee to fulfil my prayer, To leave me a posterity on earth, And not destroy all the flesh of man, And make the earth without inhabitant, So that there should be an eternal destruction.* (1 Enoch 84:5). Then he asks for the sorting that the Flood will carry out: *And now, my Lord, destroy from the earth the flesh which has aroused Thy wrath, But the flesh of righteousness and uprightness establish as a plant of the eternal seed, And hide not Thy face from the prayer of Thy servant, O Yahuah (Lord).’* (1 Enoch 84:6). The seed preserved through the water is one man and his house: *But Noah found grace in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD).* (Genesis 6:8), so that *Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark.* (Genesis 7:23). The plant of the eternal seed Enoch asks for is the remnant the prophets keep coming back to: *Except Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts) had left unto us a very small remnant, we should have been as Sodom* (Isaiah 1:9), *yet a remnant of them shall return* (Isaiah 10:22), and Paul reads the same thing in his own day as Yahuah (God) leaving Yashar'el (Israel) a seed: *Even so then at this present time also there is a remnant according to the election of grace.* (Romans 11:5). The election comes before the preserving. The righteous are already His, and they are the seed left, not a class anyone chooses his way into. Jubilees marks the same lone-survivor mercy, *no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone... for his heart was righteous in all his ways* (Jubilees 5:19), and Enoch's own commission to Noah had already framed it: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3). The flesh that aroused the wrath is swept off, and the plant of the eternal seed is established, and the two are held together in one prayer.
4719.note: 84:10-12 do not exist; the live 84:5-6 carry the plea for a posterity and the plant of the eternal seed. 10:3 stood. Micah 1:3 and Isaiah 64:1 dropped (they answered the invented 'come forth from Thy habitation' line); the rest of the canon kept. Title adjusted.

4721.title: The black bull gores the red — Cain and Abel, and the seed-war begins
4721.summary_md: Two bulls come forth with the heifer, and the seed-war is drawn at once in their colours: *Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (latter) came forth two bulls, one of them black and the other red.* (1 Enoch 85:3), *And that black bull gored the red one and pursued him over the earth, and thereupon I could no longer see that red bull.* (1 Enoch 85:4). The black bull is Cain and the red is Abel slain. The canon tells it plainly: *And Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground* (Genesis 4:2), and *Cain rose up against Abel his brother, and slew him* (Genesis 4:8). John reads the very seed-war the colours signal: *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous* (1 John 3:12). That is the line of the wicked one against the righteous line, the tares sown among the wheat from the first field, and Yahusha (Jesus) names that same sowing: *his enemy came and sowed tares among the wheat* (Matthew 13:25), *the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one* (Matthew 13:38). Jude marks the apostate by it: *Woe unto them! for they have gone in the way of Cain* (Jude 1:11). Enoch saw the black bull grow and go on while the red was seen no more, *But that black bull grew and that heifer went with him, and I saw that many oxen proceeded from him which resembled and followed him.’* (1 Enoch 85:5). That is the line of Cain woven in among the white, not the church and not a replacement, but the old seed-war Enoch saw before he ever fathered Methuselah.
4721.note: Draft had the live 85:3 only in part; quoted 85:3 and 85:4 in full and added 85:5 to carry the 'grew' the closing sentence refers to. Canon kept.

4726.title: Enoch taken up to the tower to behold the end
4726.summary_md: When the beasts begin to gore and devour one another, help comes down from heaven: *And I raised mine eyes again to heaven, and I saw in the vision, and behold there came forth from heaven beings who were like white men: and four went forth from that place and three with them.* (1 Enoch 87:2). Three of them take Enoch from among men and set him on a height to watch: *And those three that had last come forth grasped me by my hand and took me up, away from the generations of the earth, and raised me up to a lofty place, and showed me a tower raised high above the earth, and all the hills were lower.* (1 Enoch 87:3), and the charge is given: *And one said unto me: ‘Remain here till thou seest everything that befalls those elephants, camels, and asses, and the stars and the oxen, and all of them.’* (1 Enoch 87:4). This is the same Enoch the canon records was carried off from the generations of the earth: *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* (Genesis 5:24). He is set above to see the whole history play out in figures, the giants born of the stars, the fallen stars themselves, and the oxen of the patriarchal line, whose origin he had already been told: *And it came to pass, when men began to multiply on the face of the earth, and daughters were born unto them, That the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose.* (Genesis 6:2). The seed-war Enoch is lifted up to watch begins in Genesis 6, runs through the goring beasts, and ends only at the binding the white ones have come down to carry out.
4726.note: 87:5 does not exist (the giants' spirits line); dropped and 87:2 added so the white ones are introduced. 87:3-4 quoted from the live text exactly. Genesis 5:24 and 6:2 kept.

4729.title: The white bull instructed in a secret — born a bull, became a man, built the vessel
4729.summary_md: Out of the white line that runs from Adam a deliverer is raised, and he is not left to work it out for himself. One of the four is sent to him: *And one of those four went to that white bull and instructed him in a secret, without his being terrified: he was born a bull and became a man, and built for himself a great vessel and dwelt thereon; and three bulls dwelt with him in that vessel and they were covered in.* (1 Enoch 89:1). The white bull is Noah, and the three bulls with him are Shem, Ham, and Japheth. The secret he is taught is the one Genesis spells out in plain words: *Make thee an ark of gopher wood; rooms shalt thou make in the ark, and shalt pitch it within and without with pitch.* (Genesis 6:14), and then the reason for it, *And, behold, I, even I, do bring a flood of waters upon the earth, to destroy all flesh, wherein is the breath of life, from under heaven; and every thing that is in the earth shall die.* (Genesis 6:17). Peter counts the same household that Enoch saw covered in: *Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water.* (1 Peter 3:20). And Jasher remembers who closed the door: *And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and Yahuah (the Lord) shut him in.* (Jasher 6:15). Notice the order of it. The bull is chosen out of the herd and told the secret before a drop of water falls. He did not save himself by his own wit; he was instructed, he obeyed, and he was shut in and kept.
4729.note: 88:4 words live at 89:1 (live 88 has only three verses); re-cited, prose reworked, canon witnesses kept.

4730.title: The torrents and fountains — the cattle perish, the vessel floats, the earth dries
4730.summary_md: The Flood comes from above and from below at the same time. Enoch sees the roof of heaven first: *And again I raised mine eyes towards heaven and saw a lofty roof, with seven water torrents thereon, and those torrents flowed with much water into an enclosure.* (1 Enoch 89:2), and then the ground itself: *And I saw again, and behold fountains were opened on the surface of that great enclosure, and that water began to swell and rise upon the surface, and I saw that enclosure till all its surface was covered with water.* (1 Enoch 89:3). Genesis says it the same way, windows above and fountains beneath: *In the six hundredth year of Noah's life, in the second month, the seventeenth day of the month, the same day were all the fountains of the great deep broken up, and the windows of heaven were opened.* (Genesis 7:11). The whole herd of that corrupted earth goes under: *And all the cattle of that enclosure were gathered together until I saw how they sank and were swallowed up and perished in that water.* (1 Enoch 89:5). Only the vessel rides it out: *But that vessel floated on the water, while all the oxen and elephants and camels and asses sank to the bottom with all the animals, so that I could no longer see them, and they were not able to escape, (but) perished and sank into the depths.* (1 Enoch 89:6). Then the torrents are shut off and the earth comes back into view: *And again I saw in the vision till those water torrents were removed from that high roof, and the chasms of the earth were levelled up and other abysses were opened.* (1 Enoch 89:7), *Then the water began to run down into these, till the earth became visible; but that vessel settled on the earth, and the darkness retired and light appeared.* (1 Enoch 89:8). Genesis has Noah lifting the cover and seeing the same thing: *the waters were dried up from off the earth: and Noah removed the covering of the ark, and looked, and, behold, the face of the ground was dry.* (Genesis 8:13). Yahusha (Jesus) took this very scene as the picture of his own coming: *And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:39). The herd swallowed, the elect kept in the vessel, the darkness retiring and the light appearing. It ain't new.
4730.note: All five quotes moved to 89:2-8 (live 88 is three verses); the invented 88:12 'covered with verdure' replaced by the live 89:7-8; Jubilees 5:31 dropped (not in the live pool); Genesis 8:13 kept from the old text.

4733.title: The sheep saved from the wolves, the Lord who comes down, and the sea
4733.summary_md: The deliverer is one of the oppressed flock, saved out of the wolves' hands before he is ever sent back to them: *And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them.* (1 Enoch 89:16). That is Moses, carried off to Midian, and it is the Lord of the sheep himself who comes down at the cry of the flock. Then the sheep is called and sent: *And He called that sheep which had escaped the wolves, and spake with it concerning the wolves that it should admonish them not to touch the sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:17), and a second sheep goes with him into the wolves' assembly, which is Aaron at Pharaoh's court. The wolves do not let go, and so the Lord of the sheep leads the flock out himself: *And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep went with them, as their leader, and all His sheep followed Him: and His face was dazzling and glorious and terrible to behold.* (1 Enoch 89:22). At the water the picture is Exodus to the letter: *And that sea was divided, and the water stood on this side and on that before their face, and their Lord led them and placed Himself between them and the wolves.* (1 Enoch 89:24), and *And I saw till all the wolves who pursued those sheep perished and were drowned.* (1 Enoch 89:27). Moses wrote it this way: *And Moses stretched out his hand over the sea; and Yahuah (LORD) caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all that night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.* (Exodus 14:21), and *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) went into the midst of the sea upon the dry ground* (Exodus 14:22). Read the two side by side and the thing Enoch wants you to see is plain: Moses is a sheep, and a saved one, but the one who stands between the flock and the wolves at the sea is the Lord of the sheep in person.
4733.note: Invented 89:16/89:18 replaced by the live 89:16, 89:17, 89:22, 89:24, 89:27; Exodus 14 witnesses kept.

4734.title: Sinai, the covenant, and the house built for the Lord of the sheep
4734.summary_md: The sheep that led the flock out becomes a man and builds a house: *And I saw in this vision till that sheep became a man and built a house for Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep, and placed all the sheep in that house.* (1 Enoch 89:36). That is the tabernacle, the dwelling where the flock is gathered under its Shepherd, and it comes after the mountain. Enoch sets the Lord of the sheep before them on the rock first: *And after that I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep who stood before them, and His appearance was great and terrible and majestic, and all those sheep saw Him and were afraid before His face.* (1 Enoch 89:30). That is Sinai as Moses recorded it: *And mount Sinai was altogether on a smoke, because Yahuah (LORD) descended upon it in fire... and the whole mount quaked greatly.* (Exodus 19:18). There the flock is made a people set apart: *if ye will obey my voice indeed, and keep my covenant, then ye shall be a peculiar treasure unto me above all people... ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation* (Exodus 19:5-6). The covenant is the very ground of their being a flock at all, and the blood seals it: *And Moses took the blood, and sprinkled it on the people, and said, Behold the blood of the covenant, which Yahuah (LORD) hath made with you concerning all these words.* (Exodus 24:8). The house that Enoch sees raised in the wilderness later stands in stone: *it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were come out of the land of Egypt... that he began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (1 Kings 6:1). First the Lord on the mountain, then the covenant, then the house to hold the sheep. The order never changes.
4734.note: CHECK: the mechanical draft re-cited the house verse to 89:36; prose that leaned on the old 'saved sheep' and the old 89:23 'eyes opened' line mended; 89:30 added for the mountain scene.

4735.title: The sheep go astray, are forsaken, and given to the wild beasts
4735.summary_md: After the house and the tower, the flock turns away, and Enoch is shown what that costs: *And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of Yahuah (Lord) and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place.* (1 Enoch 89:54). The beasts are the nations, and the flock is handed to them: *And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:55). This is the scattering of the houses, and the canon names the first of them by king and by city: *In the ninth year of Hoshea the king of Assyria took Samaria, and carried Yashar'el (Israel) away into Assyria, and placed them in Halah and in Habor by the river of Gozan, and in the cities of the Medes.* (2 Kings 17:6). The cause was covenant-breaking, never the covenant itself: *the children of Yashar'el (Israel) had sinned against Yahuah (LORD) their Elohim (God)... and had feared other gods* (2 Kings 17:7), until *Yahuah (LORD) removed Yashar'el (Israel) out of his sight, as he had said by all his servants the prophets* (2 Kings 17:23). Ezekiel sees the same flock in the same teeth: *And they were scattered, because there is no shepherd: and they became meat to all the beasts of the field, when they were scattered.* (Ezekiel 34:5), *My sheep wandered through all the mountains... yea, my flock was scattered upon all the face of the earth, and none did search or seek after them* (Ezekiel 34:6). And the cry that goes up is the one Asaph taught the flock to pray: *Give ear, O Shepherd of Yashar'el (Israel), thou that leadest Joseph like a flock; thou that dwellest between the cherubims, shine forth.* (Psalm 80:1). The sheep given to the beasts are not thrown away. They are scattered, and a scattered flock is one that is still counted and still waited for.
4735.note: Invented 89:34-35 replaced by the live 89:54-55; 2 Kings, Ezekiel 34, Psalm 80 kept (Psalm 80:1 re-quoted in full from the live text).

4736.title: The seventy shepherds who destroy more than they were commanded
4736.summary_md: When the Lord of the sheep gives the flock over, he does not leave them unwatched. He hands them to overseers with a count: *And He called seventy shepherds, and cast those sheep to them that they might pasture them, and He spake to the shepherds and their companions: 'Let each individual of you pasture the sheep henceforward, and everything that I shall command you that do ye.* (1 Enoch 89:59), and he sets a recorder over the overseers: *And He called another and spake unto him: 'Observe and mark everything that the shepherds will do to those sheep; for they will destroy more of them than I have commanded them.* (1 Enoch 89:61). Then exactly that happens: *And I saw till those shepherds pastured in their season, and they began to slay and to destroy more than they were bidden, and they delivered those sheep into the hand of the lions.* (1 Enoch 89:65). The prophets know these shepherds by name and by habit. They feed themselves: *Son of Adam, prophesy against the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel)... Woe be to the shepherds of Yashar'el (Israel) that do feed themselves! should not the shepherds feed the flocks?* (Ezekiel 34:2), and *the diseased have ye not strengthened, neither have ye healed that which was sick... neither have ye sought that which was lost; but with force and with cruelty have ye ruled them* (Ezekiel 34:4). Yahuah (God) answers them as Enoch's book answers them, with a reckoning: *Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand* (Ezekiel 34:10). Jeremiah pronounces the woe, *Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:1), and Zechariah sees the worthless one judged in his own body: *Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye* (Zechariah 11:17). Every excess is written in a book before it is ever answered. The shepherds are the ones on trial here, not the sheep they were given.
4736.note: Invented 89:45 replaced by the live 89:59, 89:61, 89:65 (the commissioning, the recorder, the excess); the judgment itself belongs to the 90:25 thread; canon witnesses kept.

4737.title: The ram raised from the flock, and the house with the lofty tower
4737.summary_md: Between the scattering and the exile the vision shows the kingdom. The flock is being eaten by dogs and foxes and boars until a leader is raised from among the sheep themselves: *And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from their midst, which led them.* (1 Enoch 89:42). That first ram forsakes its glory, and a second is anointed in its place: *And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sent the lamb to another lamb and raised it to being a ram and leader of the sheep instead of that ram which had forsaken its glory.* (1 Enoch 89:45). Saul, then David, in colours. The second ram drives the beasts off, and under his son the house is built: *And that house became great and broad, and it was built for those sheep: and a tower lofty and great was built on the house for Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep, and that house was low, but the tower was elevated and lofty, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep stood on that tower and they offered a full table before Him.* (1 Enoch 89:50). The canon dates that tower: *And it came to pass in the four hundred and eightieth year after the children of Yashar'el (Israel) were come out of the land of Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon’s reign over Yashar'el (Israel), in the month Zif, which is the second month, that he began to build the house of Yahuah (LORD).* (1 Kings 6:1). And the ram raised out of the flock is the pattern of the one Shepherd the prophets were promised: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23), the Shepherd who says of himself, *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.* (John 10:11), and who names the scattered part of the same flock, *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16). The leader is taken from the midst of the sheep, and the house is built for the sheep. Enoch never shows a different flock moving in.
4737.note: The old summary's books, new house, and white bull were all invented at 89:41-50; the live 89:41-50 is Saul, David, Solomon and the temple, so the thread is re-formed on that and retitled. The books/new house/white bull are carried by the 90:20, 90:29, and 90:37 threads.

4738.title: The great horn raised — the eyes opened and the rams run to it
4738.summary_md: The sheep have been picked to the bone by the eagles and kites, and the few that are left are deaf and blind, until something new is born among them: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). The flock will not hear them, and the ravens tear at the lambs, and then the horn comes: *And I saw till horns grew upon those lambs, and the ravens cast down their horns; and I saw till there sprouted a great horn of one of those sheep, and their eyes were opened.* (1 Enoch 90:9), *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). The book of the Maccabees remembers the family this sprouted from, *In those days arose Mattathias the son of John, the son of Simeon, a priest of the sons of Joarib, from Jerusalem, and dwelt in Modin.* (1 Maccabees 2:1), and the son they set at the front, *As for Judas Maccabeus, he has been mighty and strong, even from his youth up: let him be your captain, and fight the battle of the people.* (1 Maccabees 2:66). But a horn that opens the eyes of the flock and gathers the rams to itself reaches past Modin to the promise Jeremiah carried: *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* (Jeremiah 23:5). The horn does not replace the sheep. It grows on one of them, cries to the rest, and they run to it because their eyes were opened to see.
4738.note: Invented 90:1 and 90:3 replaced by the live 90:6, 90:9, 90:10 (the lambs, the horn, the rams running); Maccabees and Jeremiah kept.

4739.title: The horn they could not break — the Lord of the sheep comes to its help
4739.summary_md: Every bird of prey comes against the horn at once: *And those ravens fought and battled with it and sought to lay low its horn, but they had no power over it.* (1 Enoch 90:12), *And I saw till the shepherds and eagles and those vultures and kites came, and they cried to the ravens that they should break the horn of that ram, and they battled and fought with it, and it battled with them and cried that its help might come.* (1 Enoch 90:13). The help is not its own. Heaven answers the cry: *And I saw till that man, who wrote down the names of the shepherds [and] carried up into the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep [came and helped it and showed it everything: he had come down for the help of that ram].* (1 Enoch 90:14), and then the Lord of the sheep comes himself: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them in wrath, and all who saw Him fled, and they all fell into His shadow from before His face.* (1 Enoch 90:15). This is the way the prophets always said the flock would be shepherded, by one the Lord sets up and stands behind: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23). The one shepherd gathers the fold that is not yet in the pen, *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16), and he is the one who said *I am the good shepherd: the good shepherd giveth his life for the sheep.* (John 10:11). The ram's horn holds because the power behind it is not the ram's. The Lord of the sheep came down for its help, and the sheep it cried for are his.
4739.note: Invented 90:7 and 90:10 replaced by the live 90:12-15; Ezekiel 34:23 and John 10 kept.

4740.title: The throne in the pleasant land and the sealed books opened
4740.summary_md: The staff falls first: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.* (1 Enoch 90:18). Then the seat of judgment is set in the land itself, and the record that has been kept all along is opened: *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). Daniel was shown the same throne and the same books: *I beheld till the thrones were cast down, and the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow, and the hair of his head like the pure wool: his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire.* (Daniel 7:9), *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). John sees the books opened at the last reckoning of the dead: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). The books in Enoch were written day by day as the shepherds destroyed, and sealed, and laid beside him. Nothing done to the flock was lost. The judgment reads back what was recorded.
4740.note: Invented 90:12 replaced by the live 90:18 and 90:20 (staff, throne, sealed books); Daniel 7 and Revelation 20 kept.

4741.title: The fallen stars and the seventy shepherds judged — the false shepherds reckoned
4741.summary_md: The reckoning goes in order. The first star and all that followed it are brought up first: *And Yahuah (Lord) called those men the seven first white ones, and commanded that they should bring before Him, beginning with the first star which led the way, all the stars whose privy members were like those of horses, and they brought them all before Him.* (1 Enoch 90:21), then the overseers of the flock: *And He said to that man who wrote before Him, being one of those seven white ones, and said unto him: ‘Take those seventy shepherds to whom I delivered the sheep, and who taking them on their own authority slew more than I commanded them.’* (1 Enoch 90:22). The sentence is given in the same order: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire.* (1 Enoch 90:24), *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). The stars are the Watchers who left their place. The shepherds are the appointed rulers of the exile who went past their charge, and the prophets had already put the charge against them in writing: *Woe be unto the pastors that destroy and scatter the sheep of my pasture! saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:1), *Therefore thus saith Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) of Yashar'el (Israel) against the pastors that feed my people; Ye have scattered my flock, and driven them away, and have not visited them: behold, I will visit upon you the evil of your doings, saith Yahuah (LORD).* (Jeremiah 23:2), and Zechariah's worthless shepherd gets the same sword: *Woe to the idol shepherd that leaveth the flock! the sword shall be upon his arm, and upon his right eye: his arm shall be clean dried up, and his right eye shall be utterly darkened.* (Zechariah 11:17). What goes into the fire is the misrule, the ones who took the sheep on their own authority. The sheep themselves are being gathered.
4741.note: Invented 90:15-16 replaced by the live 90:21-22 and 90:24-25; Jeremiah 23 and Zechariah 11 kept.

4742.title: The new house, greater and loftier — the New Jerusalem, the mountain of the house
4742.summary_md: The old house is not repaired. It is folded up and carried away, and a greater one is set in its place: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). And the whole flock comes home to it: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). John saw the same house come down: *And I John saw the holy city, new Jerusalem, coming down from Elohim (God) out of heaven, prepared as a bride adorned for her husband.* (Revelation 21:2), *And I heard a great voice out of heaven saying, Behold, the tabernacle of Elohim (God) is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and Elohim (God) himself shall be with them, and be their Elohim (God).* (Revelation 21:3). Micah saw it raised above every hill: *But in the last days it shall come to pass, that the mountain of the house of Yahuah (LORD) shall be established in the top of the mountains, and it shall be exalted above the hills; and people shall flow unto it.* (Micah 4:1). And Ezekiel names who the house is for, the two houses made one with the sanctuary set among them: *Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them; it shall be an everlasting covenant with them: and I will place them, and multiply them, and will set my sanctuary in the midst of them for evermore.* (Ezekiel 37:26). Read the words Enoch chose: the ones who were destroyed and dispersed are the ones who return. The new house is bigger because the whole scattered flock is coming back into it, not because a different people moved in.
4742.note: Invented 90:17 and reworded 90:19 replaced by the live 90:29 and 90:33; Revelation 21, Micah 4, Ezekiel 37 kept.

4743.title: The eyes opened, the sheep gathered — the awakening of the scattered houses
4743.summary_md: Through the whole long vision the sheep have been blind, and the last thing Enoch sees done to them is their sight given back: *And the eyes of them all were opened, and they saw the good, and there was not one among them that did not see.* (1 Enoch 90:35). It begins before the judgment, when the horn sprouts and cries: *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). And it ends with the whole flock inside, every one that had been lost: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The opened eyes are what the prophets promised for the day of the return: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5), *And in that day shall the deaf hear the words of the book, and the eyes of the blind shall see out of obscurity, and out of darkness.* (Isaiah 29:18). And the gathering is the two-house gathering Ezekiel was told to speak: *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21), the divided houses coming up under one head: *Then shall the children of Yahudah (Judah) and the children of Yashar'el (Israel) be gathered together, and appoint themselves one head, and they shall come up out of the land: for great shall be the day of Jezreel.* (Hosea 1:11). The eyes open first, then the sheep run to the one who cried to them, then they are brought home. That is the order Enoch saw, and it is the order the awakening is walking in now.
4743.note: Invented 90:10 and 90:18 replaced by the live 90:35, 90:10, 90:33; Isaiah, Ezekiel, Hosea kept.

5101.title: The book written for the generations — preserve it, hand it on, add nothing
5101.summary_md: The Epistle opens by naming what it is and who it is for: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). The charge behind that opening was given to Methuselah earlier in the book: *And now, my son Methuselah, all these things I am recounting to thee and writing down for thee, and I have revealed to thee everything, and given thee books concerning all these: so preserve, my son Methuselah, the books from thy father's hand, and (see) that thou deliver them to the generations of the world.* (1 Enoch 82:1), *I have given wisdom to thee and to thy children, [And thy children that shall be to thee], That they may give it to their children for generations, This wisdom (namely) that passeth their thought.* (1 Enoch 82:2). This is the Torah's own pattern for handing down the word, father to son to son's son: *And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart:* (Deuteronomy 6:6), *And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.* (Deuteronomy 6:7). And what is handed down is handed down whole: *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* (Deuteronomy 4:2), a fence John sets around the last book of all: *For I testify unto every man that heareth the words of the prophecy of this book, If any man shall add unto these things, Elohim (God) shall add unto him the plagues that are written in this book:* (Revelation 22:18). A book written for the generations is only any use to them if it reaches them as it was written. That is why it was given to a son with the word preserve.
5101.note: Invented 92:1-2 and 92:14 replaced by the live 92:1 (the anchor) with the Methuselah charge quoted from 82:1-2 where it actually lives; Deuteronomy and Revelation kept.

5102.title: Days appointed for all things — and the sinners who alter the order
5102.summary_md: Enoch tells his children not to be shaken by the times, because the times are not in the sinners' hands: *Let not your spirit be troubled on account of the times; For the Holy and Great One has appointed days for all things.* (1 Enoch 92:2). He had already shown them what the sinners would do to the appointed order: *And in the days of the sinners the years shall be shortened, And their seed shall be tardy on their lands and fields, And all things on the earth shall alter, And shall not appear in their time: And the rain shall be kept back And the heaven shall withhold (it).* (1 Enoch 80:2), *And the moon shall alter her order, And not appear at her time.* (1 Enoch 80:4), *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel names the horn that sets its hand to the same thing: *And he shall speak great words against the El Elyon (most High), and shall wear out the saints of the El Elyon (most High), and think to change times and laws: and they shall be given into his hand until a time and times and the dividing of time.* (Daniel 7:25). To change the times is to lay hands on the appointed feasts, and Jubilees, given on the same mountain as the Torah, says so almost word for word: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon.* (Jubilees 6:36), and *they will go wrong as to the new moons and seasons and sabbaths and festivals, and they will eat all kinds of blood with all kinds of flesh.* (Jubilees 6:37). The blood is the oldest line of all, from the days of Noah: *But flesh with the life thereof, which is the blood thereof, shall ye not eat.* (Genesis 9:4). The sinners can confuse the calendar and hide the order from themselves. They cannot move the days the Holy and Great One appointed, and that is why Enoch says do not be troubled.
5102.note: Invented 92:3 replaced by the live 92:2 (anchor) and the altered-order verses of 80:2, 80:4, 80:7 where the thought lives; Daniel 7:25, Jubilees 6, Genesis 9, Leviticus 17 kept.

5103.title: The righteous one arises and walks in the paths of righteousness — eternal light, and sin seen no more
5103.summary_md: Against the corruption of the order Enoch sets the one who rises from sleep and walks: *And the righteous one shall arise from sleep, [Shall arise] and walk in the paths of righteousness, And all his path and conversation shall be in eternal goodness and grace.* (1 Enoch 92:3). What he is given is not a lighter way but power to walk the right one: *He will be gracious to the righteous and give him eternal uprightness, And He will give him power so that he shall be (endowed) with goodness and righteousness, And he shall walk in eternal light.* (1 Enoch 92:4), *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). The Epistle says the same blessing plainly a little further on: *But in those days blessed are all they who accept the words of wisdom, and understand them, And observe the paths of the El Elyon (Most High), and walk in the path of His righteousness, And become not godless with the godless; For they shall be saved.* (1 Enoch 99:10). These are the two ways Moses set before the people at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments...* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter knows the same fork in the road: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6). And the eternal light Enoch promises is the life Yahusha (Jesus) defined in his own prayer: *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom thou hast sent.* (John 17:3). The paths of righteousness are the way of life, and grace is what gives a man the power to walk them.
5103.note: Invented 92:5 and 92:12 replaced by the live 92:3-5 (the anchor) and 99:10; Deuteronomy 30, Psalm 1, John 17 kept.

5104.title: A complete doctrine of wisdom — the law of the luminaries, exact and recorded
5104.summary_md: The Epistle names itself at the door: *The book written by Enoch—[Enoch indeed wrote this complete doctrine of wisdom, (which is) praised of all men and a judge of all the earth] for all my children who shall dwell on the earth. And for the future generations who shall observe uprightness and peace.* (1 Enoch 92:1). A great part of that wisdom is the law of the lights, which Enoch had closed out for his son a few chapters earlier: *And now, my son, I have shown thee everything, and the law of all the stars of the heaven is completed.* (1 Enoch 79:1). It was not his own reckoning. *And the account thereof is accurate and the recorded reckoning thereof exact; for the luminaries, and months and festivals, and years and days, has Uriel shown and revealed to me, to whom Yahuah (Lord) of the whole creation of the world hath subjected the host of heaven.* (1 Enoch 82:7), *And these are the orders of the stars, which set in their places, and in their seasons and festivals and months.* (1 Enoch 82:9). This is the fourth day of creation spelled out: *And Elohim (God) said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:* (Genesis 1:14). The seasons the lights are set for are the appointed ones, the feasts: *These are the feasts of Yahuah (LORD), even holy convocations, which ye shall proclaim in their seasons.* (Leviticus 23:4), and the Psalter keeps the same fixed order, *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down.* (Psalm 104:19). The lights that keep their stations preach without a word: *The heavens declare the glory of Elohim (God); and the firmament sheweth his handywork.* (Psalm 19:1). The calendar is not an opinion a man holds. It is a law written in the sky, shown to Enoch by the angel set over it, and recorded exactly so the feasts would fall where their Maker set them.
5104.note: Invented 92:6-7 replaced by the live 92:1 (anchor) and the luminary law at 79:1, 82:7, 82:9; Genesis 1, Leviticus 23, Psalms kept.

5105.title: The leaders of the stars keep their stations — and men who err by them take them for gods
5105.summary_md: Sin has an end in this book: *And sin shall perish in darkness for ever, And shall no more be seen from that day for evermore.* (1 Enoch 92:5). Set beside that the ones who never sinned at all, the chiefs of the lights: *And the leaders of the heads of the thousands, who are placed over the whole creation and over all the stars, have also to do with the four intercalary days, being inseparable from their office, according to the reckoning of the year, and these render service on the four days which are not reckoned in the reckoning of the year.* (1 Enoch 75:1). The stars keep their course; it is men who go wrong by them: *Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately.* (1 Enoch 82:5), and the error ends in idolatry: *And the whole order of the stars shall be concealed from the sinners, And the thoughts of those on the earth shall err concerning them, [And they shall be altered from all their ways], Yea, they shall err and take them to be gods.* (1 Enoch 80:7). Daniel shows the other end of the same sky, where the ones who keep and teach the order are made to shine like the lights they kept: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). Over those who fear the Name the true light rises: *But unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings; and ye shall go forth, and grow up as calves of the stall.* (Malachi 4:2). The heavens keep telling it: *Day unto day uttereth speech, and night unto night sheweth knowledge.* (Psalm 19:2). The lights never led anyone astray. The ones who hide the order and teach men to worship the lights are the ones whose sin perishes in the dark.
5105.note: Invented 92:11 and 92:13 replaced by the live 92:5 (anchor), 75:1, 82:5, 80:7; Daniel 12, Malachi 4, Psalm 19 kept.

5106.title: The plant of uprightness and the elect of the world — what Enoch learned from the tablets
5106.summary_md: Enoch opens the recounting with the ones it is about: *And Enoch said: 'Concerning the children of righteousness and concerning the elect of the world, And concerning the plant of uprightness, I will speak these things, Yea, I Enoch will declare (them) unto you, my sons: According to that which appeared to me in the heavenly vision, And which I have known through the word of the holy angels, And have learnt from the heavenly tablets.'* (1 Enoch 93:2). What follows is the planting itself: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), and the enclosure built around it: *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is the man elected, his seed the plant, Sinai the law and the fence.
