And at the far end the charge to the sons is the same one Moses gave the plant at the Jordan: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). Moses said it this way: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same fork: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), and Yahusha (Jesus) gives it its narrow gate: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat:* (Matthew 7:13). Sirach says it in one breath, *Before man is life and death; and whether him liketh shall be given him.* (Ecclesiasticus 15:17). The choice is set before a particular plant, the seed of the man who was elected, and it is the seed who are told to choose life so that they may be multiplied on the earth.
5106.note: Invented 93:7 and 93:2 replaced by the live 93:2, 93:5-6 (the anchor span) and 94:4; retitled to what the live chapter carries; canon witnesses kept.

5107.title: The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence — all who walk in unrighteousness shall perish
5107.summary_md: Enoch's own count of the weeks begins with a warning about where the wrong road ends: *And after me there shall arise in the second week great wickedness, And deceit shall have sprung up; And in it there shall be the first end. And in it a man shall be saved; And after it is ended unrighteousness shall grow up, And a law shall be made for the sinners.* (1 Enoch 93:4). The flood was the first end, and Noah the man saved out of it. Just before the recounting he had set the two roads before his sons in so many words: *And now I tell you, my sons, and show you The paths of righteousness and the paths of violence. Yea, I will show them to you again That ye may know what will come to pass.* (1 Enoch 91:18), *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19). The Psalter's first song ends on the same verdict: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). Solomon draws the two roads as light against dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day.* (Proverbs 4:18), *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble.* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) says which of the two has life at the end of it: *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it.* (Matthew 7:14). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the ungodly say it themselves on the day: *We wearied ourselves in the way of wickedness and destruction: yes, we have gone through deserts, where there lay no way: but as for the way of Yahuah (God), we have not known it.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:7). The way of violence is not struck down by some arbitrary hand. It has no way in it, and the ones who walk it perish on it.
5107.note: Invented 93:4 'cut off' replaced by the live 93:4 (anchor) and 91:18-19 where the two-paths words live; canon witnesses kept.

5108.title: The apostate generation, and the elect righteous chosen for sevenfold instruction
5108.summary_md: The seventh week is the one Enoch's sons live in: *And after that in the seventh week shall an apostate generation arise, And many shall be its deeds, And all its deeds shall be apostate.* (1 Enoch 93:9). And out of that generation, at its close, a company is chosen: *And at its close shall be elected The elect righteous of the eternal plant of righteousness, To receive sevenfold instruction concerning all His creation.* (1 Enoch 93:10). What the elect are instructed in is nothing other than the way the fathers walked, and the fathers named it as the two commandments. Jubilees has Noah charge his sons' sons *to bless their Creator, and honour father and mother, and love their neighbour* (Jubilees 7:20), and Abraham charge his house *that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour* (Jubilees 20:2). Moses gave the first of those its full weight: *And thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) with all thine heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.* (Deuteronomy 6:5), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the two side by side as the whole of it: *Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Thou shalt love Yahuah Elohayka (the Lord thy God) with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.* (Matthew 22:37), *And the second is like unto it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.* (Matthew 22:39). An apostate generation is one that has let go of both. The elect righteous at the close of it are the plant of righteousness coming back to the instruction the plant was given at the start. It ain't new. The same love of Elohim (God) and neighbour runs from Enoch to Noah to Abraham to the one who called it the first and second commandment.
5108.note: Invented 93:9-10 replaced by the live 93:9-10 (the anchor: apostate generation, elect righteous instructed); retitled; Jubilees, Deuteronomy, Matthew kept.

5109.title: The plant of righteousness, the law, and the enclosure — judgment and righteousness as the way
5109.summary_md: The third and fourth weeks are the planting and the fencing: *And after that in the third week at its close A man shall be elected as the plant of righteous judgement, And his posterity shall become the plant of righteousness for evermore.* (1 Enoch 93:5), *And after that in the fourth week, at its close, Visions of the holy and righteous shall be seen, And a law for all generations and an enclosure shall be made for them.* (1 Enoch 93:6). Abraham is elected as a plant of righteous judgment, which tells you what the plant is for, and the law given in the fourth week is the enclosure that keeps it. Micah summed up that law in a line: *He hath shewed thee, O man, what is good; and what doth Yahuah (LORD) require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy Elohim (God)?* (Micah 6:8). Abraham's own house was charged with the same thing in the same words: *And he commanded them that they should observe the way of Yahuah (God); that they should work righteousness, and love each his neighbour, and act on this manner amongst all men; that they should each so walk with regard to them as to do judgment and righteousness on the earth.* (Jubilees 20:2). The Epistle's woes are what it looks like when the plant forgets the enclosure: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). So the two ways here are not abstract. A plant elected for righteous judgment that tramples the lowly has left its own enclosure, and the humble walk is the fence it was given.
5109.note: Invented 93:5-6 'paths of righteousness are these' replaced by the live 93:5-6 (anchor: plant and enclosure); the reworded 94:6 re-cited to the live 94:6 and 96:5; Micah 6:8 kept, Jubilees 20:2 added from the live pool.

5110.title: The two ways — choose the paths of righteousness, that ye may live
5110.summary_md: Enoch frames the whole Epistle as a choice between two roads: *And now I say unto you, my sons, love righteousness and walk therein; For the paths of righteousness are worthy of acceptation, But the paths of unrighteousness shall suddenly be destroyed and vanish.* (1 Enoch 94:1). He warns off the one road, *And now I say unto you the righteous: Walk not in the paths of wickedness, nor in the paths of death, And draw not nigh to them, lest ye be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 94:3), and sets the other in front of them: *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). This is Moses' summons at the edge of the land: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). Jeremiah had the same two roads in his mouth: *Thus saith Yahuah (LORD); Behold, I set before you the way of life, and the way of death* (Jeremiah 21:8). The Psalter opens on it: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish* (Psalm 1:6), and Proverbs paints the two in light and dark: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day* (Proverbs 4:18) against *The way of the wicked is as darkness: they know not at what they stumble* (Proverbs 4:19). Yahusha (Jesus) set the same fork before the crowds: *Enter ye in at the strait gate: for wide is the gate, and broad is the way, that leadeth to destruction, and many there be which go in thereat* (Matthew 7:13), *Because strait is the gate, and narrow is the way, which leadeth unto life, and few there be that find it* (Matthew 7:14). It is one summons from Sinai to Enoch to the mount where he sat down and taught. Walk the way that has life at the end of it.
5110.note: 94:1 re-quoted from the live verse; the invented 94:23 replaced by the live 94:3-4; canon witnesses kept.

5111.title: Woe to you who trust in your riches — they will not deliver in the day of affliction
5111.summary_md: The woe is not on having money. It is on what the heart leaned on while the money was there: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Epistle says later what that trust is worth when the day comes: *And (then) the children of the earth shall see the wise in security, And shall understand all the words of this book, And recognize that their riches shall not be able to save them In the overthrow of their sins.* (1 Enoch 100:6). The Psalter had already weighed it: *They that trust in their wealth, and boast themselves in the multitude of their riches* (Psalm 49:6), and found that *None of them can by any means redeem his brother, nor give to Elohim (God) a ransom for him* (Psalm 49:7), because *when he dieth he shall carry nothing away: his glory shall not descend after him* (Psalm 49:17). Yahusha (Jesus) told the story of one such man and let him speak for himself: *Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry* (Luke 12:19), and then the answer, *Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). James says the same over the same departing wealth: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the rich say it themselves when it is too late: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8). The riches depart and the man who did not remember the Most High in the good days has nothing left to remember him by in the bad ones.
5111.note: Reworded 94:3 re-quoted from the live 94:8; invented 94:5 replaced by the live 100:6; Psalm 49, Luke 12, James 5, Wisdom kept.

5112.title: Your riches shall not endure — the sinner's glory withers and goes into the furnace
5112.summary_md: Enoch lets the rich man make his boast in full before he answers it: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer is in the next breath: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And in the woes before it the house itself goes: *Woe to those who build their houses with sin; For from all their foundations shall they be overthrown, And by the sword shall they fall. [And those who acquire gold and silver in judgement suddenly shall perish.]* (1 Enoch 94:7). The end of the splendour is the furnace: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). Ben Sira had mocked the hoarder's plan long before: *Whereas he says, I have found rest, and now will eat continually of my goods; and yet he knoweth not what time shall come upon him, and that he must leave those things to others, and die* (Ecclesiasticus 11:19). The Psalter's picture of the wicked's end is the grass: *For they shall soon be cut down like the grass, and wither as the green herb* (Psalm 37:2), and *the wicked shall perish... into smoke shall they consume away* (Psalm 37:20). James sets the rust on the hoard as a witness of fire: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Granaries full as with water, and lies that flow away like water. Enoch chose the same word for both on purpose.
5112.note: The two reworded boasts re-quoted from the live 97:8-9; the invented 94:12 and 94:16 replaced by the live 97:10, 94:7 (anchor) and 98:3; canon witnesses kept.

5113.title: Woe to you who feast in luxury and tread upon the poor
5113.summary_md: The woes turn on the ones whose table is laid on other men's backs: *Woe to those who build unrighteousness and oppression And lay deceit as a foundation; For they shall be suddenly overthrown, And they shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 94:6), and in the plainest picture of it, *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Isaiah had the same woe against the same appetite: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8), *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink* (Isaiah 5:22). Amos drew the very bowl: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph* (Amos 6:6). Yahusha (Jesus) set the woe right beside the blessings: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger* (Luke 6:25), which is the Epistle's own sentence on the ones who spread harm to their neighbours: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). And James closes it: *Ye have lived in pleasure on the earth, and been wanton; ye have nourished your hearts, as in a day of slaughter* (James 5:5). The lowly trodden under foot are the ones the Lord of the whole thing is going to answer for, and the feast built on their backs is what gets overthrown.
5113.note: Reworded 94:6/94:18 re-quoted from the live 94:6 and 96:5; invented 94:19 replaced by the live 99:11 (the anchor's far end); Isaiah, Amos, Luke, James kept.

5114.title: Woe to those who pervert the words of uprightness and transgress the eternal law
5114.summary_md: Enoch weeps before he pronounces anything: *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), *Who has permitted you to practise reproaches and wickedness? And so judgement shall overtake you, sinners.* (1 Enoch 95:2). The woes that follow fall on the systems of deceit, and the sharpest of them is kept for the ones who rewrite the standard itself: *Woe to you who work godlessness, And glory in lying and extol them: Ye shall perish, and no happy life shall be yours.* (1 Enoch 99:1), *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Isaiah's woes name the same inversion: *Woe unto them that call evil good, and good evil; that put darkness for light, and light for darkness; that put bitter for sweet, and sweet for bitter!* (Isaiah 5:20), *Woe unto them that are wise in their own eyes, and prudent in their own sight!* (Isaiah 5:21). Yahusha (Jesus) turned the same word on the self-satisfied of his day: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24). Notice what Enoch calls the thing they pervert. It is the eternal law, and the ones who alter it do not become something new and better. They transform themselves into what they were not, which is sinners, and they write their own sentence in the act.
5114.note: Reworded 95:1 and invented 95:2 replaced by the live 95:1-2 (anchor) and 99:1-2 where the perverted-words woe lives; Isaiah 5, Luke 6 kept.

5115.title: Woe to the lying witnesses, the false weights, and those who persecute the righteous
5115.summary_md: The heart of the chapter is a run of woes on the ways men wrong one another: *Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 95:5), *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish.* (1 Enoch 95:6), *Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous; For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.* (1 Enoch 95:7). The false balance and the false witness are the Torah's own list, and Amos saw both at work in the market: *Saying, When will the new moon be gone, that we may sell corn? and the sabbath, that we may set forth wheat, making the ephah small, and the shekel great, and falsifying the balances by deceit?* (Amos 8:5). Amos pronounced the same sentence on the ones at ease who did the weighing: *Woe to them that are at ease in Zion... That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph. Therefore now shall they go captive with the first that go captive* (Amos 6:1,6,7). The Epistle keeps the gold in the same hands: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8). James carries the cry of the defrauded into the last days: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). Riches weighed out with a false measure cannot stand, *for he that getteth riches, and not by right... at his end shall be a fool.* (Jeremiah 17:11). Requited according to your works is the whole of it. The measure a man uses on his neighbour is the measure that comes back on him.
5115.note: Invented 95:5 and reworded 95:6-7 replaced by the live 95:5-7 (anchor: requital, lying witnesses, false weights, persecution) and 97:8; retitled; Amos 8:5 added from the live pool; Amos 6, James 5, Jeremiah 17 kept.

5116.title: Where are your riches now? — the rich man's wealth perishes
5116.summary_md: Enoch's tears open the chapter, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and the Epistle goes on to stage the reckoning those tears are for: *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). The Parables let the mighty say what they see when it is gone: *For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, [nor glorified our Lord] But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory.* (1 Enoch 63:7), *Now they shall say unto themselves: 'Our souls are full of unrighteous gain, but it does not prevent us from descending from the midst thereof into the burden of Sheol.'* (1 Enoch 63:10), which is the Epistle's own woe: *Woe to you who spread evil to your neighbours; For you shall be slain in Sheol.* (1 Enoch 99:11). Yahusha (Jesus) told the scene as a story: *And I will say to my soul, Soul, thou hast much goods laid up for many years; take thine ease, eat, drink, and be merry. But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:19-20). That is the boast of the full granaries answered by the night of demand. And the Wisdom of Solomon puts the confession in the mouths of the proud when they have perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us? All those things are passed away like a shadow* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8-9). Unrighteous gain fills the soul and does nothing at all to keep it out of Sheol.
5116.note: Invented 95:12-13 replaced by the live 95:1 (anchor), 98:3, 63:7, 63:10, 99:11; Luke 12 and Wisdom kept.

5117.title: Fear not the sinners, ye righteous — the two paths and the way that lives
5117.summary_md: Enoch's woes are spoken through tears, *Oh that mine eyes were [a cloud of] waters That I might weep over you, And pour down my tears as a cloud of waters: That so I might rest from my trouble of heart!* (1 Enoch 95:1), and in the middle of them he turns to the righteous: *Fear not the sinners, ye righteous; For again will Yahuah (Lord) deliver them into your hands, That ye may execute judgement upon them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 95:3). The choice that governs the whole Epistle was set out before the woes began: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' covenant charge, life set against death with the seed's blessing hanging on it: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly... For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:1,6), and Proverbs lights the difference: *But the path of the just is as the shining light, that shineth more and more unto the perfect day. The way of the wicked is as darkness* (Proverbs 4:18-19). The way of violence perishes for ever, and the ones who walk the other road are told not to be afraid of the ones on it.
5117.note: Invented 95:17-18 replaced by the live 95:1 and 95:3 (anchor) with the two-paths charge from 91:19 and 94:4; canon witnesses kept.

5118.title: Woe to those who tread on the lowly with their might
5118.summary_md: The first woe in the chapter is on the ones whose money makes them look like the righteous: *Woe unto you, ye sinners, for your riches make you appear like the righteous, But your hearts convict you of being sinners, And this fact shall be a testimony against you for a memorial of (your) evil deeds.* (1 Enoch 96:4), and the next is on what that money was built on: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). The prophets had already named the crime. Amos: *Forasmuch therefore as your treading is upon the poor, and ye take from him burdens of wheat: ye have built houses of hewn stone, but ye shall not dwell in them; ye have planted pleasant vineyards, but ye shall not drink wine of them.* (Amos 5:11), and *they afflict the just, they take a bribe, and they turn aside the poor in the gate from their right.* (Amos 5:12). Isaiah carries it to the rulers who ate the vineyard: *Yahuah (LORD) will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof: for ye have eaten up the vineyard; the spoil of the poor is in your houses.* (Isaiah 3:14), *What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces, and grind the faces of the poor? saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD) of hosts.* (Isaiah 3:15). And the Torah's own protection of the afflicted stands behind every one of these woes: *Rob not the poor, because he is poor: neither oppress the afflicted in the gate:* (Proverbs 22:22), because *Yahuah (LORD) will plead their cause, and spoil the soul of those that spoiled them.* (Proverbs 22:23). Riches can make a man look righteous. The one who treads the lowly under foot has a heart that convicts him, and Enoch says that heart is the memorial that will be read.
5118.note: Invented 96:1 replaced by the live 96:4 and 96:5 (the reworded 96:4 re-quoted in full); Amos, Isaiah, Proverbs kept.

5119.title: Woe to the mighty who oppress the righteous — the day of your destruction is coming
5119.summary_md: Enoch's woes are bracketed by comfort to the ones being trodden on. He begins, *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), and *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). Then the woe on the strong: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8), and on the ones who forsook the only fountain, *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Yahusha (Jesus) spoke the same reversal in almost the same words: *But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.* (Luke 6:24), *Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.* (Luke 6:25). James says it over the hoard: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). And the Wisdom of Solomon lets the mighty confess it afterward: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), *All those things are passed away like a shadow, and as a post that hasted by;* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:9). The day of the mighty man's destruction and the good days of the righteous are the same day. That is why the righteous are told to be hopeful and the mighty are told woe.
5119.note: Invented 96:2-3 replaced by the live 96:1, 96:3, 96:6, 96:8 (anchor span); Luke 6, James 5, Wisdom kept.

5121.title: The mighty who oppress the righteous, and the furnace at the end of their splendour
5121.summary_md: The last woe of the chapter is on strength used against the righteous: *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8). The Epistle tells where that strength ends: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). James hears the cry of the ones whose labour paid for the purple: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4), and names the end of the oppression, *Ye have condemned and killed the just; and he doth not resist you.* (James 5:6). Ben Sira calls the withheld wage what it is: *He that takes away his neighbour's living slayeth him; and he that defraudeth the labourer of his hire is a bloodshedder.* (Ecclesiasticus 34:22). And the Wisdom of Solomon watches the proud blow away: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). Poured out as water, and gone like smoke. The righteous they oppressed get their many and good days on the very day the mighty are judged.
5121.note: Invented 96:8-10 replaced by the live 96:8 (anchor) and 98:2-3; James, Sirach, Wisdom kept.

5122.title: Be hopeful, ye righteous — the two paths and the fountain of life
5122.summary_md: The chapter opens on hope for the ones on the right road: *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1), *Wherefore fear not, ye that have suffered; For healing shall be your portion, And a bright light shall enlighten you, And the voice of rest ye shall hear from heaven.* (1 Enoch 96:3). The other road is named by what it drinks from: *Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:6). Enoch had set the two roads before his sons at the start of the Epistle: *And now, hearken unto me, my sons, And walk in the paths of righteousness, And walk not in the paths of violence; For all who walk in the paths of unrighteousness shall perish for ever.'* (1 Enoch 91:19), *But seek and choose for yourselves righteousness and an elect life, And walk in the paths of peace, And ye shall live and prosper.* (1 Enoch 94:4). That is Moses' charge at the Jordan: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *In that I command thee this day to love Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God), to walk in his ways, and to keep his commandments and his statutes and his judgments, that thou mayest live and multiply: and Yahuah Elohayka (the LORD thy God) shall bless thee in the land whither thou goest to possess it.* (Deuteronomy 30:16), *therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The forsaken fountain is the one Jeremiah wept over: *For my people have committed two evils; they have forsaken me the fountain of living waters, and hewed them out cisterns, broken cisterns, that can hold no water.* (Jeremiah 2:13). And the Psalter sets the same two roads: *Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly, nor standeth in the way of sinners, nor sitteth in the seat of the scornful.* (Psalms 1:1), *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). One road drinks from every fountain and withers. The other is told to be hopeful, because healing and light and rest are its portion.
5122.note: Invented 96:15-16 replaced by the live 96:1, 96:3, 96:6 (anchor span) and the two-paths charge at 91:19 and 94:4; Jeremiah 2:13 added from the live pool; Deuteronomy 30 and Psalm 1 kept.

5123.title: We have become rich — the riches that testify against the rich
5123.summary_md: Enoch lets the unrighteous rich make their speech, and the speech is the evidence: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: 'We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *And now let us do what we purposed: For we have gathered silver, And many are the husbandmen in our houses.' And our granaries are (brim) full as with water,* (1 Enoch 97:9). The answer turns their own picture on them: *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). And the day it is all read out: *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). James hears the hoard itself give testimony: *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days.* (James 5:3). Habakkuk had raised the taunt already: *Shall not all these take up a parable against him, and a taunting proverb against him, and say, Woe to him that increaseth that which is not his! how long? and to him that ladeth himself with thick clay!* (Habakkuk 2:6). Yahusha (Jesus) calls it what it is on the night it is exposed: *But Elohim (God) said unto him, Thou fool, this night thy soul shall be required of thee: then whose shall those things be, which thou hast provided?* (Luke 12:20). And the proverb gives the verdict Enoch is pronouncing: *Riches profit not in the day of wrath: but righteousness delivereth from death.* (Proverbs 11:4). The woe is on the acquiring in unrighteousness, not on possessing. The wealth gathered that way keeps a record of how it was gathered, and the record is read.
5123.note: Reworded 97:7 re-quoted from the live 97:8-9; invented 97:14-15 replaced by the live 97:10 and 97:6; James, Habakkuk, Luke, Proverbs kept.

5124.title: The prayer of the righteous reaches the Lord — and the days of your judgement come
5124.summary_md: The sinners are asked a question they cannot answer: *What will ye do, ye sinners, And whither will ye flee on that day of judgement, When ye hear the voice of the prayer of the righteous?* (1 Enoch 97:3), *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5), *And all the words of your unrighteousness shall be read out before the Great Holy One, And your faces shall be covered with shame, And He will reject every work which is grounded on unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:6). The ones praying are the ones the Epistle has just shown trodden under foot: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Amos drew that table, the couch, the feast, the bowl of wine, with the poor uncared for in the next room: *That lie upon beds of ivory, and stretch themselves upon their couches, and eat the lambs out of the flock, and the calves out of the midst of the stall;* (Amos 6:4), *That drink wine in bowls, and anoint themselves with the chief ointments: but they are not grieved for the affliction of Joseph.* (Amos 6:6). Isaiah ties the strong drinker to the cry of the oppressed: *Woe unto them that are mighty to drink wine, and men of strength to mingle strong drink:* (Isaiah 5:22), having already wept that the vineyard yielded *oppression... a cry* instead of judgement (Isaiah 5:7). James gives the cry a voice and an address: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The reapers' cry enters the ears of the Lord of hosts. Enoch calls it the prayer of the righteous reaching him, and says the day it arrives is the day the judgement of the ones at the table begins.
5124.note: Invented 97:5 and reworded 97:6 replaced by the live 97:3, 97:5, 97:6 (anchor) with 96:5 for the bowls; retitled to the live anchor; Amos, Isaiah, James kept.

5125.title: The sinners will become a shame and perish — the end of the splendour
5125.summary_md: The chapter opens with a word to the righteous to believe what they cannot yet see: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1), *Be it known unto you (ye sinners) that the El Elyon (Most High) is mindful of your destruction, And the angels of heaven rejoice over your destruction.* (1 Enoch 97:2). The Epistle has already described the splendour that goes into the fire: *For ye men shall put on more adornments than a woman, And coloured garments more than a virgin: In royalty and in grandeur and in power, And in silver and in gold and in purple, And in splendour and in food they shall be poured out as water.* (1 Enoch 98:2), *Therefore they shall be wanting in doctrine and wisdom, And they shall perish thereby together with their possessions; And with all their glory and their splendour, And in shame and in slaughter and in great destitution, Their spirits shall be cast into the furnace of fire.* (1 Enoch 98:3). And the woe that stands behind it: *Woe to you, ye rich, for ye have trusted in your riches, And from your riches shall ye depart, Because ye have not remembered the El Elyon (Most High) in the days of your riches.* (1 Enoch 94:8). The Wisdom of Solomon puts the lament in the mouths of the perished: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:8), and likens what they hoped in to dust: *For the hope of the ungodly is like dust that is blown away with the wind; like a thin froth that is driven away with the storm; like as the smoke which is dispersed here and there with a tempest, and passeth away as the remembrance of a guest that tarrieth but a day.* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:14). The purple and the grandeur are real while they last. Enoch's point is that the righteous should believe the end of them before it arrives, because the Most High is already mindful of it.
5125.note: Invented 97:11-12 and 94:4 replaced by the live 97:1-2 (anchor), 98:2-3, 94:8; retitled; Wisdom kept.

5126.title: The prayer of the righteous reaches him, and the riches of the unrighteous flow away like water
5126.summary_md: The chapter opens on the day the woes come due, and Enoch sets the two ends side by side so the righteous can hold on: *Believe, ye righteous, that the sinners will become a shame And perish in the day of unrighteousness.* (1 Enoch 97:1). What turns that day is not the strength of the righteous but their prayer, which is heard: *And in those days the prayer of the righteous shall reach unto Yahuah (Lord), And for you the days of your judgement shall come.* (1 Enoch 97:5). The men who built their lives on gathered silver hear the same verdict James will preach centuries later: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), and then the answer, *Yea and like water your lies shall flow away; For your riches shall not abide But speedily ascend from you; For ye have acquired it all in unrighteousness, And ye shall be given over to a great curse.* (1 Enoch 97:10). James heard the same cry rising from the reaped fields: *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The Psalm had already drawn the two roads, the one that prospers and the one that perishes: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). The righteous do not win the day by force. They pray, the prayer is heard, and what was gathered in unrighteousness runs off like water.
5126.note: old quotes 97:17-18 were invented (the two-ways charge lives in ch 91/94); rebuilt on the live 97:1-10 — prayer heard, riches flow away; new title; Deut 30 and Psalm 1:1/1:3 dropped, Psalm 1:6 and James 5:4 added from the index

5129.title: All your deeds are written down in heaven
5129.summary_md: Enoch takes away the one thing the oppressor counts on, that nobody sees. *I have sworn unto you, ye sinners, by the Holy Great One, That all your evil deeds are revealed in the heavens, And that none of your deeds of oppression are covered and hidden.* (1 Enoch 98:6). He will not let them talk themselves out of it either: *And do not think in your spirit nor say in your heart that ye do not know and that ye do not see that every sin is every day recorded in heaven in the presence of the El Elyon (Most High).* (1 Enoch 98:7), *From henceforth ye know that all your oppression wherewith ye oppress is written down every day till the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 98:8). The canon keeps the same ledger, and it records both sides of the page. Malachi saw the righteous written in: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). Later in the same book Enoch answers the sinner who says the record will never be kept: *And, although ye sinners say: “All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down,” nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day.* (1 Enoch 104:7). James says the fraud of the rich is already in the ears of heaven: *the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4). Nothing done to the poor is lost. It is written the day it is done, and the book waits for the day of judgement.
5129.note: 104:9 'books of the living opened' was invented; replaced with the live 104:7 (sins written down every day); 98:7 re-quoted in full

5142.title: Fear not, ye souls of the righteous — wait for the day of judgement
5142.summary_md: When the fire comes, Enoch asks the sinners a question they cannot answer: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). The whole creation shakes before that word, *And ye sinners shall be cursed for ever, And ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 102:3). Then he turns to the dead who died keeping the covenant, and the tone changes entirely: *Fear ye not, ye souls of the righteous, And be hopeful ye that have died in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 102:4), *And grieve not if your soul into Sheol has descended in grief, And that in your life your body fared not according to your goodness, But wait for the day of the judgement of sinners And for the day of cursing and chastisement.* (1 Enoch 102:5). Wisdom says the same thing about the same souls: *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them.* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:1). The world reads their death wrong — *In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:2) — *but they are in peace* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:3), *their hope full of immortality* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). The righteous dead are not forgotten in Sheol; they are told to wait, because a day is coming that settles the account. Daniel names who comes out of it: *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). They were written before they died. The day only reveals it.
5142.note: 102:3 'souls of the righteous in the hand of Elohim' is Wisdom 3:1, not Enoch; rebuilt on live 102:1-5 (fear not, be hopeful, wait); Wisdom and Daniel kept; title adjusted

5143.title: As we die, so die the righteous — the sinners' taunt over the dead, and its answer
5143.summary_md: Enoch lets the sinners say their piece over the graves of the righteous, and it is the oldest taunt there is: *And yet when ye die the sinners speak over you: ‘As we die, so die the righteous, And what benefit do they reap for their deeds?* (1 Enoch 102:6), *Behold, even as we, so do they die in grief and darkness, And what have they more than we? From henceforth we are equal.* (1 Enoch 102:7), *And what will they receive and what will they see for ever? Behold, they too have died, And henceforth for ever shall they see no light.’* (1 Enoch 102:8). The whole argument rests on the grave being the end, and the canon answers it at the grave itself. Daniel was shown the awakening: *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3), and Yahusha (Jesus) set the same shining at the harvest: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father.* (Matthew 13:43). Wisdom stages the very scene Enoch records, with the mockers now watching the man they mocked: *This was he, whom we had sometimes in derision, and a proverb of reproach* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:3), *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:4), *How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (Wisdom of Solomon 5:5). Malachi heard the same complaint in his own day, *It is vain to serve Elohim (God)* (Malachi 3:14), and showed the book that settles it: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16). The sinners counted themselves equal with the righteous dead because both went into the ground. The book of remembrance says otherwise, and the day of awakening reads it out.
5143.note: 102:7 'righteous shining like the sun' was invented; rebuilt on the live taunt 102:6-8 answered by Daniel 12, Matthew 13:43, Wisdom 5, Malachi 3 (all kept); new title

5145.title: Content to eat and drink and acquire wealth — whither will ye flee from the fire?
5145.summary_md: Enoch puts one question to the men who lived for their table and their takings: *In those days when He hath brought a grievous fire upon you, Whither will ye flee, and where will ye find deliverance? And when He launches forth His word against you Will you not be affrighted and fear?* (1 Enoch 102:1). He describes their life without any ornament: *I tell you, ye sinners, ye are content to eat and drink, and rob and sin, and strip men naked, and acquire wealth and see good days.* (1 Enoch 102:9). Against that he sets the end of the righteous, who had none of it and did no violence to get it: *Have ye seen the righteous how their end falls out, that no manner of violence is found in them till their death?* (1 Enoch 102:10). Yahusha (Jesus) names where that fire ends: *And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 13:42). Malachi saw the same day with its two sides: *the day cometh, that shall burn as an oven; and all the proud, yea, and all that do wickedly, shall be stubble* (Malachi 4:1), while *unto you that fear my name shall the Sun of righteousness arise with healing in his wings* (Malachi 4:2), and he closes the whole prophecy with *Remember ye the law of Moses my servant* (Malachi 4:4), because the Torah is what still stands on the far side of the oven. The Psalmist had already told the poor man not to be moved by what the rich man gathered: *Be not thou afraid when one is made rich, when the glory of his house is increased;* (Psalm 49:16). The good days Enoch's sinners saw were real, and so is the fire. The question of where to flee from it has no answer for a man whose whole life was the eating and the acquiring.
5145.note: 102:17-22 (kings, gods, 'where are your riches now') do not exist in Charles; rebuilt on live 102:1, 102:9-10; Matthew 13:42, Malachi 4, Psalm 49 kept; new title

5146.title: The oath: the spirits of the righteous dead shall live and rejoice
5146.summary_md: Enoch does not merely hope this; he swears it, and he says where he read it. *Now, therefore, I swear to you, the righteous, by the glory of the Great and Honoured and* (1 Enoch 103:1) *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2), *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3), *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). That is the resurrection hope the canon carries in the same words. Daniel saw the awakening: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2), and the wise *shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* (Daniel 12:3). Yahusha (Jesus) sealed it: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43). And the wisdom of the fathers said it plainly, *But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (The Wisdom of Solomon 3:1), *For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality* (The Wisdom of Solomon 3:4). What Enoch read on the heavenly tablets is what Daniel was shown and what the King spoke in the open. The righteous dead are kept, their memorial is kept, and they will live.
5146.note: 103:4 and 103:7 were quoted from the corrupt text; the oath lives at live 103:1-4 and is quoted there in full; canon witnesses kept

5147.title: Written in the holy books — the lot of the righteous dead, and the names that are blotted out
5147.summary_md: Enoch's assurance to the righteous rests on something he read, not something he guessed. *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2), *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). Their lot is written before they die, and their memorial does not go out with them: *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). Malachi saw the same book being kept: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), and John saw it opened at the end: *another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works* (Revelation 20:12), with the rest promised to the ones written there: *Blessed are the dead which die in Yahuah (Lord) from henceforth... that they may rest from their labours; and their works do follow them* (Revelation 14:13). Enoch's last book tells which way the pen moves on that page. Names are never added late; they are blotted out: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). The righteous were written before the Great One from the start. What the end does is keep the name or strike it.
5147.note: 103:2-3 quotes were invented ('books of life', 'names written'); rebuilt on live 103:2-4 (holy books, lot written, memorial kept) and 108:3 (blotted out); canon kept; title adjusted

5148.title: Blessed are the sinners, they have seen all their days — and then Sheol
5148.summary_md: Enoch lets the sinner's friends preach his funeral, because the sermon is the lie itself: *Woe to you, ye sinners, when ye have died, If ye die in the wealth of your sins, And those who are like you say regarding you: “Blessed are the sinners: they have seen all their days.* (1 Enoch 103:5), *And now they have died in prosperity and in wealth, And have not seen tribulation or murder in their life; And they have died in honour, And judgement has not been executed on them during their life.”* (1 Enoch 103:6). Then he tells them what the grave actually holds: *Know ye, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.* (1 Enoch 103:7), *And into darkness and chains and a burning flame where there is grievous judgement shall your spirits enter; And the great judgement shall be for all the generations of the world. Woe to you, for ye shall have no peace.* (1 Enoch 103:8). Yahusha (Jesus) told the same story about a man who died in honour and prosperity: *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom* (Luke 16:23), *I am tormented in this flame* (Luke 16:24). Revelation gives the end of it for the name not found in the book: *And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire* (Revelation 20:15). None of this is cruelty for its own sake. It is requital, measured to the deed, as Enoch had already said to the man who wronged his neighbour: *Woe to you who requite your neighbour with evil; For ye shall be requited according to your works.* (1 Enoch 95:5). The man who died with judgement never executed on him in his life has not escaped it. He has only postponed it to the one place he cannot buy his way out of.
5148.note: 103:6 and 103:10-11 were invented; rebuilt on live 103:5-8; Luke 16, Rev 20:15 kept, 95:5 from the mechanical re-quote kept; title adjusted

5149.title: They helped those who robbed us — the rulers who sided with the oppressor
5149.summary_md: The righteous bring their complaint to Enoch, and it is the complaint of every generation that has been eaten alive by the men who were supposed to protect it: *We desired to get away from them that we might escape and be at rest, But found no place whereunto we should flee and be safe from them.* (1 Enoch 103:13), *And we complained to the rulers in our tribulation, And cried out against those who devoured us, But they did not attend to our cries And would not hearken to our voice.* (1 Enoch 103:14), *And they helped those who robbed us and devoured us and those who made us few; and they concealed their oppression, and they did not remove from us the yoke of those that devoured us and dispersed us and murdered us, and they concealed their murder, and remembered not that they had lifted up their hands against us.* (1 Enoch 103:15). Enoch had already pronounced the woe on the men at the top of that table: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). The prophets and the brother of Yahusha (Jesus) sound the same alarm, and it is aimed at the heaping of land and treasure and the defrauding of labourers, not at persons. Isaiah: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place* (Isaiah 5:8). James: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1), *Behold, the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth* (James 5:4). The rulers in Enoch's chapter would not hear the cry. James says it went past them and was heard anyway. The wisdom of the fathers gives the oppressor's own verdict on the far side of it: *What has pride profited us? or what good has riches with our vaunting brought us?* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:8).
5149.note: CHECK found a second invented quote the grader missed ('103:15, 24' riches shall not endure); rebuilt on the live anchor 103:13-15 (the complaint to the rulers) with 96:5 and the canon witnesses kept; new title

5150.title: Two lots in one chapter: the righteous dead rejoice, the prosperous sinner goes down to Sheol
5150.summary_md: The whole of this chapter is built on two lots, and Enoch swears to both. To the righteous: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). To the sinner who died rich and honoured, with judgement never executed on him in his life: *Know ye, that their souls will be made to descend into Sheol And they shall be wretched in their great tribulation.* (1 Enoch 103:7). Between the two he records the complaint of the righteous in this life, and the words they use are the words of the exile curse: *We hoped to be the head and have become the tail: We have toiled laboriously and had no satisfaction in our toil; And we have become the food of the sinners and the unrighteous, And they have laid their yoke heavily upon us.* (1 Enoch 103:11). That is the Torah's own fork, and Moses set it before the people in the same two words: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), *I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter opens on the same two roads: *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalms 1:6). And the wisdom of the fathers shows where the road of the righteous comes out: *But the righteous live for evermore; their reward also is with Yahuah (God), and the care of them is with the Most High* (The Wisdom of Solomon 5:15). The righteous in Enoch's day felt like the tail. The lot written for them says they are not, and the way of life that leads there is the Torah itself, never the curse.
5150.note: 103:25 (two paths charge) does not exist; the chapter's own two lots (103:3 / 103:7) with the righteous' exile-language complaint (103:11) carry the thread; Deut 30, Psalm 1:6 (index), Wisdom 5:15 kept; new title

5151.title: Ye shall shine as the lights of heaven — companions of the hosts of heaven
5151.summary_md: Enoch swears to the righteous that heaven has not lost track of them: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Then he tells them what their shame turns into: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2), *Be hopeful, and cast not away your hope; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:4), and the company they are headed for: *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). Daniel was shown the same shining on the far side of the grave: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2), where *they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). Yahusha (Jesus) names the same hope at the harvest: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). And the Wisdom of Solomon sees the persecuted righteous vindicated in the same light: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). The shining is not something the righteous work up in themselves. Their names were already written before the glory of the Great One; the day of their visitation only makes visible what heaven already had on record.
5151.note: the mechanical re-quote had swapped in 50:2, which does not carry the shining; live 104:1-2, 104:4, 104:6 do; canon kept; title adjusted

5152.title: Your names are written before the glory of the Great One — blotted out, never added
5152.summary_md: Enoch puts the register first and the shining second: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1), *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). The name is on the page before the man is vindicated, not after. That is the canon's book of remembrance: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name.* (Malachi 3:16). Daniel ties the deliverance to the same book: *and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* (Daniel 12:1). And scripture only ever speaks of the pen moving one way on that page. Names are blotted, never written in late: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous.* (Psalm 69:28), which Yahusha (Jesus) confirms to the overcomer, *He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5). Enoch's last book says the same of the wicked: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). The ones who hear were already written. The warning about the blot is spoken to them, not to those who were never on the page.
5152.note: 104:3 and 104:8 were invented; the live 104:1 carries 'your names are written before the glory of the Great One'; 108:3 quoted in full; canon kept; title adjusted

5153.title: Every sin written down — and the sinners who alter the words and write their own books
5153.summary_md: Enoch answers the sinner who thinks the record is never kept: *And, although ye sinners say: “All our sins shall not be searched out and be written down,” nevertheless they shall write down all your sins every day.* (1 Enoch 104:7), *And now I show unto you that light and darkness, day and night, see all your sins.* (1 Enoch 104:8). Then he names the sin that will do the most damage to the generations after him, the handling of the words themselves: *And now I know this mystery, that sinners will alter and pervert the words of righteousness in many ways, and will speak wicked words, and lie, and practise great deceits, and write books concerning their words.* (1 Enoch 104:10). Over against those books he sets the ones written truthfully: *But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully—all that I first testified concerning them.* (1 Enoch 104:11), *Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom.* (1 Enoch 104:12). The Torah had already drawn that line around its own words: *Ye shall not add unto the word which I command you, neither shall ye diminish ought from it, that ye may keep the commandments of Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) which I command you.* (Deuteronomy 4:2), and Jeremiah watched the scribes cross it: *How do ye say, We are wise, and the law of Yahuah (LORD) is with us? Lo, certainly in vain made he it; the pen of the scribes is in vain.* (Jeremiah 8:8). The books that are written down every day and the books that were altered both come to the same table at the end: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12), where *whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.* (Revelation 20:15). The verdict is not arbitrary. The record was kept the whole time, and the men who rewrote the words of righteousness are in it.
5153.note: 104:9/104:12 'books of the living opened' were invented; the live anchor 104:9-12 is about sins written daily and sinners altering the words / books given to the righteous; built on 104:7-8, 104:10-12 with Deut 4:2 and Jer 8:8 added from the index; Rev 20 kept; new title

5154.title: The sinners growing strong and prospering — keep afar from their violence
5154.summary_md: Enoch does not pretend the sinners are losing in this life. He tells the righteous what to do while the sinners are winning: *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). The woe he had already laid on that prospering says how it was got and how it ends: *Woe to you who acquire silver and gold in unrighteousness and say: ‘We have become rich with riches and have possessions; And have acquired everything we have desired.* (1 Enoch 97:8), *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might.* (1 Enoch 96:5). Isaiah cried the same woe against the men who swallowed the land a field at a time: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place, that they may be placed alone in the midst of the earth!* (Isaiah 5:8). James turns it on the hoarders of the last days: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you.* (James 5:1), for *the hire of the labourers who have reaped down your fields, which is of you kept back by fraud, crieth: and the cries of them which have reaped are entered into the ears of Yahuah (Lord) of sabaoth.* (James 5:4). The woe is on the taking and the treading, on the system that wrings wealth out of labourers, and not on persons as such. And the chapter ends with the other recompense, the one that waits for those who kept apart from it: *And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.’* (1 Enoch 104:13).
5154.note: 104:14-24 do not exist; the woes live at 96:5 / 97:8 (kept from the re-quote) and the anchor 104:13 is the recompense of the righteous; built around 104:6; Isaiah 5:8 and James kept; new title

5155.title: The books given to the righteous teach the paths of uprightness
5155.summary_md: Enoch does not end this chapter with a father's charge in his own words; he ends it with the books. *Then, I know another mystery, that books will be given to the righteous and the wise to become a cause of joy and uprightness and much wisdom.* (1 Enoch 104:12), *And to them shall the books be given, and they shall believe in them and rejoice over them, and then shall all the righteous who have learnt therefrom all the paths of uprightness be recompensed.’* (1 Enoch 104:13). The paths of uprightness are learned from the books, and the books are the ones written down without change, as he had just said: *But when they write down truthfully all my words in their languages, and do not change or minish ought from my words but write them all down truthfully—all that I first testified concerning them.* (1 Enoch 104:11). That is Moses setting the two ways before the people out of the same written word: *See, I have set before thee this day life and good, and death and evil;* (Deuteronomy 30:15), pressed to its choice, *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live:* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The Psalter frames the same fork, *For Yahuah (LORD) knoweth the way of the righteous: but the way of the ungodly shall perish.* (Psalm 1:6). The way of life is a written way, and the Torah is that writing. The righteous who learn the paths of uprightness from it are the ones Enoch says will be recompensed, which is the same thing the King said of the man who does and teaches the least of its commandments: *Whosoever therefore shall break one of these least commandments, and shall teach men so, he shall be called the least in the kingdom of heaven: but whosoever shall do and teach them, the same shall be called great in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:19).
5155.note: 104:25 (two-paths charge) does not exist; live 104:11-13 carries 'the paths of uprightness' learned from the books; Deut 30 and Psalm 1:6 kept, Matthew 5:19 added from the index; title adjusted

5156.title: I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness
5156.summary_md: The Epistle ends with the Father speaking, and he does not speak alone: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1), *For I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen.* (1 Enoch 105:2). Read that slowly. The One speaking has a Son, and the two of them together are joined to the children of uprightness for ever. David heard the same voice speak to the same Son: *I will declare the decree: Yahuah (LORD) hath said unto me, Thou art my Son; this day have I begotten thee.* (Psalms 2:7), and the Son himself said what the union amounts to: *And this is life eternal, that they might know thee the only true Elohim (God), and Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ), whom thou hast sent.* (John 17:3). The children of uprightness are known by name before any of this, which is why they can be told to rejoice before the day comes. Malachi saw the book that holds those names: *Then they that feared Yahuah (LORD) spake often one to another: and Yahuah (LORD) hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), and Daniel ties the deliverance to it, *at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). The Father and the Son walking with their own in the paths of uprightness is the whole of the covenant said in one sentence, and the Torah is the path they walk it on.
5156.note: 105:1-2 quotes were invented and the prose was degraded; chapter 105 is two verses and the live 105:2 names the Father and the Son united with the children of uprightness — built on that, Psalm 2:7 and John 17:3 added from the index, Malachi 3:16 / Daniel 12:1 kept; new title

5157.title: Ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth
5157.summary_md: The last word of the Epistle sets the righteous over the earth, not as its owners by conquest but as its guides: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1). That is the inheritance the Psalter promised to the ones who waited rather than grabbed: *For evildoers shall be cut off: but those that wait upon Yahuah (LORD), they shall inherit the earth* (Psalm 37:9), *The righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein for ever* (Psalm 37:29). Yahusha (Jesus) set it as a beatitude, *Blessed are the meek: for they shall inherit the earth* (Matthew 5:5), and Daniel saw the kingdom handed to the same people: *And the kingdom and dominion, and the greatness of the kingdom under the whole heaven, shall be given to the people of the saints of the El Elyon (most High), whose kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and all dominions shall serve and obey him* (Daniel 7:27). The office they hold over the whole earth was named at Sinai: *And ye shall be unto me a kingdom of priests, and an holy nation. These are the words which thou shalt speak unto the children of Yashar'el (Israel).* (Exodus 19:6). This is no church standing in for Yashar'el (Israel). It is the covenant seed, the children of uprightness, set as guides to the children of earth in the reign, and the land-promise of the Torah stands under it. They did not earn the earth; they waited on Yahuah (God) and were kept, and at the end they are told to rejoice.
5157.note: 105:3 ('righteous shall inherit the earth') does not exist; live 105:1 sets the righteous as guides and recompense over the whole earth; Psalm 37, Matthew 5:5, Daniel 7:27 kept, Exodus 19:6 added from the index; new title

5158.title: Show it unto them — the wisdom of the righteous as a light to the children of earth
5158.summary_md: When the Epistle closes, the righteous are not told to hide their light and wait; they are sent: *In those days Yahuah (Lord) bade (them) to summon and testify to the children of earth concerning their wisdom: Show (it) unto them; for ye are their guides, and a recompense over the whole earth.* (1 Enoch 105:1). The wisdom shown to the children of earth is the light the prophets saw rising on the gathered: *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee.* (Isaiah 60:1). Daniel ties the shining to exactly this work of guiding others: *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever* (Daniel 12:3), after *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). Yahusha (Jesus) said the same two things to the same people, that they will shine in the kingdom, *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43), and that they are to be seen now: *Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.* (Matthew 5:14), *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 5:16). Isaiah promises the dust will give back the ones who shine: *Thy dead men shall live, together with my dead body shall they arise. Awake and sing, ye that dwell in dust: for thy dew is as the dew of herbs, and the earth shall cast out the dead* (Isaiah 26:19), and the Wisdom of Solomon sees the same sparks: *And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). The names were written first. Then they wake, they shine, and they show the children of earth the wisdom they were given.
5158.note: 105:4 ('shine as the lights of heaven') lives at 104:2, not 105; this thread is built on the live 105:1 charge to show wisdom to the children of earth, with Isaiah 60:1 and Matthew 5:14,16 added from the index; Daniel, Matthew 13:43, Isaiah 26:19, Wisdom 3:7 kept; new title

5159.title: Ye shall have peace — the end of the refrain that gave the sinners none
5159.summary_md: All through the Epistle one line keeps falling on the sinners like a hammer: ye shall have no peace. The last verse of the Epistle turns the same word the other way and gives it to the righteous: *For I and My Son will be united with them for ever in the paths of uprightness in their lives; and ye shall have peace: rejoice, ye children of uprightness. Amen.* (1 Enoch 105:2). Isaiah had the same refrain and the same division: *There is no peace, saith Yahuah (LORD), unto the wicked.* (Isaiah 48:22), *There is no peace, saith my Elohim (God), to the wicked.* (Isaiah 57:21). What stands between the two peaces is the day, and the Epistle's whole hope rests on that day coming.
