Isaiah saw it: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire* (Isaiah 66:15), *For by fire and by his sword will Yahuah (LORD) plead with all flesh: and the slain of Yahuah (LORD) shall be many* (Isaiah 66:16). Paul binds it to the revealing of Yahusha (Jesus): *And to you who are troubled rest with us, when the Lord Yahusha (Lord Jesus) shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels* (2 Thessalonians 1:7), *In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not Elohim (God), and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Yahusha HaMashiach (Lord Jesus Christ)* (2 Thessalonians 1:8). And the canon says plainly whose prophecy that coming was: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints* (Jude 1:14). The judgement falls on the ungodly for what they have done, not on persons for being persons, and on the far side of it the children of uprightness are told to rejoice, because the peace is theirs and the Father and the Son are with them.
5159.note: 105:5-6 (Most High arises in wrath) do not exist; chapter 105 ends on 'ye shall have peace' — built on that against Isaiah 48:22/57:21 (index) with the day of Isaiah 66, 2 Thess 1, Jude 14 kept; new title

5160.title: He will comfort the earth after all the destruction — Noah, the sign of what is coming
5160.summary_md: Lamech was afraid of the child, and Enoch's answer travels back down through Methuselah with two things in it: the boy is his, and the boy is a sign. *And now, my son, go and make known to thy son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.’* (1 Enoch 107:2), *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). The name itself is the promise, given before the flood it answers. Genesis names the grace that stood behind it: *But Noah found grace in the eyes of Yahuah (LORD)* (Genesis 6:8), *These are the generations of Noah: Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations, and Noah walked with Elohim (God)* (Genesis 6:9), and the verdict is spoken over him face to face, *And Yahuah (LORD) said unto Noah, Come thou and all thy house into the ark; for thee have I seen righteous before me in this generation* (Genesis 7:1). The choosing comes first and the keeping follows it. Elohim (God) saw the righteous one before the water rose and carried him through it, and the keeping is never a wage paid afterward for merit. Jubilees says the same of the one house: *no man's person was accepted save that of Noah alone; for his person was accepted in behalf of his sons, whom Elohim (God) saved from the waters of the flood on his account; for his heart was righteous in all his ways* (Jubilees 5:19). What Enoch read on the tablets reaches past Noah's own flood: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). The child who comforted the earth after one destruction is the sign of the generation that comes after the last one.
5160.note: 107:5 was invented; built on the live 107:1-3 (the name Noah, 'comfort the earth after all the destruction'); Genesis and Jubilees kept; title adjusted

5161.title: A generation of righteousness arises — the plant of righteousness after the destruction
5161.summary_md: Enoch read the whole arc on the heavenly tablets before Noah was weaned: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). The child's name carries the first instalment of that promise: *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). The keeping of his seed had already been ordered when the Watchers were sentenced: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3), and in the same breath the planting was named: *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16). The seed-line of the elect runs through Noah. One house is kept across the judgement, and from it the earth is replanted. The Messiah set his own coming against that same picture: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be* (Matthew 24:37), one righteous house preserved while the flood takes all the rest. The generation of righteousness Enoch saw written is not Noah's generation; it is the one that comes when transgression is destroyed for good, and Noah's preserved seed is the line it grows from.
5161.note: 107:6 and 107:9 were invented; built on live 107:1, 107:3, 10:3, 10:16 (10:16 stood); Matthew 24:37 kept; title adjusted

5162.title: Generation upon generation shall transgress — the violence that brings the judgement
5162.summary_md: Before he sends the word down to Lamech, Enoch reads the reason the flood has to come, and it is written as a pattern, not a single crime: *And I saw written on them that generation upon generation shall transgress, till a generation of righteousness arises, and transgression is destroyed and sin passes away from the earth, and all manner of good comes upon it.* (1 Enoch 107:1). Genesis gives the same verdict over the same earth: *The earth also was corrupt before Elohim (God), and the earth was filled with violence* (Genesis 6:11), and the sentence that follows it, *And Elohim (God) said unto Noah, The end of all flesh is come before me; for the earth is filled with violence through them; and, behold, I will destroy them with the earth* (Genesis 6:13). The flood is not wrath for its own sake. It is the answer to a corruption that had been taught into all flesh, the Watchers' teaching working itself out generation after generation until there was nothing left to spare. Jubilees describes the tide as it rose: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way... and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth* (Jubilees 5:2). The judgement lands on the corrupting system, and one righteous house is carried through it, which is why the same chapter can name the child: *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). Transgression runs on until the generation of righteousness arises. The flood was the first clearing of the ground for it; the last one is still ahead.
5162.note: 107:8 was invented; built on the live 107:1 and 107:3; Genesis 6 and Jubilees 5:2 kept; title adjusted

5163.title: He called the name of that son Noah — comfort after the destruction, comfort for the cursed ground
5163.summary_md: Enoch's reply reaches Lamech through Methuselah, and the fear over the strange child turns into a name: *And now, my son, go and make known to thy son Lamech that this son, which has been born, is in truth his son, and that (this) is no lie.’* (1 Enoch 107:2), *And when Methuselah had heard the words of his father Enoch—for he had shown to him everything in secret—he returned and showed (them) to him and called the name of that son Noah; for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction.* (1 Enoch 107:3). Genesis has Lamech give the name, and gives the reason in his own mouth: *And he called his name Noah, saying, This same shall comfort us concerning our work and toil of our hands, because of the ground which Yahuah (LORD) hath cursed* (Genesis 5:29). Jubilees keeps the same words: *and he called his name Noah, saying, 'This one will comfort me for my trouble and all my work, and for the ground which Yahuah (God) has cursed'* (Jubilees 4:28). Enoch looks forward to the comfort that comes after the destruction; Lamech feels the curse on the ground he is working now; both reasons hang on the one name, and both are right. The seed kept through the flood is also the comfort of the cursed ground, and Hebrews names what that one house did for the rest of the world by being kept: *By faith Noah, being warned of Elohim (God) of things not seen as yet, moved with fear, prepared an ark to the saving of his house; by the which he condemned the world, and became heir of the righteousness which is by faith* (Hebrews 11:7). The comfort was in the child before the flood came, and the name said so.
5163.note: 107:10 was invented; live 107:2-3 has Methuselah naming Noah 'for he will comfort the earth after all the destruction', set beside Genesis 5:29 / Jubilees 4:28 (Lamech's reason) and Hebrews 11:7, all kept; title adjusted

5166.title: Those born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous are resplendent
5166.summary_md: The last page of the book shows the two ends at the same moment, and it is the Father himself speaking: *And now I will summon the spirits of the good who belong to the generation of light, and I will transform those who were born in darkness, who in the flesh were not recompensed with such honour as their faithfulness deserved.* (1 Enoch 108:11), *And I will bring forth in shining light those who have loved My holy name, and I will seat each on the throne of his honour.* (1 Enoch 108:12), *And they shall be resplendent for times without number; for righteousness is the judgement of Elohim (God); for to the faithful He will give faithfulness in the habitation of upright paths.* (1 Enoch 108:13). Then the other side of it: *And they shall see those who were born in darkness led into darkness, while the righteous shall be resplendent.* (1 Enoch 108:14), *And the sinners shall cry aloud and see them resplendent, and they indeed will go where days and seasons are prescribed for them.’* (1 Enoch 108:15). The place they go to was shown to Enoch a few verses earlier: *And he said unto me: ‘This place which thou seest—here are cast the spirits of sinners and blasphemers, and of those who work wickedness, and of those who pervert everything that Yahuah (Lord) hath spoken through the mouth of the prophets—(even) the things that shall be.* (1 Enoch 108:6). That is the canon's own last picture: *they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched* (Isaiah 66:24), the verse Yahusha (Jesus) pressed three times. The parable of the tares has the same two halves in the same order, *And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth* (Matthew 13:42), and then, *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father* (Matthew 13:43). The sinners see the righteous resplendent and cry aloud. They were not condemned for being born; they were sent where they had chosen to go, the ones who perverted everything spoken through the prophets, and righteousness is the judgement that sends them.
5166.note: 108:11-13 quoted from the corrupt text (the woes live at 100:7/100:9) and 104:6 invented; rebuilt on the live anchor 108:11-15 with 108:6; Isaiah 66:24, Matthew 13:42-43 kept; new title

5167.title: The two ways — the good keep the law to the end
5167.summary_md: The closing book names its readers in its first line, and they are the keepers of the law: *Another book which Enoch wrote for his son Methuselah and for those who will come after him, and keep the law in the last days.* (1 Enoch 108:1), *Ye who have done good shall wait for those days till an end is made of those who work evil, and an end of the might of the transgressors.* (1 Enoch 108:2). That is the two ways of the whole Epistle, the same choice set down once at Sinai's gate: *I call heaven and earth to record this day against you, that I have set before you life and death, blessing and cursing: therefore choose life, that both thou and thy seed may live* (Deuteronomy 30:19). The good keep the law and wait while an end is made of the transgressors, because the Torah is the way of life and never the curse. The other half of the page describes what the good did not love: *Who love Elohim (God) and loved neither gold nor silver nor any of the good things which are in the world, but gave over their bodies to torture.* (1 Enoch 108:8), *And all the blessings destined for them I have recounted in the books. And He hath assigned them their recompense, because they have been found to be such as loved heaven more than their life in the world, and though they were trodden under foot of wicked men, and experienced abuse and reviling from them and were put to shame, yet they blessed Me.* (1 Enoch 108:10). The ones who trod them under foot are the hoarders James names plainly: *Go to now, ye rich men, weep and howl for your miseries that shall come upon you* (James 5:1), *Your gold and silver is cankered; and the rust of them shall be a witness against you, and shall eat your flesh as it were fire. Ye have heaped treasure together for the last days* (James 5:3). Isaiah pronounces the same woe on the systems that swallow the land: *Woe unto them that join house to house, that lay field to field, till there be no place* (Isaiah 5:8). The two ways divide the keeper of the law, who loved heaven more than his life, from the oppressor whose gold burns him.
5167.note: CHECK: 108:16 and 108:10 quotes were invented (ch 108 has 15 verses); re-quoted 108:1-2 in full and set 108:8 / 108:10 (live) in place of the invented riches lines; Deut 30:19, James, Isaiah kept

11049.title: The cherub and the flaming sword at the eastern gate
11049.summary_md: Adam and Eve, blind with sorrow, climb the border of the garden until they stand at the gate they may no longer enter: *And the cherub who guarded the garden was standing at the western gate, and guarding it against Adam and Eve, lest they should suddenly come into the garden* (1-adam-eve 54:3); *suddenly came the cherub with a flashing sword of fire in his hand* (1-adam-eve 54:4). This is the very scene Moses sealed at the close of Eden: *Therefore Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) sent him forth from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from whence he was taken* (Genesis 3:23), and *he placed at the east of the garden of Eden Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Jubilees keeps the same memory of the sending-forth: *And He made for them coats of skin, and clothed them, and sent them forth from the Garden of Eden* (Jubilees 3:26). Enoch was carried to the same garden and shown the tree that put them outside it, and the angel told him whose parents had eaten from it: *Then Raphael the holy angel, who was with me, answered me and said: ‘This is the tree of wisdom, of which thy father old (in years) and thy aged mother, who were before thee, have eaten, and they learnt wisdom and their eyes were opened, and they knew that they were naked and they were driven out of the garden.’* (1 Enoch 32:6). From the first day outside the garden the way to life is guarded, and it stays guarded until the Lamb opens it again: *Blessed are they that do his commandments, that they may have right to the tree of life, and may enter in through the gates into the city* (Revelation 22:14).
11049.note: 32:4 'tree of life' quote was invented (32:4 is the tree of wisdom); the live 32:6 names Adam and Eve eating and driven out, which is the thread's own scene; rest kept verbatim

38640.title: I saw Yahuah on his throne, and all the host of heaven
38640.summary_md: Micaiah lifts the veil on the heavenly court: *Hear thou therefore the word of Yahuah (LORD): I saw Yahuah (LORD) sitting on his throne, and all the host of heaven standing by him on his right hand and on his left* (1 Kings 22:19). This is Yahuah (God) enthroned amid the divine council, the Most High on his throne, the host of heaven his ministers and witnesses, deliberating over the fall of Ahab. It is the same court the other seers are shown. Job sees it: *Now there was a day when the sons of Elohim (God) came to present themselves before Yahuah (LORD)* (Job 1:6). Daniel beholds the enthroned Most High in fire: *the Ancient of days did sit, whose garment was white as snow... his throne was like the fiery flame* (Daniel 7:9), attended by the innumerable host — *thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set* (Daniel 7:10). Isaiah's call is word for word Micaiah's sight: *I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple* (Isaiah 6:1). And John on Patmos hears the same numberless company — *the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands* (Revelation 5:11) — round about the throne. Enoch is carried up into the same house and sees the same throne with the same host before it: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim.* (1 Enoch 14:18), *And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:20), *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). One throne, one Most High, one host of heaven encircling him in counsel and in worship. This is not a co-equal trinity and not an Arian counterfeit either: the Father is the enthroned Most High, and the host, including the spirit who comes forth and *stood before Yahuah* (22:21), stand before him as servants who do his bidding.
38640.note: CHECK: the mechanical re-quote had swapped the throne for 18:8 (a mountain 'like the throne'); the throne vision is live 14:18-22, quoted there (14:22's ten thousand times ten thousand matches Daniel 7:10); rest kept

14531.title: The spirits in prison — the days of Noah — the Watchers (Genesis 6, 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Jude)
14531.summary_md: Peter gathers the whole story into a few verses. *For Messiah (Christ) also hath once suffered for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to Elohim (God), being put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit: By which also he went and preached unto the spirits in prison; Which sometime were disobedient, when once the longsuffering of Elohim (God) waited in the days of Noah, while the ark was a preparing, wherein few, that is, eight souls were saved by water* (1 Peter 3:18-20). The *spirits in prison* who *were disobedient... in the days of Noah* are the fallen ones of Genesis 6: *the sons of Elohim (God) saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives of all which they chose* (Genesis 6:2), and *there were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:4), so that *the wickedness of man was great in the earth* (Genesis 6:5) and the longsuffering of Yahuah (LORD) waited while Noah built. The Hebrew library narrates the imprisonment Peter assumes. Yahuah (God) commands Raphael, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness* (1 Enoch 10:4), and Michael to bind Semjaza and his associates: *bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement* (1 Enoch 10:12), *to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13). Enoch the scribe is sent to *declare to the Watchers of the heaven who have left the high heaven... and have taken unto themselves wives* (1 Enoch 12:4), saying *Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds* (1 Enoch 13:1) — the pattern of a righteous one sent to proclaim to the bound spirits. Enoch is shown the place itself: *The angel said: ‘This place is the end of heaven and earth: this has become a prison for the stars and the host of heaven. And the stars which roll over the fire are they which have transgressed the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) in the beginning of their rising, because they did not come forth at their appointed times.* (1 Enoch 18:14-15), *And He was wroth with them, and bound them till the time when their guilt should be consummated (even) for ten thousand years.’* (1 Enoch 18:16), and the angel says plainly of it, *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees tells the same days: *the angels of Elohim (God)... took themselves wives of all whom they chose, and they bare to them sons and they were giants* (Jubilees 5:1); Yahuah (God) *bade us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold they are bound* (Jubilees 5:6), *bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:10). The apostolic witnesses confirm the one narrative: *the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 6), and *Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). One story runs from Genesis 6 through 1 Enoch and Jubilees to Jude, 2 Peter, and here: the Watchers, the giants, the Flood, the prison of bound spirits reserved unto judgement. Keep the order Peter keeps: it is the Son, *put to death in the flesh, but quickened by the Spirit,* who *went and preached unto the spirits in prison.* The Son is the one put to death and made alive again and sent to proclaim; the Father is the one who quickens and raises him — *the resurrection of Yahusha HaMashiach (Jesus Christ)* (1 Peter 3:21) — and exalts him to his right hand (1 Peter 3:22). The proclamation to the imprisoned spirits is no rescue of the rebel angels but the announcement of the sentence already gone forth, the same *no peace* Enoch carried to the bound Watchers of old.
14531.note: 21:11 is gone (now 21:10) and 18:14/21:5 moved — mechanical re-quotes kept, the sentence re-ordered to read, and an internal editorial note (CHRISTOLOGY — keep the order…) removed from reader-facing text

13704.title: The earth gives back her dead: the day of resurrection in the Hebrew library (2 Esdras 7, 1 Enoch 51)
13704.summary_md: The hope Paul preached — *the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first* (1 Thessalonians 4:16) — the restored library held before him, beholding the earth and the grave surrendering the asleep. The seer of Esdras saw it: *the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them* (2 Esdras 7:32). And Enoch beheld the same: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1), *And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:2), *For in those days the Elect One shall arise, And the earth shall rejoice, And the righteous shall dwell upon it, And the elect shall walk thereon.* (1 Enoch 51:5). The earth restoring the asleep, Sheol giving back what it received, the righteous chosen out from among them at the arising of the Elect One — this is *Yahuah (Lord) himself shall descend from heaven... and the dead in Messiah (Christ) shall rise first.* The hope is one; the risings are two. At his coming the dead in Messiah (Christ) rise first — the righteous seed out of Sheol, the first resurrection, that the chosen should be saved. After the reign the earth gives up the rest of her dead to the judgment of the dead, the great resurrection. Not a secret snatching severed from the people, but the asleep raised each in their own order.
13704.note: CHECK: the re-quote had trimmed the old 51:1 quote so the prose's 'arising of the Elect One' and 'chosen' had no verse; 51:2 and 51:5 added in full; rest kept

13706.title: Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day (Isaiah 60, 1 Enoch 58)
13706.summary_md: *Ye are all the children of light, and the children of the day: we are not of the night, nor of darkness* (1 Thessalonians 5:5). Against the day of darkness that overtakes the sleeping, Paul sets the assembly on the day-side of the great division — and that division is Isaiah's. *Arise, shine; for thy light is come, and the glory of Yahuah (LORD) is risen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:1); and the contrast: *For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but Yahuah (LORD) shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee* (Isaiah 60:2). While gross darkness covers the peoples, Yahuah (LORD) rises upon his own — and those upon whom his glory is seen are the children of light, the children of the day. Enoch's third Parable holds the same hope for the same people: *And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:3), for in the end *And there shall be a light that never endeth, And to a limit (lit. ‘number’) of days they shall not come, For the darkness shall first have been destroyed, [And the light established before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits] And the light of uprightness established for ever before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 58:6), because, as the same Parable says, *it has become bright as the sun upon earth, And the darkness is past.* (1 Enoch 58:5). The portion of the elect is unceasing light; the night is destroyed. So Paul reasons from the assembly's identity to its conduct: *Therefore let us not sleep, as do others; but let us watch and be sober* (1 Thessalonians 5:6), *For they that sleep sleep in the night; and they that be drunken are drunken in the night* (1 Thessalonians 5:7). Sleep and drunkenness belong to the night; watchfulness and sobriety to the day. Because the glory of Yahuah (LORD) has risen upon them, the children of the day are not overtaken by the day of darkness.
13706.note: 58:6 was quoted from the corrupt text; re-quoted from the live 58:6 in full with 58:5 beside it; 58:3 quoted in full; rest kept

13353.title: The western gates — the sun draws away its light, the days of the year
13353.summary_md: At the western parts Enoch is shown gates *corresponding to the eastern gates, opposite to where the sun sets, according to the number of the days* of the year (2 Enoch 14:1), where the sun *goes down to the western gates, and draws away its light... under the earth* (2 Enoch 14:2). It ain't new — the lights were appointed *for days, and years* (Genesis 1:14), and the Psalmist already traced the sun's full arc: *His going forth is from the end of the heaven, and his circuit unto the ends of it* (Psalms 19:6). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had marked the same setting: *And this is the first law of the luminaries: the luminary the Sun has its rising in the eastern portals of the heaven, and its setting in the western portals of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:2), *When the sun rises in the heaven, he comes forth through that fourth portal thirty mornings in succession, and sets accurately in the fourth portal in the west of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 72:8). The sun's evening descent and the counted days of the year are the ordered courses Yahuah set, not a secret of the seer's own making.
13353.note: CHECK: the re-quote had landed on 72:11, which does not say 'western'; 72:2 and 72:8 do, quoted in full; rest kept

13357.title: The solar year and the lunar year — the ordinances of the lights
13357.summary_md: Enoch is shown the two reckonings side by side: the moon *accomplishes the three hundred and sixty-five and a quarter days of the solar year, while the lunar year has three hundred fifty-four, and there are wanting to it twelve days* (2 Enoch 16:3), with longer cycles closing the gap. It ain't new — the sun and moon keep distinct ordinances by Yahuah's appointment: *which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night* (Jeremiah 31:35). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had weighed the same difference, and it counts the moon's shortfall against the sun's 364: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12), *And the overplus of the sun and of the stars amounts to six days: in 5 years 6 days every year come to 30 days: and the moon falls behind the sun and stars to the number of 30 days.* (1 Enoch 74:11), *For the moon alone the days amount in 3 years to 1,062 days, and in 5 years she falls 50 days behind: [i.e. to the sum (of 1,770) there is to be added (1,000 and) 62 days.]* (1 Enoch 74:14). Jubilees warns of the lunar drift: *now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon* (Jubilees 6:36) — the same falling-behind Enoch counted. The lights keep their separate counts by ordinance, not by chance.
13357.note: 74:11 was quoted from the corrupt text; the live 74:11-12 and 74:14 carry the moon falling behind the 364-day sun and are quoted in full; Jeremiah and Jubilees kept

13356.title: The courses of the moon — the lesser light for seasons
13356.summary_md: Now the moon's turn: *the other course, that of the moon, twelve great gates, crowned from west to east, by which the moon goes in and out of the customary times* (2 Enoch 16:1), reckoned out month by month through its gates. It ain't new — the moon is the lesser light Moses records, *the lesser light to rule the night* (Genesis 1:16), and the Psalmist's appointed timekeeper: *He appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his going down* (Psalms 104:19). Enoch's own Astronomical Book had already traced the moon through the same portals: *And I saw another course, a law for her, (and) how according to that law she performs her monthly revolution.* (1 Enoch 74:1), *In single seventh parts she accomplishes all her light in the east, and in single seventh parts accomplishes all her darkness in the west.* (1 Enoch 74:3). The moon's circuit through its gates is not augury; it is the lesser light keeping its appointed seasons as Moses and the Psalms declare.
13356.note: 74:2 was quoted from the corrupt text; live 74:1 and 74:3 carry the moon's law and portals; Genesis 1:16 and Psalm 104:19 kept

13387.title: A later generation that reads the books and tells the next
13387.summary_md: Beyond the flood the Lord promises a faithful remnant who will recover the written witness: *Behold from their seed shall arise another generation... He who raises that generation, shall reveal to them the books of your handwriting, of your fathers... to the faithful men and workers of my pleasure* (2 Enoch 35:1-2), *And they shall tell another generation, and those others having read shall be glorified thereafter* (2 Enoch 35:3). It ain't new — this is the very charge of the law, that the witness be written and handed on: *That the generation to come might know them, even the children which should be born; who should arise and declare them to their children* (Psalms 78:6), *We will not hide them from their children, shewing to the generation to come the praises of Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalms 78:4). Enoch himself was given this commission in his own book, with a year to carry it out: *And those seven holy ones brought me and placed me on the earth before the door of my house, and said to me: ‘Declare everything to thy son Methuselah, and show to all thy children that no flesh is righteous in the sight of Yahuah (Lord), for He is their Creator.* (1 Enoch 81:5), *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). The handing-down of the books is the handing-down Moses and the prophets command.
13387.note: 81:3 was invented; the commission to teach and record for his children is live 81:5-6, quoted in full; Psalm 78 kept

13388.title: No other Elohim but me — teach and keep the commandments
13388.summary_md: Enoch is sent back for thirty days with a single charge for his house: *tell your sons and all your household... how there is no other Elohim (God) but me. And that they may always keep my commandments, and begin to read and take in the books of your handwriting* (2 Enoch 36:1-2). It ain't new — this is the Shema and its commission word for word: *Hear, O Yashar'el (Israel): Yahuah Eloheinu (The LORD our God) is one Yahuah (LORD)* (Deuteronomy 6:4), and *these words, which I command thee this day, shall be in thine heart: And thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thine house* (Deuteronomy 6:6-7). The charge to teach the sons is the one the holy ones laid on Enoch at his own door: *One year we will leave thee with thy son, till thou givest thy (last) commands, that thou mayst teach thy children and record (it) for them, and testify to all thy children; and in the second year they shall take thee from their midst.* (1 Enoch 81:6). 2 Enoch teaches no new God and no new law — only the One and His commandments, handed to the sons.
13388.note: 81:3 was invented; live 81:6 carries the charge to teach and record for his children; Deuteronomy 6 kept

13395.title: The prisoners in pain and all that are judged — written down
13395.summary_md: Enoch's books reach past the lights to the place of sentence: *I saw how the prisoners are in pain, expecting the limitless judgment. And I wrote down all those being judged by the judge, and all their judgment and sentences and all their works* (2 Enoch 40:10-11). It ain't new — this is the bound waiting for judgment Peter and Jude name: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). And the writing-down of every work for the judgment is the books of remembrance the prophets keep — what Enoch was charged to record in his own book: *And he said unto me: ‘Observe, Enoch, these heavenly tablets, And read what is written thereon, And mark every individual fact.’* (1 Enoch 81:1), *And I observed the heavenly tablets, and read everything which was written (thereon) and understood everything, and read the book of all the deeds of mankind, and of all the children of flesh that shall be upon the earth to the remotest generations.* (1 Enoch 81:2). Enoch's ledger of works and sentences is the very ledger the judgment opens.
13395.note: CHECK: 81:2 (the book of all the deeds of mankind) added beside 81:1 so the prose's 'every work' has its verse

14877.title: The angels that sinned in chains of darkness, Noah, and Sodom — the Watchers (Genesis 6, 1 Enoch, Jubilees, Jude)
14877.summary_md: To prove the certain judgment of the false teachers, Kepha (Peter) lays down three judgments the library records — and the first of them is the one the whole library keeps coming back to: *For if Elohim (God) spared not the angels that sinned, but cast them down to hell, and delivered them into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment; And spared not the old world, but saved Noah the eighth person, a preacher of righteousness, bringing in the flood upon the world of the ungodly; And turning the cities of Sodom and Gomorrha into ashes condemned them with an overthrow, making them an ensample... And delivered just Lot* (2 Peter 2:4-7). The *angels that sinned* are the Watchers — the *sons of Elohim (God)* who *came in unto the daughters of men, and they bare children to them... men of renown* (Genesis 6:4). Kepha is not coining a myth; he is reading Torah's own account of the fall that brought the Flood, and the library tells exactly how those angels were bound. Yahuah (God) commanded, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness* (1 Enoch 10:4), and of Semjâzâ, *bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement* (1 Enoch 10:12) — the very *chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment.* Enoch was shown the place itself: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees agrees to the word: Elohim (God) *bade us to bind them in the depths of the earth, and behold they are bound* (Jubilees 5:6), *bound in the depths of the earth for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:10). This is the same Watchers record Kepha (Peter) leaned on in his first letter (1 Peter 3:19-20) and Jude leans on in his: *the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 6). Then the Flood: *Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23), *Noah was a just man and perfect in his generations* (Genesis 6:9) — *Noah the eighth person,* the few *saved by water* (1 Peter 3:20), the days of Noah the Master made the type of his coming (Matthew 24:37). Then Sodom: *Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire... and he overthrew those cities* (Genesis 19:24-25), *set forth for an example, suffering the vengeance of eternal fire* (Jude 7); and just Lot delivered when *they brought him forth, and set him without the city* (Genesis 19:16). The Hebrew library catalogues every one of these: *the earth being drowned with the flood, wisdom again preserved it... in a piece of wood* (Wisdom 10:4), *she delivered the righteous man, who fled from the fire which fell down upon the five cities* (Wisdom 10:6), and in the same order Kepha keeps — *the old giants, who fell away* (Sirach 16:7), the place of Lot not spared (Sirach 16:8), Noah *left as a remnant to the earth, when the flood came* (Sirach 44:17). The lesson is one: *Yahuah (Lord) knoweth how to deliver the godly out of temptations, and to reserve the unjust unto the day of judgment to be punished* (2 Peter 2:9). The angels that sinned, the old world, the cities of the plain — the judgment-history the whole library records, and the false teachers stand in its line.
14877.note: 21:11 is gone (now 21:10, re-quoted); two internal references ('the apparatus') reworded for the reader; rest kept

1017.title: A cloud received him — the Son of Adam taken up and returning on the clouds
1017.summary_md: *A cloud received him out of their sight* (Acts 1:9), and two men in white promise *this same Yahusha (Jesus) … shall so come in like manner as ye have seen him go* (Acts 1:11). The cloud is the Formed-one's own chariot. Daniel saw the same figure on the same clouds — *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven* (Daniel 7:13) — the kaph honoring the incarnation: he resembled mortal-man because he took on flesh, while remaining the cloud-rider brought before the Ancient of days to receive the everlasting kingdom. The Revelation names the manner of the return: *behold, he cometh with clouds; and every eye shall see him* (Revelation 1:7). And Zechariah names the place: they watched him go from the mount of Olives (Acts 1:12), and *his feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives* (Zechariah 14:4) — he ascended from Olivet and to Olivet he returns. The Hebrew library already named the coming the angels promise: *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9) — the same coming Jude quoted. The One taken up in a cloud returns on the clouds, and the holy ones who come with him are the seed of promise, gathered to him.
1017.note: Enoch 1:9 re-quoted in full from the live verse; closing sentence mended to the live wording (holy ones).

423.title: All power given — the Son of Adam seated on the throne of glory in 1 Enoch's Parables
423.summary_md: When the risen King says *And Yahusha (Jesus) came and spake unto them, saying, All power is given unto me in heaven and in earth.* (Matthew 28:18), he is not announcing something new. He is stepping into a seat the prophets had already described. Daniel saw it given: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14), and David heard the Father speak it: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* (Psalms 110:1). The Parables of Enoch had set the same figure on the same throne long before: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8), and again, *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). The power is over earth as much as heaven, because the kings of the earth answer to it: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). And the first thing that authority does is open the graves and sort who comes out of them: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes. And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:1-2). The empty tomb at the start of Matthew 28 and the *all power* at the end of it belong to the same morning. The Son of Adam who came out of the grave is the one who will call the rest of the seed out of theirs.
423.note: Degraded prose rewritten from scratch; 51:1-2, 61:8, 62:2 and 62:9 quoted in full from the live text (62:6 dropped — the live verse is a different thought); Daniel 7:14 and Psalm 110:1 added from the index.

47.title: The Animal Apocalypse — the dispersed sheep gathered home
47.summary_md: *And he saith unto them, Follow me, and I will make you fishers of men.* (Matthew 4:19). The men he calls are being sent after sheep, and the Animal Apocalypse had already told the story of those sheep from the scattering to the gathering. First the blindness and the losing of them: *And as touching all this the eyes of those sheep were blinded so that they saw not, and (the eyes of) their shepherds likewise; and they delivered them in large numbers to their shepherds for destruction, and they trampled the sheep with their feet and devoured them. And Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep remained unmoved till all the sheep were dispersed over the field and mingled with them (i.e. the beasts), and they (i.e. the shepherds) did not save them out of the hand of the beasts.* (1 Enoch 89:74-75). Then, late in the age, a generation among them begins to see: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). And at the close, the ones who had been lost come home: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). That is the gathering Ezekiel promised, *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21), and it is the work the Shepherd names as his own: *And other sheep I have, which are not of this fold: them also I must bring, and they shall hear my voice; and there shall be one fold, and one shepherd.* (John 10:16). The disciples called by the lake are the first hands put to that gathering. The sheep who were mingled with the beasts open their eyes when the Shepherd's voice reaches them, and the fishers of men are sent to carry it.
47.note: Was citation-only with two unmarked quotes; 89:74-75, 90:6 and 90:33 now quoted in full from the live text, hyphen-chain prose replaced; Matthew 4:19 kept, John 10:16 and Ezekiel 37:21 added from the index.

11792.title: Borne up on the wings — heaven, earth, abyss, the whole world shown
11792.summary_md: The angel takes the turtledove and pigeon for himself: *I will ascend upon the wings of the bird, in order to shew thee in heaven, and on the earth, and in the sea, and in the abyss, and in the under-world, and in the Garden of Eden, and in its rivers and in the fulness of the whole world and its circle — thou shalt gaze in them all* (Apocalypse of Abraham 12:9). Enoch had been carried the same way before him, not by his own strength but by the winds that were sent for him: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.* (1 Enoch 14:8). And what he was shown was the whole of it, the ends of everything: *And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen.* (1 Enoch 19:3). The opened heaven is the same fire Ezekiel saw come out of the north — *a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it, and out of the midst thereof as the colour of amber* (Ezekiel 1:4) — and what Abraham will gaze upon is the whole creation, from the beginning: *In the beginning Elohim (God) created the heaven and the earth* (Genesis 1:1). The same hand that lifted Enoch lifts Abraham, and shows him the same world.
11792.note: The old Enoch quote (whirlwind and chariot of fire) is 2 Kings 2:11 wording, not Enoch; replaced with the live 14:8 ascent and 19:3; Apocalypse of Abraham 12:9 and Ezekiel/Genesis kept as they stood.

11788.title: Forty days, no bread, no water — the fast of the mountain
11788.summary_md: Abraham journeys to the holy mount as Moses fasted before the LORD: *And we went, the two of us together, forty days and nights, and I ate no bread, and drank no water, because my food was to see the angel who was with me, and his speech — that was my drink* (Apocalypse of Abraham 12:1). This is the very measure of the mountain-fast: *And he was there with Yahuah (LORD) forty days and forty nights; he did neither eat bread, nor drink water* (Exodus 34:28), and again *then I abode in the mount forty days and forty nights, I neither did eat bread nor drink water* (Deuteronomy 9:9). What sustained Abraham was what he was shown, and Enoch says the same of his own seeing, that it was given to him alone and to no other man: *And I, Enoch, alone saw the vision, the ends of all things: and no man shall see as I have seen.* (1 Enoch 19:3). The friend of Elohim is fed not by bread but by the word of the messenger, and the sight he is given on the mountain is his meat.
11788.note: Invented 14:2 quote replaced with the live 19:3 (the thought it was reaching for); canon quotes kept as they stood.

11804.title: Borne up with many winds to the flaming fire — the chariot ascent
11804.summary_md: *And he bore me to the borders of the flaming fire, and we ascended as with many winds to the heaven which was fixed upon the surface* (Apocalypse of Abraham 15:4). The road Abraham is carried on is the road Enoch was carried on first, winds doing the lifting and fire waiting at the top of the climb: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven. And I went in till I drew nigh to a wall which is built of crystals and surrounded by tongues of fire: and it began to affright me.* (1 Enoch 14:8-9). Ezekiel's throne-vision comes wrapped in the same wind and the same fire: *And I looked, and, behold, a whirlwind came out of the north, a great cloud, and a fire infolding itself, and a brightness was about it... out of the midst of the fire* (Ezekiel 1:4). Three men, one ascent, and the same fiery threshold at the border of the heavens.
11804.note: Invented 14:3 quote replaced with the live 14:8-9 (winds bearing Enoch up to the wall of fire); Ezekiel kept.

11817.title: The chariot of fiery wheels full of eyes
11817.summary_md: Behind the living creatures Abraham sees *a chariot with fiery wheels, each wheel full of eyes round about; and over the wheels was a throne... covered with fire* (Apocalypse of Abraham 18:9). Ezekiel's merkabah is this very wheelwork — *their rings were full of eyes round about them four* (Ezekiel 1:18), the wheel within the wheel — *and their whole body, and their backs, and their hands, and their wings, and the wheels, were full of eyes round about, even the wheels that they four had* (Ezekiel 10:12). Daniel saw the Ancient of days on the same flaming wheels — *his throne was like the fiery flame, and his wheels as burning fire* (Daniel 7:9). And Enoch, brought into the second house, saw the throne before any of them: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon.* (1 Enoch 14:18-19). The wheels, the cherubim, the fire pouring out from under the seat: every seer who is taken up is shown the same chariot, because there is only one throne.
11817.note: Invented 14:3 chariot quote replaced with the live 14:18-19 (the throne with wheels and the fire beneath it); Ezekiel and Daniel kept.

48.title: The Beatitudes — the blessing pronounced over the righteous and elect
48.summary_md: *Blessed are the poor in spirit: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:3). *Blessed are they that mourn: for they shall be comforted.* (Matthew 5:4). *Blessed are they which are persecuted for righteousness’ sake: for theirs is the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 5:10). The pulpit has long read these as a ladder, conditions a person meets in order to get in. Enoch had already pronounced the same blessing, and he pronounced it over a people, not over a performance: *But with the righteous He will make peace. And will protect the elect, And mercy shall be upon them. And they shall all belong to Elohim (God), And they shall be prospered, And they shall all be blessed. And He will help them all, And light shall appear unto them, And He will make peace with them.* (1 Enoch 1:8). The comfort promised to the mourners is this light and this peace, and the inheritance is the same one the meek are told they will receive: *And for you the godless there shall be a curse. But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, And they shall inherit the earth.* (1 Enoch 5:7). Then the form itself, blessed-are-ye, spoken to the persecuted: *Blessed are ye, ye righteous and elect, For glorious shall be your lot. And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:2-3). The Wisdom of Solomon says it the same way, that *the souls of the righteous are in the hand of Yahuah (God), and there shall no torment touch them* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:1), and that *grace and mercy is to his saints, and he has care for his elect* (the Wisdom of Solomon 3:9). Read beside these, the Beatitudes describe the citizens the King has come to gather. The blessing is on them because of who they are to him, and the poverty of spirit, the mourning, the hunger for righteousness are what that people looks like in the lands of their scattering before he brings them home.
48.note: Citation-only gloss in hyphen-chain prose; rewritten with 1:8, 5:7 and 58:2-3 quoted in full from the live text, Matthew 5:3, 5:4, 5:10 and Wisdom 3:1, 3:9 added from the index.

188.title: The binding of the Watchers — Azazel bound hand and foot, and the strong man bound
188.summary_md: *But if I cast out devils by the Spirit of Elohim (God), then the kingdom of Elohim (God) is come unto you. Or else how can one enter into a strong man’s house, and spoil his goods, except he first bind the strong man? and then he will spoil his house.* (Matthew 12:28-29). The picture of a strong one bound so that his house can be plundered was not drawn fresh for the Pharisees. It is how the Watchers were dealt with, and the library had told it in detail: *And again Yahuah (Lord) said to Raphael: ‘Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness: and make an opening in the desert, which is in Dûdâêl, and cast him therein. And place upon him rough and jagged rocks, and cover him with darkness, and let him abide there for ever, and cover his face that he may not see light. And on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire.* (1 Enoch 10:4-6). The chains were not for him alone: *And he said unto me: ‘These are being prepared for the hosts of Azâzêl, so that they may take them and cast them into the abyss of complete condemnation, and they shall cover their jaws with rough stones as Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits commanded.* (1 Enoch 54:5). Jubilees tells why there are still spirits to cast out at all: *And we did according to all His words: all the malignant evil ones we bound in the place of condemnation, and a tenth part of them we left that they might be subject before Satan on the earth.* (Jubilees 10:11). The devils Yahusha (Jesus) drives out are that tenth, the loose remainder of a host already mostly in chains, and the one they serve is the strong man whose binding is still ahead: *And he laid hold on the dragon, that old serpent, which is the Devil, and Satan, and bound him a thousand years, And cast him into the bottomless pit, and shut him up, and set a seal upon him, that he should deceive the nations no more, till the thousand years should be fulfilled: and after that he must be loosed a little season.* (Revelation 20:2-3). When the King empties a man of a devil by the Spirit, the house is being spoiled by the one who has the authority to bind its master. That is why he could say the kingdom had come upon them.
188.note: Degraded prose rewritten; 10:4-6, 54:5 and Jubilees 10:11 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 12:28-29 and Revelation 20:2-3 from the index. The old 'inaugurated binding now' framing dropped; the binding of the adversary is set at the end where Revelation puts it.

198.title: Bound and cast into the furnace of fire — the Watchers' judgement and the tares
198.summary_md: *The Son of Adam shall send forth his angels, and they shall gather out of his kingdom all things that offend, and them which do iniquity; And shall cast them into a furnace of fire: there shall be wailing and gnashing of teeth.* (Matthew 13:41-42). The tares are gathered first and bound in bundles to burn, and the reapers are angels. Enoch had watched the same angels do the same work on the Watchers: *And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated. In those days they shall be led off to the abyss of fire: and to the torment and the prison in which they shall be confined for ever.* (1 Enoch 10:12-13). The Parables name the hands that carry them there and the day it happens: *And Michael, and Gabriel, and Raphael, and Phanuel shall take hold of them on that great day, and cast them on that day into the burning furnace, that Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits may take vengeance on them for their unrighteousness in becoming subject to Satan and leading astray those who dwell on the earth.’* (1 Enoch 54:6). And the Animal Apocalypse shows the order of it at the end, the fallen stars first and then the shepherds who destroyed the sheep: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire. And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:24-25). The burning furnace of the parable is this abyss. The angels who bound Azazel in the desert are the angels sent at the harvest, and what they gather out of the kingdom goes where the Watchers went. The seed sown by the enemy is dealt with the same way the enemy's own hosts were dealt with, and before the wheat is brought in.
198.note: Degraded prose rewritten; 10:12-13, 54:6 and 90:24-25 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 13:41-42 from the index; internal thread references removed.

195.title: The fowls that devour the seed — Mastema's birds and the spirits of the Watchers
195.summary_md: In the parable the seed by the wayside is lost when *fowls came and devoured them up* (Matthew 13:4), and the King does not leave the birds as scenery. He tells us who they are: *When any one heareth the word of the kingdom, and understandeth it not, then cometh the wicked one, and catcheth away that which was sown in his heart. This is he which received seed by the way side.* (Matthew 13:19). Jubilees had already put birds in the adversary's hand, sent against the seed in the days of Abraham's father: *Prince Mastema sent ravens and birds to devour the seed which was sown in the land, in order to destroy the land, so as to rob the children of men of their labours. Before they could plough in the seed, the ravens picked it from the surface of the ground* (Jubilees 11:11). And Enoch names the spirits that do the robbing, where they came from and what they are working toward: *And Uriel said to me: ‘Here shall stand the angels who have connected themselves with women, and their spirits assuming many different forms are defiling mankind and shall lead them astray into sacrificing to demons as gods, (here shall they stand,) till the day of the great judgement in which they shall be judged till they are made an end of.* (1 Enoch 19:1). Abraham drove the fowls off his sacrifice (Genesis 15:11); Mastema sent them against the furrows; the wicked one sends them against the heart where the word of the kingdom has just been sown. It is one enemy with one aim, to take the seed before it can root, and the same birds come back later in the chapter to lodge in the branches of the mustard tree, because what grows in the field grows with the enemy still working in it until the harvest.
195.note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 19:1 quoted in full from the live text; Jubilees 11:11 and the Matthew quotes kept as they stood; Matthew 13:19 completed from the index.

185.title: The righteous stands in boldness before those who condemned him — Wisdom 5 and 1 Enoch 95
185.summary_md: *Then the Pharisees went out, and held a council against him, how they might destroy him.* (Matthew 12:14). A council of the religious sits to condemn a righteous man, and the verdict it reaches stands for a season. The Wisdom of Solomon had already written the day that verdict is turned over: *then shall the righteous man stand in great boldness before the face of such as have afflicted him* (the Wisdom of Solomon 5:1), and the men who condemned him are made to say out loud what they got wrong: *We fools accounted his life madness, and his end to be without honour: How is he numbered among the children of Yahuah (God), and his lot is among the saints!* (the Wisdom of Solomon 5:4-5). Enoch pronounces the woe on that council and on every one like it, and says the sentence will fall on them in the same coin: *Woe to you, lying witnesses, And to those who weigh out injustice, For suddenly shall ye perish. Woe to you, sinners, for ye persecute the righteous; For ye shall be delivered up and persecuted because of injustice, And heavy shall its yoke be upon you.* (1 Enoch 95:6-7). The road from questioning his disciples over dinner, to calling him a glutton and a friend of sinners, to plotting his death, is the road the lying witnesses walk, and it ends at the cross. But the resurrection is the first turning of the verdict, and the day of judgement is the last. The same thing happens to the seed who keep his commandments today, condemned by councils that hold the pulpit, and the same reversal is waiting for them.
185.note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 95:6-7 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom 5 quotes kept, Matthew 12:14 and Wisdom 5:4-5 completed from the index.

115.title: A man's foes shall be they of his own household — the family torn in the day of destruction
115.summary_md: *Think not that I am come to send peace on earth: I came not to send peace, but a sword. For I am come to set a man at variance against his father, and the daughter against her mother, and the daughter in law against her mother in law. And a man’s foes shall be they of his own household.* (Matthew 10:34-36). He is quoting Micah, and Micah is describing a day. Enoch describes the same day, and the house is where it tears first: *And in those days the destitute shall go forth and carry off their children, And they shall abandon them, so that their children shall perish through them: Yea, they shall abandon their children (that are still) sucklings, and not return to them, And shall have no pity on their beloved ones.* (1 Enoch 99:5). Then the blood: *And in those days in one place the fathers together with their sons shall be smitten And brothers one with another shall fall in death Till the streams flow with their blood. For a man shall not withhold his hand from slaying his sons and his sons’ sons, And the sinner shall not withhold his hand from his honoured brother: From dawn till sunset they shall slay one another.* (1 Enoch 100:1-2). The enmity set in the garden between the two seeds does not stop at the front door. Wheat and tares can be born under one roof, and when the Shepherd's voice is heard by one and not the other, the line runs straight through the family. What the King warns his disciples of in this age is the first showing of the division Enoch saw finished in the day of destruction, when the house that would not hear falls on itself.
115.note: Degraded prose rewritten; 1 Enoch 99:5 and 100:1-2 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 10:34-36 from the index.

41.title: This is the Son of Adam — the voice that names him at the investiture
41.summary_md: *And lo a voice from heaven, saying, This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased.* (Matthew 3:17). A voice from above the water names the one standing in it. Enoch heard the same form of words spoken over the same figure when he was carried up into the heavens: *And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14). This is the Son of Adam, this is my beloved Son. The naming at the Jordan is public, and the Parables explain why it had to come as a disclosure and not as common knowledge: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). The one hidden with the Father from the beginning is revealed to the elect, and at the river the revealing is spoken out loud. The Ascension of Isaiah carries the other end of the arc, the Beloved who came down in the form of a man going back up: *And I saw how He ascended into the seventh heaven, and all the righteous and all the angels praised Him. And then I saw Him sit down on the right hand of that Great Glory whose glory I told you that I could not behold.* (Ascension of Isaiah 11:32). Descent, naming, ascent. The voice at the Jordan is one point on a line the library had already drawn end to end.
41.note: The '39:5 voice of the Holy One' quote is not in the live text and was dropped; the 'This is the Son of Adam' words live at 71:14, not 62:7 — re-cited and quoted in full with 62:7; Matthew 3:17 and Ascension 11:32 from the index.

69.title: Gather all the tribes of Jacob — Sirach 36 and the return to the house in 1 Enoch 90
69.summary_md: *And I say unto you, That many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven.* (Matthew 8:11). East and west is the language of the gathering, and the prophets used it of a seed, not of strangers: *Fear not: for I am with thee: I will bring thy seed from the east, and gather thee from the west; I will say to the north, Give up; and to the south, Keep not back: bring my sons from far, and my daughters from the ends of the earth;* (Isaiah 43:5-6). Sirach prays for exactly this, and names who is being gathered: *gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Ecclesiasticus 36:11), and the people whose name the prayer rests on, *Yahuah (God), have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn* (Ecclesiasticus 36:12). Enoch saw the end of that prayer in the Animal Apocalypse, the scattered sheep brought back into the house: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The many from east and west who sit at the table with the patriarchs are the tribes of Jacob come home, the sons and daughters brought from far. The children of the kingdom cast out in the next verse are not Judah set aside for a church; they are the unfruitful of the house, sifted under the rod as Ezekiel 20 says the whole gathered people will be. The seat at the table is for the seed that hears, wherever the scattering carried it.
69.note: Degraded prose rewritten; the invented 90:18 quote replaced by 90:33 quoted in full; Sirach quotes kept as they stood; Isaiah 43:5-6 added from the index.

39.title: The heavens opened at the investiture — the open door of the throne-room
39.summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:* (Matthew 3:16). Heaven opens over a man at the moment he is set apart for service. Levi was shown it at his own calling to the priesthood: *behold the heavens were opened, and an angel of Elohim (God) said to me, Levi, enter* (Testament of Levi 2:6). Enoch was shown what the open heaven opens onto. First the door itself: *And I beheld a vision, And lo! there was a second house, greater than the former, and the entire portal stood open before me, and it was built of flames of fire.* (1 Enoch 14:15). Then, in the Parables, the ascent into that house where the Son of Adam is named: *And it came to pass after this that my spirit was translated And it ascended into the heavens: And I saw the holy sons of Elohim (God). They were stepping on flames of fire: Their garments were white [and their raiment], And their faces shone like snow.* (1 Enoch 71:1). The portal that stood open before Enoch is the heaven that opened over the Jordan. What came down through it onto the Son was the Spirit, and what was spoken through it was the Father's voice. The priesthood Levi entered through an open heaven and the office the Son is sealed into at the water are reached through the same door.
39.note: Citation-only; 14:15 and 71:1 now quoted in full from the live text, Testament of Levi quote kept, Matthew 3:16 from the index.

16569.title: When he saw his glory — the enthroned One Isaiah saw is the Formed Son
16569.summary_md: Isaiah saw a Person on the throne: *In the year that king Uzziah died I saw also Yahuah (Lord) sitting upon a throne, high and lifted up, and his train filled the temple* (Isaiah 6:1); *for mine eyes have seen the King, Yahuah Tseva'ot (LORD of hosts)* (6:5). John reads this very chapter and names whose glory it was. He first quotes the commission of 6:10 — *He hath blinded their eyes, and hardened their heart; that they should not see with their eyes, nor understand with their heart, and be converted, and I should heal them* (John 12:40) — and then declares: *These things said Esaias, when he saw his glory, and spake of him* (John 12:41). The glory that filled the temple was HIS glory. This is the Formed and the Formless: the visible enthroned Glory whom Isaiah saw is the Formed Son, the expressed Word drawn from the Formless Father — the One who appeared, who is Yahuah, and who HAS a Father. Not co-equal trinitarian persons; not a modalist collapse — the One enthroned, of whom Isaiah *spake*, is Yahusha (Jesus). Enoch was brought before the same throne and could say no more of the One on it than Isaiah could: *And I looked and saw therein a lofty throne: its appearance was as crystal, and the wheels thereof as the shining sun, and there was the vision of cherubim. And from underneath the throne came streams of flaming fire so that I could not look thereon. And the Great Glory sat thereon, and His raiment shone more brightly than the sun and was whiter than any snow.* (1 Enoch 14:18-20) — the throne high and lifted up, the fire, the Glory none could look upon.
16569.note: The mechanical re-quote had landed on 18:8-9 (a mountain 'like the throne'); the throne-vision the summary is about is 14:18-20, quoted in full instead.

17454.title: Behold, I create new heavens and a new earth — the keystone of the new creation
17454.summary_md: Here is the keystone toward which the whole promise runs: *For, behold, I create new heavens and a new earth: and the former shall not be remembered, nor come into mind* (Isaiah 65:17). Peter names this very promise as the hope of the people: *Nevertheless we, according to his promise, look for new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness* (2 Peter 3:13). John sees it come: *And I saw a new heaven and a new earth: for the first heaven and the first earth were passed away; and there was no more sea* (Revelation 21:1) — and *the former things are passed away* (Revelation 21:4), the very *former* that *shall not be remembered, nor come into mind*. Isaiah himself seals its permanence in the next chapter: *For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), so shall your seed and your name remain* (Isaiah 66:22) — the new creation endures, and the seed of promise and the name endure with it. The Parables of Enoch sing the same renewal, and they put the Elect One in the middle of it: *Then will I cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them. And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light: And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon.* (1 Enoch 45:4-5). The Father is the formless Source; the Elect One dwelling among his people is the Formed Son. The creating of Isaiah, the looking-for of Peter, the seeing of John, the transforming of the Parables — one new creation, the end every promise was pointed at.
17454.note: Invented 45:4 quote replaced with the live 45:4-5 in full; the rest stands.

17463.title: By fire and by his sword will Yahuah plead with all flesh — the fiery judgment and the rebels' end
17463.summary_md: Against the rejoicing of the restored comes the fire upon the rebels: *For, behold, Yahuah (LORD) will come with fire, and with his chariots like a whirlwind, to render his anger with fury, and his rebuke with flames of fire. For by fire and by his sword will Yahuah (LORD) plead with all flesh: and the slain of Yahuah (LORD) shall be many* (Isaiah 66:15-16). The Formed Son is the executor of this fire: *when the Lord Yahusha (Lord Jesus) shall be revealed from heaven with his mighty angels* (2 Thessalonians 1:7), *In flaming fire taking vengeance on them that know not Elohim (God)* (1:8); *out of his mouth goeth a sharp sword, that with it he should smite the nations... and he treadeth the winepress of the fierceness and wrath of El Shaddai (Almighty God)* (Revelation 19:15). The day burns as an oven: *all that do wickedly, shall be stubble; and the day that cometh shall burn them up* (Malachi 4:1); the heavens are *reserved unto fire against the day of judgment* (2 Peter 3:7). Enoch opens his whole book on this advent, the verse Jude quotes by name: *And behold! He cometh with ten thousands of His holy ones To execute judgement upon all, And to destroy all the ungodly: And to convict all flesh Of all the works of their ungodliness which they have ungodly committed, And of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against Him.* (1 Enoch 1:9). And the Parables say where the sinners stand when the earth is made new, which is nowhere on it: *And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon. For I have provided and satisfied with peace My righteous ones And have caused them to dwell before Me: But for the sinners there is judgement impending with Me, So that I shall destroy them from the face of the earth.* (1 Enoch 45:5-6). The book's very last verse fixes the rebels' final state, quoted verbatim by Yahusha of Gehenna: *they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched* (66:24); *Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched* (Mark 9:48); *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake... some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2). The swine's-flesh rebels of v.17 are the *all flesh* this fire pleads against — the dietary rebellion judged, not licensed.
17463.note: 1:9 re-quoted in full from the live verse (holy ones); the invented 45:5 'straw in the fire' quote replaced with the live 45:5-6.

17465.title: From one sabbath to another shall all flesh come to worship — the appointed times into eternity
17465.summary_md: The book closes on the plainest answer to lawlessness in the whole Tanakh: *For as the new heavens and the new earth, which I will make, shall remain before me, saith Yahuah (LORD), so shall your seed and your name remain. And it shall come to pass, that from one new moon to another, and from one sabbath to another, shall all flesh come to worship before me, saith Yahuah (LORD)* (Isaiah 66:22-23). The new moons AND the sabbaths are KEPT BY ALL FLESH in the new creation — the appointed times are not abolished; they continue into eternity, as permanent as the new heavens themselves, and the seed and name of the people remain with them. The new creation is the one just promised: *behold, I create new heavens and a new earth* (Isaiah 65:17); *I saw a new heaven and a new earth* (Revelation 21:1); *new heavens and a new earth, wherein dwelleth righteousness* (2 Peter 3:13); and Enoch's Parables, where the Elect One dwells among the elect on the earth made new: *Then will I cause Mine Elect One to dwell among them. And I will transform the heaven and make it an eternal blessing and light: And I will transform the earth and make it a blessing: And I will cause Mine elect ones to dwell upon it: But the sinners and evil-doers shall not set foot thereon.* (1 Enoch 45:4-5). Zechariah names the same kept feast: *every one that is left of all the nations... shall... go up from year to year to worship the King... and to keep the feast of tabernacles* (Zechariah 14:16). And Colossians, so often misread as abolition, is the shadow whose BODY remains: *Let no man therefore judge you... of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: Which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Messiah (Christ)* (Colossians 2:16-17) — the shadow stands because the body stands; Paul forbids the outsider judging those who keep them, while Isaiah shows all flesh keeping them on into the new heavens. The filter holds: *hereby we do know that we know him, if we keep his commandments* (1 John 2:3). Any reading that abolishes the kept sabbath fails the test Isaiah's own ending sets, for the very last vision of the book is all flesh worshipping from sabbath to sabbath, for ever.
17465.note: Invented 45:4 fragment replaced with the live 45:4-5 in full; the rest stands.

6180.title: Enoch prophesied — the seventh from Adam and the day of judgment
6180.summary_md: Before he is taken, Jasher's Enoch gives a last charge: *And now therefore I will teach you wisdom and knowledge and will give you instruction before I leave you, how to act upon earth by which you may live* (Jasher 3:25), and *he placed before them statutes and judgments to do upon earth, and he made peace amongst them, and he taught them everlasting life* (Jasher 3:26). The Renewed Covenant remembers this Enoch as a prophet of the judgment to come: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14), *To execute judgment upon all, and to convince all that are ungodly among them of all their ungodly deeds* (Jude 1:15). The book of Enoch itself is the testimony Jude is quoting, the witness of the man who *placed the testimony on earth for all the children of men and for their generations* (Jubilees 4:19) and *should recount all the deeds of the generations until the day of condemnation.* (Jubilees 4:24). The statutes he taught and the judgment he warned of come from the same mouth, and they belong together. It ain't new.
