6180.note: No Enoch quote to grade; 'the live 1 Enoch' and 'one apparatus' phrasing replaced with plain words.

6179.title: Enoch was not, for Elohim took him — translated that he should not see death
6179.summary_md: Jasher's whole chapter drives to the moment Genesis states in five words. An angel calls again — *behold an angel of Yahuah (the Lord) then called to Enoch from heaven, and wished to bring him up to heaven to make him reign there over the sons of Elohim* (Jasher 3:23) — and *it was upon the seventh day that Enoch ascended into heaven in a whirlwind, with horses and chariots of fire.* (Jasher 3:36). That is Genesis told long: *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him.* (Genesis 5:24). The Renewed Covenant reads it as faith: *By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him: for before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased Elohim (God).* (Hebrews 11:5). Enoch tells the whirlwind in his own words: *And in those days a whirlwind carried me off from the earth, And set me down at the end of the heavens.* (1 Enoch 39:3), and how the winds bore him up: *And the vision was shown to me thus: Behold, in the vision clouds invited me and a mist summoned me, and the course of the stars and the lightnings sped and hastened me, and the winds in the vision caused me to fly and lifted me upward, and bore me into heaven.* (1 Enoch 14:8). Jubilees seals the taking: *And he was taken from amongst the children of men, and we conducted him into the Garden of Eden in majesty and honour* (Jubilees 4:23). The translation of Enoch is one event held by five witnesses, and not one of them has him die.
6179.note: The 'chariot of fire' Enoch quote is 2 Kings 2:11 wording and is nowhere in Enoch; replaced with the live 39:3 and 14:8, which do describe his being carried off.

6195.title: Yahuah shut him in — the men shut out, all flesh died
6195.summary_md: Jasher records the shutting of the door and the perishing of all flesh: *And Noah and his household, and all the living creatures that were with him, came into the ark on account of the waters of the flood, and Yahuah (the Lord) shut him in* (Jasher 6:15), and *all flesh that was upon the earth or in the waters died, whether men, animals, beasts, creeping things or birds of the air, and there only remained Noah and those that were with him in the ark* (Jasher 6:26). Genesis is the same shutting and the same death: *and Yahuah (LORD) shut him in* (Genesis 7:16), and *And every living substance was destroyed which was upon the face of the ground… and Noah only remained alive, and they that were with him in the ark* (Genesis 7:23). Jasher adds the seven hundred thousand who begged at the door (Jasher 6:17) — the rebellion that said *that he does not exist* (Jasher 6:19) — but the verdict is the canon's: the door of mercy was shut after a hundred and twenty years of warning. The flood is judgment on the corrupted earth that the Watchers (Jasher 4, 1 Enoch, Jubilees 5) defiled.
6195.note: Mentions 1 Enoch only as a witness name beside Jasher 4 and Jubilees 5; nothing quoted, nothing to fix.

6205.title: Adam's garments, Enoch translated, and the birth of Abram
6205.summary_md: Verse 18 carries two threads the chosen line will need. First the garments: *the garments of skin which Elohim made for Adam and his wife... were given to Enoch, the son of Jared, and when Enoch was taken up to Elohim, he gave them to Methuselah, his son* (Jasher 7:18). Enoch's being taken up is the canon's own — *And Enoch walked with Elohim (God): and he was not; for Elohim (God) took him* (Genesis 5:24), which the witness names as translation by faith: *By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and was not found, because Elohim (God) had translated him* (Hebrews 11:5). Jasher 3, the book of Enoch, and Jubilees all tell that same taking at length. Then the elect line surfaces against Nimrod's kingdom: *Terah was seventy years old when he begat him, and Terah called the name of his son that was born to him Abram* (Jasher 7:18). It ain't new: *And Terah lived seventy years, and begat Abram, Nahor, and Haran* (Genesis 11:26). And the canon remembers Terah served other gods — *even Terah, the father of Abraham... and they served other gods* (Joshua 24:2) — out of which the called seed Abram is taken: the wheat among the tares of Nimrod's Babel.
6205.note: No Enoch quote; the 'live 1 Enoch and Jubilees apparatus' sentence replaced with plain words.

35907.title: Exalted for a little while, but brought low
35907.summary_md: Job ends the catalogue not with despair but with the verdict the retribution doctrine could not give him on its own terms: *He draweth also the mighty with his power: he riseth up, and no man is sure of life... They are exalted for a little while, but are gone and brought low; they are taken out of the way as all other, and cut off as the tops of the ears of corn* (Job 24:22,24). The strong man's height is real, and brief. Asaph was staggered by the same prosperity — *envious... when I saw the prosperity of the wicked* (Psalm 73:3) — until the sanctuary opened his eyes: *Surely thou didst set them in slippery places: thou castedst them down into destruction* (Psalm 73:18); *as a dream when one awaketh; so, O Yahuah (Lord), when thou awakest, thou shalt despise their image* (Psalm 73:20). Enoch says the same thing to the righteous first, before he turns to the mighty: *Be hopeful, ye righteous; for suddenly shall the sinners perish before you, And ye shall have lordship over them according to your desires.* (1 Enoch 96:1). Then the woes, and they read like Job's catalogue turned into a sentence: *Woe to you who devour the finest of the wheat, And drink wine in large bowls, And tread under foot the lowly with your might. Woe to you who drink water from every fountain, For suddenly shall ye be consumed and wither away, Because ye have forsaken the fountain of life.* (1 Enoch 96:5-6), and *Woe to you, ye mighty, Who with might oppress the righteous; For the day of your destruction is coming. In those days many and good days shall come to the righteous—in the day of your judgement.* (1 Enoch 96:8). Job's sickle, Asaph's waking dream, Enoch's withering. The exaltation is *a little while*; the cutting off is sure, and the day that ends the mighty is the day that begins the good days of the righteous.
35907.note: All three Enoch quotes were invented (96:10 does not exist); replaced with the live 96:1, 96:5-6 and 96:8 in full.

37171.title: Where Wast Thou When I Laid the Foundations — and the Morning Stars Sang
37171.summary_md: *Where wast thou when I laid the foundations of the earth?... Whereupon are the foundations thereof fastened? or who laid the corner stone thereof; When the morning stars sang together, and all the sons of Elohim (God) shouted for joy?* (Job 38:4-7). The man was not there; the Creator alone laid them — and He laid them with Wisdom, the Formed Son: *When he... appointed the foundations of the earth: Then I was by him, as one brought up with him: and I was daily his delight* (Proverbs 8:29-30). The foundations stand fixed forever: *Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever* (Psalm 104:5). The NT names the agent through whom they were laid: *For by him were all things created, that are in heaven, and that are in earth, visible and invisible... all things were created by him, and for him* (Colossians 1:16) — the Formed Son, who has a Father, never the Father Himself. The *sons of Elohim (God)* who *shouted for joy* are the same heavenly court that opens the book: *Now there was a day when the sons of Elohim (God) came to present themselves before Yahuah (LORD)* (Job 1:6). Job was not there, but Enoch was shown the place, foundations and corner-stone and all: *I saw the treasuries of all the winds: I saw how He had furnished with them the whole creation and the firm foundations of the earth. And I saw the corner-stone of the earth: I saw the four winds which bear [the earth and] the firmament of the heaven. And I saw how the winds stretch out the vaults of heaven, and have their station between heaven and earth: these are the pillars of the heaven.* (1 Enoch 18:1-3). The question put to Job out of the whirlwind has an answer in the library, and the answer is a man who was carried to see it.
37171.note: Invented 18:1-2 quote replaced with the live 18:1-3 in full; the rest stands.

668.title: The resurrection and the life — the earth giving back its dead in 2 Esdras and 1 Enoch
668.summary_md:
At the grave of Lazaros, Martha confesses the resurrection at the last day, and the Formed one answers with a name: *I am the resurrection, and the life.* The inherited reading treats the raising of Lazaros as a stand-alone miracle and the saying as a comfort. The Hebrew library shows what the saying stands on: the earth, Sheol, and death itself giving back the dead at the resurrection, and the Elect One arising to choose the righteous from among them.

*Martha saith unto him, I know that he shall rise again in the resurrection at the last day. Yahusha (Jesus) said unto her, I am the resurrection, and the life: he that believeth in me, though he were dead, yet shall he live: and whosoever liveth and believeth in me shall never die.* (John 11:24-26)

*And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32)

*And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes. And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:1-2)

*For in those days the Elect One shall arise, And the earth shall rejoice, And the righteous shall dwell upon it, And the elect shall walk thereon.* (1 Enoch 51:5)

Martha's hope — *the resurrection at the last day* — is the Hebrew library's own hope: the earth restoring the sleeping, the dust giving back those in silence, Sheol and death giving back what they hold. And the library binds that resurrection to a person, the Elect One who arises and chooses the righteous from among the raised. John 11:25 says the same thing in the first person. The Formed one is himself the resurrection the library awaited, the Elect One whose arising brings the dead back from the earth, from Sheol, from death's keeping. The raising of Lazaros — *Lazarus, come forth* — is the firstfruit sign of it, the head doing in one grave what the whole gathered body will follow him through at the last day.
668.note: Mechanical re-quote of 51:1-2 holds; the closing prose still spoke of the Elect One 'arising', which is 51:5 — added in full so the prose has its verse; 'architecture' wording plained.

670.title: The hour is come — the Son of Adam glorified and enthroned in the Enochic Parables
670.summary_md:
When the Greeks at the feast ask to see him, the Formed one answers not with an audience but with the hour: *the hour is come, that the Son of Adam should be glorified.* The inherited reading hears *glorified* as a soft word for the crucifixion. It carries more than that. The Son of Adam is a named figure in the Hebrew library, shown to Enoch beside the Head of Days and seated on the throne of glory, and his glorifying is the enthronement the Parables already wrote, reached by way of the lifting-up.

*And Yahusha (Jesus) answered them, saying, The hour is come, that the Son of Adam should be glorified.* (John 12:23)

*Father, glorify thy name. Then came there a voice from heaven, saying, I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.* (John 12:28)

*And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14)

*And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed. And when he shall lift up his countenance To judge their secret ways according to the word of the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And their path according to the way of the righteous judgement of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, Then shall they all with one voice speak and bless, And glorify and extol and sanctify the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 61:8-9)

The Son of Adam is not a veil over a generic human. The library names him — *this is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness* — and the righteousness of the Head of Days never forsakes him. In the Parables the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits is glorified at the moment the Elect One is set on the throne and lifts up his face to judge; John 12:28 puts the same thing in the Father's own voice from heaven: *Father, glorify thy name ... I have both glorified it, and will glorify it again.* The hour of the Son of Adam's glorifying is the hour the Father's name is glorified. And the path to the throne the Parables describe runs through the lifting-up: *I, if I be lifted up from the earth, will draw all men unto me* (John 12:32). The Son of Adam the library names beside the Head of Days is the Formed one whose hour has come, glorified through the cross and drawing the gathered home.
670.note: Mechanical re-quotes (71:14, 61:9) hold; prose mended so the naming is the angel's voice as 71:14 has it, 61:8 added in full for the enthronement, 'the framework hears / architecture' wording plained.

33996.title: The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do (Deuteronomy 18; Daniel 7; 1 Enoch 49, 61, 71)
33996.summary_md:
Here is the heart of who the Son is. *The Son can do nothing of himself, but what he seeth the Father do: for what things soever he doeth, these also doeth the Son likewise* (John 5:19). Not an independent deity acting on his own; not a creature improvising. The Formed Son does only what he sees the Father do.

Moses foretold him so: *I will raise them up a Prophet from among their brethren... and will put my words in his mouth; and he shall speak unto them all that I shall command him.* (Deuteronomy 18:18). The Prophet carries the Sender's word, never his own. And the kingdom is *given*: *one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days* (Daniel 7:13) — the kaph preserved, the Formed Son brought near — *and there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom... his dominion is an everlasting dominion* (Daniel 7:14). Given by the Father, received by the Son. So *the Father hath given to the Son to have life in himself, and hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of Adam* (John 5:26-27).

The older witnesses say the same. *Because the Elect One standeth before Yahuah (God) of Spirits... he shall judge the secret things, And none shall be able to utter a lying word before him* (1 Enoch 49:2,4): the Son stands before the Father and judges by what he is given. The throne is given too: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8). And his standing with the Father is what the angel names over him: *And he (i.e. the angel) came to me and greeted me with His voice, and said unto me: ‘This is the Son of Adam who is born unto righteousness, And righteousness abides over him, And the righteousness of the Head of Days forsakes him not.’* (1 Enoch 71:14). The Father seats the Son of Adam to judge, and the righteousness he judges by is the Head of Days' own. One will, one work: the Father shows, the Son does; the Father gives, the Son receives.
33996.note: Invented 62:6-7 quote replaced: the seating is 61:8 and the naming is 71:14, both quoted in full from the live text; 49:2,4 abridged quote kept (stands).

5294.title: Sodom overthrown, Lot delivered — judgment engraved on the tables
5294.summary_md: In the same month judgment falls: *And in this month Yahuah (God) executed his judgments on Sodom, and Gomorrah, and Zeboim, and all the region of the Jordan, and He burned them with fire and brimstone, and destroyed them until this day* (Jubilees 16:5). This is the Genesis overthrow retold — *Then Yahuah (LORD) rained upon Sodom and upon Gomorrah brimstone and fire from Yahuah (LORD) out of heaven; And he overthrew those cities, and all the plain* (Genesis 19:24-25). Jubilees keeps the deliverance of Lot for Abraham's sake exactly as Genesis does: *But Lot we saved; for Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent him out from the midst of the overthrow* (Jubilees 16:6) — word for word the Torah's *and it came to pass, when Elohim (God) destroyed the cities of the plain, that Elohim (God) remembered Abraham, and sent Lot out of the midst of the overthrow* (Genesis 19:29). But Jubilees adds something Genesis leaves unsaid, a verdict already on the heavenly tables: the uncleanness of Sodom is *commanded and engraven concerning all his seed, on the heavenly tables, to remove them and root them out* (Jubilees 16:9). The judgment of the wicked was written before it fell, and the sentence runs on through everyone who joins them, the way the Watchers' doom was fixed before their day came: *And whosoever shall be condemned and destroyed will from thenceforth be bound together with them to the end of all generations.* (1 Enoch 10:14).
5294.note: 'the framework leans on' removed; 1 Enoch 10:14 quoted in full instead of cited bare.

5201.title: The 364-day year on the heavenly tablets, and the sinners who follow the moon
5201.summary_md: The calendar climax. Jubilees commands the solar reckoning engraved on the tablets — *And command you the children of Yashar'el (Israel) that they observe the years according to this reckoning-three hundred and sixty-four days, and (these) will constitute a complete year, and they will not disturb its time from its days and from its feasts* (Jubilees 6:32) — and warns that those who watch the moon will wreck the appointed times: *For there will be those who will assuredly make observations of the moon–now (it) disturbs the seasons and comes in from year to year ten days too soon* (Jubilees 6:36), confounding the holy with the unclean, *for they will go wrong as to the months and sabbaths and feasts and jubilees* (Jubilees 6:37). Enoch's book of the luminaries gives the same count and says it will not drift: *And the sun and the stars bring in all the years exactly, so that they do not advance or delay their position by a single day unto eternity; but complete the years with perfect justice in 364 days.* (1 Enoch 74:12). And it names the same fault Jubilees names, men who leave the four added days out of the reckoning and so lose the year: *Blessed are all the righteous, blessed are all those who walk in the way of righteousness and sin not as the sinners, in the reckoning of all their days in which the sun traverses the heaven, entering into and departing from the portals for thirty days with the heads of thousands of the order of the stars, together with the four which are intercalated which divide the four portions of the year, which lead them and enter with them four days. Owing to them men shall be at fault and not reckon them in the whole reckoning of the year: yea, men shall be at fault, and not recognize them accurately. For they belong to the reckoning of the year and are truly recorded (thereon) for ever, one in the first portal and one in the third, and one in the fourth and one in the sixth, and the year is completed in three hundred and sixty-four days.* (1 Enoch 82:4-6). Daniel names the same spirit at work in the last days: *and think to change times and laws* (Daniel 7:25). The order is fixed on the heavenly tablets. To follow the moon's drift is to lose the path of the years, and with it the feasts the year was made to carry.
5201.note: The 'alter the times… eat blood' quote is nowhere in Enoch and was dropped; 74:12 and 82:4-6 quoted in full from the live text (the 364-day count and the men who go wrong in the reckoning); internal references removed.

5212.title: Shem's lot — the middle of the earth, Eden, Sinai and Zion the navel
5212.summary_md: The first lot falls to Shem, and it is the holy centre: *And there came forth on the writing as Shem’s lot the middle of the earth which he should take as an inheritance for himself and for his sons for the generations of eternity* (Jubilees 8:11), *that they should possess it for ever to his generations for evermore* (Jubilees 8:17). And the reason is unveiled: *he knew that the Garden of Eden is the holy of holies, and the dwelling of Yahuah (God), and Mount Sinai the centre of the desert, and Mount Zion–the centre of the navel of the earth: these three were created as holy places facing each other* (Jubilees 8:18). This is the land of promise itself, with Jerusalem at the centre of the world. Ezekiel says it plainly: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); This is Jerusalem: I have set it in the midst of the nations and countries that are round about her* (Ezekiel 5:5), and again of the regathered people *that dwell in the midst of the land* (Ezekiel 38:12). Enoch was walked to the same centre on his journeys and saw the mountain standing in it: *And I went from thence to the middle of the earth, and I saw a blessed place in which there were trees with branches abiding and blooming [of a dismembered tree]. And there I saw a holy mountain, and underneath the mountain to the east there was a stream and it flowed towards the south.* (1 Enoch 26:1-2) — Zion, the navel, the kept inheritance of the seed.
5212.note: 26:1 re-quoted in full from the live verse; 'the framework's land' and 'the live Enoch apparatus' phrasing removed.

15479.title: The angels which kept not their first estate — the Watchers reserved in everlasting chains (Genesis 6; 1 Enoch 10, 13, 21; Jubilees 5; 1 Peter 3, 2 Peter 2)
15479.summary_md: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day* (Jude 1:6). These are the Watchers — the *sons of Elohim (God)* of Genesis 6 who *saw the daughters of men that they were fair; and they took them wives,* and *there were giants in the earth in those days* (Genesis 6:1-4). They left their own habitation and broke the bound order, and the library tells in full what Jude names in brief. Yahuah (God) commanded, *Bind Azâzêl hand and foot, and cast him into the darkness... on the day of the great judgement he shall be cast into the fire* (1 Enoch 10:4-6). For Semjaza and his company the order was the same, with the term of it fixed: *And when their sons have slain one another, and they have seen the destruction of their beloved ones, bind them fast for seventy generations in the valleys of the earth, till the day of their judgement and of their consummation, till the judgement that is for ever and ever is consummated.* (1 Enoch 10:12), and then to be *led off to the abyss of fire... the prison in which they shall be confined for ever* (1 Enoch 10:13). Enoch was sent to pronounce the sentence already gone forth: *Azâzêl, thou shalt have no peace: a severe sentence has gone forth against thee to put thee in bonds* (1 Enoch 13:1); and on his journeys he was shown the place itself: *And he said unto me: ‘This place is the prison of the angels, and here they will be imprisoned for ever.’* (1 Enoch 21:10). Jubilees says the same: the angels are *bound in the depths of the earth... for ever, until the day of the great condemnation* (Jubilees 5:6,10). This is the third canonical pass over the Watchers — Peter wrote it twice: the *spirits in prison... in the days of Noah* to whom the Formed Son preached (1 Peter 3:19-20), and *the angels that sinned... delivered into chains of darkness, to be reserved unto judgment* (2 Peter 2:4). Jude, Peter, Genesis, 1 Enoch, and Jubilees hold one settled witness: the everlasting chains, the darkness, the judgment of the great day. The faith once delivered names the Watchers as Jude names them; the antinomians who left the faith are warned by the angels who left their estate.
15479.note: Mechanical re-quotes hold (10:12 in full; 21:11 → 21:10); the sentences around them mended so the full verses read as sentences.

388.title: Leaves without fruit — the fig tree, the unfruitful branches of Wisdom and Sirach, and the flock torn when its shepherds fall away
388.summary_md: *And when he saw a fig tree in the way, he came to it, and found nothing thereon, but leaves only, and said unto it, Let no fruit grow on thee henceforward for ever. And presently the fig tree withered away.* (Matthew 21:19). The tree had the look of a tree in season and nothing under the leaves, and the King's hand on it was a prophet's act against a leadership that had the same look. The prophets had used the fig that way for a long time, Hosea and Jeremiah and Joel and Micah all going to the tree for fruit and finding none. The Wisdom of Solomon says what becomes of such a tree: *for though they flourish in branches for a time; yet standing not last, they shall be shaken with the wind, and through the force of winds they shall be rooted out* (the Wisdom of Solomon 4:4), and *the imperfect branches shall be broken off, their fruit unprofitable, not ripe to eat, yes, meet for nothing* (the Wisdom of Solomon 4:5). Sirach says the same of the line that has no root: *her children shall not take root, and her branches shall bring forth no fruit* (Ecclesiasticus 23:25). The Animal Apocalypse shows what it costs the flock when the ones set over it forsake the house: *And after that I saw that when they forsook the house of Yahuah (Lord) and His tower they fell away entirely, and their eyes were blinded; and I saw Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep how He wrought much slaughter amongst them in their herds until those sheep invited that slaughter and betrayed His place. And He gave them over into the hands of the lions and tigers, and wolves and hyenas, and into the hand of the foxes, and to all the wild beasts, and those wild beasts began to tear in pieces those sheep.* (1 Enoch 89:54-55). The curse on the tree is not a curse on Yashar'el (Israel). It falls on the leaders with leaves and no fruit, the same men the woes of Matthew 23 are spoken to, the shepherds Ezekiel 34 and Jeremiah 23 said fed themselves and scattered the sheep. Leaves without fruit leave a flock without a shepherd, and the good shepherd came for the flock those shepherds scattered.
388.note: Degraded prose rewritten from scratch; the invented 89:35 quote replaced with the live 89:54-55; Wisdom 4:4-5 and Sirach 23:25 quotes kept; Matthew 21:19 from the index.

49.title: The light of the elect and the throne of glory
49.summary_md: *Ye are the light of the world. A city that is set on an hill cannot be hid.* (Matthew 5:14). *Let your light so shine before men, that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 5:16). He does not tell them to become the light. He tells them what they are, and the Parables of Enoch say where that light comes from and whose face it rests on: *And the righteous shall be in the light of the sun, And the elect in the light of eternal life: The days of their life shall be unending, And the days of the holy without number.* (1 Enoch 58:3). The first Parable opens with the same light appearing on the same people, and the powerful of the earth unable to look at it: *From that time those that possess the earth shall no longer be powerful and exalted: And they shall not be able to behold the face of the holy, For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits has caused His light to appear On the face of the holy, righteous, and elect.* (1 Enoch 38:4). And it is the Righteous One's own appearing that lights them: *And when the Righteous One shall appear before the eyes of the righteous, Whose elect works hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And light shall appear to the righteous and the elect who dwell on the earth, Where then will be the dwelling of the sinners, And where the resting-place of those who have denied Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits? It had been good for them if they had not been born.* (1 Enoch 38:2). The disciples are the light because they are the elect, and the light is his. A city on a hill in this age is the first showing of the face of the holy that the mighty will not be able to look upon in that day, and the good works that make men glorify the Father are the elect works that hang upon him.
49.note: Citation-only gloss rewritten with 38:2, 38:4 and 58:3 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew 5:14 and 5:16 from the index.

631.title: Gabriel, that stand in the presence — the named angel of the presence in 1 Enoch
631.summary_md: *And the angel answering said unto him, I am Gabriel, that stand in the presence of Elohim (God); and am sent to speak unto thee, and to shew thee these glad tidings.* (Luke 1:19). He gives the priest his name and his post, and both were already written. Enoch saw the post: *And on the four sides of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits I saw four presences, different from those that sleep not, and I learnt their names: for the angel that went with me made known to me their names, and showed me all the hidden things.* (1 Enoch 40:2). And he was given the names: *And he said to me: ‘This first is Michael, the merciful and long- suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.’* (1 Enoch 40:9). Gabriel is the third of the four who stand on the four sides of the throne, and the gospel sends that same angel from that same place to the altar of incense. The roster even follows into the next chapter, where Anna is *the daughter of Phanuel* (Luke 2:36). The angel who stands in the presence is not a New Testament invention. Luke names the one Enoch had already seen standing there.
631.note: Citation-only; 40:2 and 40:9 now quoted in full from the live text; Luke 1:19 from the index.

641.title: Satan fallen as lightning — the watcher-fall in 1 Enoch and Wisdom of Solomon
641.summary_md: *And he said unto them, I beheld Satan as lightning fall from heaven.* (Luke 10:18). *Behold, I give unto you power to tread on serpents and scorpions, and over all the power of the enemy: and nothing shall by any means hurt you.* (Luke 10:19). Seven words name a fall the Hebrew library had told at length. The King says it as the seventy come back glad that *even the devils are subject unto us through thy name* (Luke 10:17), town by town taking ground from the unclean spirits whose master he had watched come down. Enoch tells how the coming down began, by their own oath: *And they were in all two hundred; who descended in the days of Jared on the summit of Mount Hermon, and they called it Mount Hermon, because they had sworn and bound themselves by mutual imprecations upon it.* (1 Enoch 6:6). And he shows where a fallen star ends up: *And I saw one of those four who had come forth first, and he seized that first star which had fallen from the heaven, and bound it hand and foot and cast it into an abyss: now that abyss was narrow and deep, and horrible and dark.* (1 Enoch 88:1). The Wisdom of Solomon names what the fall brought with it: *Nevertheless through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it.* (the Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The enemy the seventy are given power to tread on is the devil whose envy was the door death came through, and the spirits they drive out are what is left loose of the host that came down on Hermon. The King names the fall in seven words and sends his men out against what it left behind.
641.note: Quotes stand; prose plained (no 'wisdom-stream', 'administration', 'inaugurated'); the internal note at the end removed.

648.title: The rich man and Lazaros — the hollow places of the dead in 1 Enoch and 2 Esdras
648.summary_md: The parable assumes a place the pulpit has never been able to describe. Lazaros dies and *was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;* (Luke 16:22). The rich man is awake there: *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.* (Luke 16:23). And the two places do not touch: *And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.* (Luke 16:26). Enoch was shown that very place. *And there was in it four hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. How smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.* (1 Enoch 22:2). The angel told him what they are for: *Then Raphael answered, one of the holy angels who was with me, and said unto me: ‘These hollow places have been created for this very purpose, that the spirits of the souls of the dead should assemble therein, yea that all the souls of the children of men should assemble here.* (1 Enoch 22:3), and how long they are for: *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). The dead are awake, they are kept apart, and the keeping has an end. The righteous have their own division with the bright spring of water, and the sinners theirs, set apart in pain till the great day (1 Enoch 22:9-11). That is why the parable can speak of torment and of comfort in the same hour without either being the last word. The last word is the resurrection out of those places: *And the earth shall restore those that are asleep in her, and so shall the dust those that dwell in silence, and the secret places shall deliver those souls that were committed to them.* (2 Esdras 7:32). When Abraham says they would not be persuaded though one rose from the dead, he is speaking of a rising out of exactly these chambers.
648.note: Was tagged READ but the gloss cited 22:9-11 for words that live at 22:2-4 and carried S185/framework/member-row language; rewritten with the live verses, Luke kept verbatim.

649.title: As it was in the days of Noach — the flood judgment in 1 Enoch and Jubilees
649.summary_md: When Yahusha (Jesus) wants to tell his disciples what his own day will look like, he reaches for the flood. *And as it was in the days of Noe, so shall it be also in the days of the Son of Adam.* (Luke 17:26). *They did eat, they drank, they married wives, they were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, and the flood came, and destroyed them all.* (Luke 17:27). The flood he points to is the one Enoch describes, and Enoch gives it a cause and a purpose that Genesis compresses. The warning went to Noah by the hand of an angel: *’Go to Noah and tell him in my name “Hide thyself!” and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The purpose was a seed carried through: *And now instruct him that he may escape and his seed may be preserved for all the generations of the world.’* (1 Enoch 10:3). Jubilees names what had filled the earth by then: *lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way* (Jubilees 5:2), and the decree that answered it: *I shall destroy man and all flesh upon the face of the earth which I have created* (Jubilees 5:4). So the eating and drinking and marrying of Luke 17:27 are not innocence; they are a world going about its business on the eve of a judgment it had been warned of, while one household was told to hide itself and was kept. The days of the Son of Adam run the same way, a corrupted order judged and a seed preserved through it, and the ones who are busy with the ordinary things are the ones the day overtakes.
649.note: Degraded prose (framework reads, S185, member-rows) rewritten; 10:2-3 quoted in full from the live text; Jubilees and Luke quotes kept as they stood.

650.title: The Son of Adam is come to seek and save the lost — the gathering of the tribes of Jacob in Sirach and 1 Enoch
650.summary_md: At the house of Zakkay (Zacchaeus) the King says what he came for: *For the Son of Adam is come to seek and to save that which was lost.* (Luke 19:10). The lost he means are a people, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered and gone from memory, and the library had been praying for their return long before he said it. Sirach asks for it by name: *gather all the tribes of Jacob together, and inherit you them, as from the beginning* (Sirach (Ecclesiasticus) 36:11), all the tribes and not Yahudah (Judah) alone, and names the people he is asking for: *have mercy upon the people that is called by your name, and upon Yashar'el (Israel), whom you have named your firstborn* (Sirach 36:12). Enoch saw the same gathering in his vision of the sheep. When the great horn was raised among the flock, *And it looked at them [and their eyes opened], and it cried to the sheep, and the rams saw it and all ran to it.* (1 Enoch 90:10). And at the end of the vision the whole scattered flock comes home: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). Seeking and saving the lost is shepherd's work, and the sheep he is seeking are the ones that were devoured and scattered through the long periods of the shepherds. Sirach prayed it, Enoch saw it, and at Zakkay's table the Son of Adam says he has come to do it.
650.note: Degraded prose rewritten; the old 90:3 quote (invented) replaced with the live 90:10 and 90:33, which carry the gathering; Sirach and Luke kept.

633.title: The multitude of the heavenly host — the innumerable host praising before Yahuah of Spirits in 1 Enoch
633.summary_md: Over the shepherds' fields the sky fills: *And suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host praising Elohim (God), and saying,* (Luke 2:13) *Glory to Elohim (God) in the highest, and on earth peace, good will toward men.* (Luke 2:14). Enoch had already stood in front of that host. *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). He heard what they do there, day and night: *Those who sleep not bless Thee: they stand before Thy glory and bless, praise, and extol, saying: “Holy, holy, holy, is Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: He filleth the earth with spirits.”’* (1 Enoch 39:12), and again, *And here my eyes saw all those who sleep not: they stand before Him and bless and say: ‘Blessed be Thou, and blessed be the name of Yahuah (Lord) for ever and ever.’* (1 Enoch 39:13). The host that never sleeps and never stops blessing before the throne is the host that came down over Bethlehem the night the Word was born in flesh. Their song did not change when they came down; the glory they give in the highest is the same blessing Enoch heard them give, now sounded over a stable because the One they bless had come to the earth.
633.note: The two Enoch 'citations' were really quotes in the old wording (40:1, 39:12-13 differ in the live text); re-quoted from the live verses, Luke kept.

652.title: Equal unto the angels — the children of the resurrection dwelling with the angels in 1 Enoch
652.summary_md: The Sadducees deny the resurrection and Yahusha (Jesus) answers them with what the raised will be: *But they which shall be accounted worthy to obtain that world, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry, nor are given in marriage:* (Luke 20:35), *Neither can they die any more: for they are equal unto the angels; and are the children of Elohim (God), being the children of the resurrection.* (Luke 20:36). Enoch was carried to the place where that life is already laid up. *And there I saw another vision, the dwelling-places of the holy, And the resting-places of the righteous.* (1 Enoch 39:4). *Here mine eyes saw their dwellings with His righteous angels, And their resting-places with the holy. And they petitioned and interceded and prayed for the children of men, And righteousness flowed before them as water, And mercy like dew upon the earth: Thus it is amongst them for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 39:5). And at the end of the book the righteous are told plainly what they are being kept for: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). *Be hopeful, and cast not away your hope; for ye shall have great joy as the angels of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:4). *And now fear not, ye righteous, when ye see the sinners growing strong and prospering in their ways: be not companions with them, but keep afar from their violence; for ye shall become companions of the hosts of heaven.* (1 Enoch 104:6). Equal unto the angels, companions of the hosts of heaven, dwelling with the righteous angels: it is one picture. Daniel saw the same people rise to it: *And many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt.* (Daniel 12:2). *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). The King grounds it in the bush, where the Elohim (God) of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob is not the Elohim (God) of the dead but of the living; the fathers are not gone, they are kept, and the resting-places Enoch saw are where they wait to shine.
652.note: The old Enoch 'citations' were quotes in old wording (39:4-5 reworded; the old 104:4 words are not at 104:4); re-quoted 39:4-5 and 104:2, 104:4, 104:6 from the live text; Daniel added from the index; Exodus 3:6 named in prose.

33891.title: Hereafter shall the Son of Adam sit on the right hand of the power of Elohim (Psalm 110; Daniel 7)
33891.summary_md:
Before the council they ask, *Art thou the Messiah (Christ)? tell us* (Luke 22:67), and Yahusha (Jesus) answers with a throne: *Hereafter shall the Son of Adam sit on the right hand of the power of Elohim (God).* (Luke 22:69). He names himself by David's oracle and by Daniel's vision at once.

David heard the Father speak it: *Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool* (Psalm 110:1); the Father seats the Son at his own right hand. And Daniel saw it given in heaven: *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13). The likeness is kept in the words, one *like* the Son of Adam, because the Formed Son came in flesh and was brought near before the Father, and the dominion was handed to him there: *And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom, that all people, nations, and languages, should serve him: his dominion is an everlasting dominion, which shall not pass away, and his kingdom that which shall not be destroyed.* (Daniel 7:14). It is given him. The Son is enthroned by the Father; he never seizes what is the Father's to bestow.

Peter, once converted and strengthening his brethren, preaches this very throne: *For David is not ascended into the heavens: but he saith himself, Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand,* (Acts 2:34). And Enoch saw the same seating and the same faces looking on it. *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). *And one portion of them shall look on the other, And they shall be terrified, And they shall be downcast of countenance, And pain shall seize them, When they see that Son of Adam Sitting on the throne of his glory.* (1 Enoch 62:5). The men who blindfolded him and struck him are told to their faces where they will next see him, and Enoch had already written down what their faces will do when they do.
33891.note: The 62:5 quote was invented (its words are 60:24); replaced with the live 62:2 and 62:5, which say exactly what the thread needs; the rest kept, 'the kaph stands' said in plain words.

653.title: Paradise and the chambers of the souls of the dead in 1 Enoch
653.summary_md: To the thief beside him the King says a word about where they are both going before the day is out: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said unto him, Verily I say unto thee, To day shalt thou be with me in paradise.* (Luke 23:43). Enoch had been shown the place. *And there was in it four hollow places, deep and wide and very smooth. How smooth are the hollow places and deep and dark to look at.* (1 Enoch 22:2). *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). The dead are not all kept in one room: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9). The paradise the thief was promised that same day is the righteous division of those chambers, the one with the bright spring, set apart from the chamber of the sinners who wait in pain for the great day. The King went there that day, and the thief with him. The rich man and Lazaros in Luke 16 look across the gulf between those same divisions, and when Paul says he ascended on high and led captivity captive, the captives he led out are the ones who had been waiting by that spring. The chambers Enoch walked through are what Luke names with a single word.
653.note: Old 22:9/22:11/22:16 quotes were at the wrong addresses (22:16 does not exist live); re-quoted 22:2, 22:4, 22:9 from the live text; degraded prose and the internal thread reference removed; Luke 16 and Ephesians 4:8 named in prose.

635.title: The genealogy back to Adam, the son of Elohim — the seed of Adam in Jubilees and 1 Enoch
635.summary_md: Luke runs his genealogy backward until it can go no further: *Which was the son of Enos, which was the son of Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of Elohim (God).* (Luke 3:38). That line, father to son back to the man Elohim (God) formed, is the thread the whole promise hangs on, and the library watched it being kept. Jubilees tells how it was carried past the first murder: *And Adam and his wife mourned for Abel four weeks of years, and in the fourth year of the fifth week they became joyful, and Adam knew his wife again, and she bare him a son, and he called his name Seth; for he said “Elohim (God) has raised up a second seed to us on the earth instead of Abel; for Cain slew him.”* (Jubilees 4:7). Enoch saw the same line in his first dream, as cattle. *Before I took thy mother Edna, I saw in a vision on my bed, and behold a bull came forth from the earth, and that bull was white; and after it came forth a heifer, and along with this (latter) came forth two bulls, one of them black and the other red.* (1 Enoch 85:3). The black bull gores the red one, and then the second seed comes: *And after that she bore another white bull, and after him she bore many bulls and black cows.* (1 Enoch 85:8). *And I saw in my sleep that white bull likewise grow and become a great white bull, and from him proceeded many white bulls, and they resembled him.* (1 Enoch 85:9). White bull following white bull, each resembling the one before, is Seth's line going down the generations, and Luke's list is that same line read upward. Enoch counts himself in it from the same head: Adam is *the seventh from Adam, the first man whom Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits created* (1 Enoch 60:8), and Jude counts the same way: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14). Luke, Jubilees, Enoch, and Jude are all counting the same fathers, and the count ends where Luke ends it, at the son of Elohim (God).
635.note: Degraded prose (FRAMEWORK-CENTRAL, toledot labels) rewritten; Jubilees 4:7 and 85:3, 85:8-9, 60:8 quoted in full from the live text; Jude added from the index. 60:8 quote is a partial because the verse runs on about Behemoth; it is the live wording.

638.title: Legion into the deep — the spirits of the giants and the place of condemnation in 1 Enoch and Jubilees
638.summary_md: The spirits in the man at Gerasa know who has come ashore: *When he saw Yahusha (Jesus), he cried out, and fell down before him, and with a loud voice said, What have I to do with thee, Yahusha (Jesus), thou Son of Elohim (God) most high? I beseech thee, torment me not.* (Luke 8:28). And they know where they are headed: *And they besought him that he would not command them to go out into the deep.* (Luke 8:31). Enoch tells where such spirits came from and why they dread the deep. *And now, the giants, who are produced from the spirits and flesh, shall be called evil spirits upon the earth, and on the earth shall be their dwelling.* (1 Enoch 15:8). *Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called.* (1 Enoch 15:9). They have a season, and it has an end already written: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated.”* (1 Enoch 16:1). Noah asked for them to be shut away before the end: *And You know how Your Watchers, the fathers of these spirits, acted in my day: and as for these spirits which are living, imprison them and hold them fast in the place of condemnation, and let them not bring destruction on the sons of your servant, my Elohim (God); for these are malignant, and created in order to destroy.* (Jubilees 10:5). So Legion is begging not to be sent early to the place Noah prayed them into and Enoch said they are bound for. The torment they fear is the deep before their appointed day, and the One standing on the shore in flesh is the One who holds that day.
638.note: Old 'citations' quoted 15:8, 15:11, 16:1 in wording that differs from the live text (the old 15:8 words are the bracketed 15:10); re-quoted 15:8-9 and 16:1 live; Jubilees 10:5 and Luke quoted in full from the index; the internal 'existing thread' remark dropped.

32.title: The Magi and the Book of Luminaries
32.summary_md: *Now when Yahusha (Jesus) was born in Bethlehem of Judaea in the days of Herod the king, behold, there came wise men from the east to Jerusalem,* (Matthew 2:1) *Saying, Where is he that is born King of the Yahudim (Jews)? for we have seen his star in the east, and are come to worship him.* (Matthew 2:2). Men who read the heavens for a king were not working from nothing. The library carries a whole book on the subject, and it opens by saying where the knowledge came from: *The book of the courses of the luminaries of the heaven, the relations of each, according to their classes, their dominion and their seasons, according to their names and places of origin, and according to their months, which Uriel, the holy angel, who was with me, who is their guide, showed me; and he showed me all their laws exactly as they are, and how it is with regard to all the years of the world and unto eternity, till the new creation is accomplished which dureth till eternity.* (1 Enoch 72:1). That is the Book of Luminaries, 1 Enoch 72–82, the heavens read as law and appointed season rather than as omen. Daniel stood at the head of the wise men of Babylon and Persia, and a learning like Enoch's in the hands of men like Daniel's is where the Magi's watching came from. Enoch's second dream, the vision of the sheep in chapters 89–90, ends with a great horn raised among the flock and a white bull before whom all the beasts bow, and men who held that book knew there was one to look for. The star over Judea and the men who followed it belong inside that tradition, not outside it.
32.note: Mentioned Enoch without a verse; 72:1 was quoted in the old text and stands live, now cited; 'extras-tier witness' and 'Hebrew library' labels removed; Matthew quoted in full from the index.

382.title: Many be called, but few chosen — 1 Enoch 48 and 2 Esdras 8 on the broad call and the few
382.summary_md: The parable of the laborers closes on a hard line: *So the last shall be first, and the first last: for many be called, but few chosen.* (Matthew 20:16). The call goes out broadly because the sheep are scattered everywhere and no one can tell them by sight, and the chosen are the ones who were his before the call ever reached them. He says it himself in John 10: *ye believe not, because ye are not of my sheep ... my sheep hear my voice.* The hearing does not make a sheep; it shows one. Enoch saw the broad call as a fountain anyone could come to: *And in that place I saw the fountain of righteousness Which was inexhaustible: And around it were many fountains of wisdom: And all the thirsty drank of them, And were filled with wisdom, And their dwellings were with the righteous and holy and elect.* (1 Enoch 48:1). And he saw who the Son of Adam was kept for: *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). Ezra was told the same count in plainer arithmetic: *there be many created, but few shall be saved* (2 Esdras 8:3). The many are not cheated; the call really went out to them. The few are the ones written from the foundation of the world (Revelation 13:8), who heard because they were his, and who then walked in it, because the warning about being blotted out is spoken to the wheat and never to the tares. The last made first are the scattered ones nobody expected, and the first made last are the ones who stood in the field all day and never bore the fruit.
382.note: Old summary was almost entirely internal shorthand (Red Line #11, substance chains, Reformed/Arminian labels); rewritten in plain words around 48:1 and 48:7 (live); the old 39:1 quote dropped (39:1 is a Noah fragment about the descent of the holy children and does not carry the thought); John 10 and 2 Esdras 8:3 kept as the old summary quoted them; title plainer.

629.title: The Son of Adam enthroned on the throne of glory in the Parables of Enoch
629.summary_md: Under oath at the Sanhedrin the King answers the high priest plainly: *And Yahusha (Jesus) said, I am: and ye shall see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Mark 14:62). He is naming himself by a title the Parables of Enoch had already given to one figure. *And there I saw One who had a head of days, And His head was white like wool, And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.* (1 Enoch 46:1). *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). *And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 46:4). The seating itself comes later in the Parables: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). And the rulers who had him bound will do what Enoch said they would: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). The Parables name him beside the Head of Days as a title, the chosen one seated on the throne of glory. Mark's courtroom has that same one standing in the dock, telling the court that condemns him where they will next see him sitting.
629.note: Degraded prose and Red Line talk removed; 46:1, 3, 4 quoted in full; the old 62:1 and 62:9 quotes were other verses' words (62:2 and 46:4) — replaced with live 62:2, 62:7, 62:9.

624.title: The worm dieth not and the place of punishment in Judith and 1 Enoch
624.summary_md: Three times in a row the King says it: *And if thy hand offend thee, cut it off: it is better for thee to enter into life maimed, than having two hands to go into hell, into the fire that never shall be quenched:* (Mark 9:43) *Where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not quenched.* (Mark 9:44). The picture is Isaiah's: *And they shall go forth, and look upon the carcases of the men that have transgressed against me: for their worm shall not die, neither shall their fire be quenched; and they shall be an abhorring unto all flesh.* (Isaiah 66:24). Judith sings the same two things together for the day of judgment: *Yahuah (God) Almighty will take vengeance of them in the day of judgment, in putting fire and worms in their flesh; and they shall feel them, and weep for ever.* (Judith 16:17). Enoch was walked through the geography of it. The dead are held first: *And these places have been made to receive them till the day of their judgement and till their appointed period [till the period appointed], till the great judgement (comes) upon them.’* (1 Enoch 22:4). Then he is shown a blessed land full of trees and a cursed valley beside it, and asks what the valley is for: *Then Uriel, one of the holy angels who was with me, answered and said: ‘This accursed valley is for those who are accursed for ever: Here shall all the accursed be gathered together who utter with their lips against Yahuah (Lord) unseemly words and of His glory speak hard things. Here shall they be gathered together, and here shall be their place of judgement.* (1 Enoch 27:2). That cursed valley beside the holy mountain is the valley of Hinnom, and Gehenna, the word Mark uses for hell, is its name. The King is not inventing a place to frighten people with. He is naming the valley Enoch stood over, with Isaiah's worm and Judith's fire, appointed for a day of judgment that has not yet come, after a holding that has an end.
624.note: Degraded 'framework-honest' prose removed; the old 22:11 quote is the live 22:4, re-quoted; 27:2 quoted in full; Mark, Isaiah from the index, Judith kept as the old summary quoted it.

118.title: The restoration of the age to come — 1 Enoch 5 and 10, Jubilees 23
118.summary_md: When John sends from prison to ask whether he is the one, Yahusha (Jesus) answers with what is happening in front of the messengers: *The blind receive their sight, and the lame walk, the lepers are cleansed, and the deaf hear, the dead are raised up, and the poor have the gospel preached to them.* (Matthew 11:5). It is Isaiah's list: *Then the eyes of the blind shall be opened, and the ears of the deaf shall be unstopped.* (Isaiah 35:5). And it is a taste of an age the library had already described in full. Enoch tells what is kept for the elect once the judgment has passed: *And for you the godless there shall be a curse. But for the elect there shall be light and joy and peace, And they shall inherit the earth.* (1 Enoch 5:7). *And then there shall be bestowed upon the elect wisdom, And they shall all live and never again sin, Either through ungodliness or through pride: But they who are wise shall be humble.* (1 Enoch 5:8). *And they shall not again transgress, Nor shall they sin all the days of their life, Nor shall they die of (the divine) anger or wrath, But they shall complete the number of the days of their life. And their lives shall be increased in peace, And the years of their joy shall be multiplied, In eternal gladness and peace, All the days of their life.* (1 Enoch 5:9). The same promise is given to Noah's seed after the Watchers are bound: *And then shall all the righteous escape, And shall live till they beget thousands of children, And all the days of their youth and their old age Shall they complete in peace.* (1 Enoch 10:17). *And then shall the whole earth be tilled in righteousness, and shall all be planted with trees and be full of blessing.* (1 Enoch 10:18). Jubilees 23 says the same of the last days, long life, peace and joy, no Satan and no destroyer, and healing. What John's messengers saw was that age reaching back into theirs, the blind and lame and dead already being handled the way the whole earth will be handled. The day of vengeance in the same breath of Isaiah 61 he left unread, because that part waits for his return.
118.note: Internal shorthand rewritten; the old 5:7-9 words were not the live text — 5:7, 5:8, 5:9 now quoted in full from the live verses, with 10:17-18; Matthew and Isaiah from the index; Jubilees 23 named in prose (not in the index).

200.title: Mysteries hidden from the foundation of the world revealed to the elect — 1 Enoch 46 and 48, Wisdom of Solomon 6, 2 Esdras 6
200.summary_md: *All these things spake Yahusha (Jesus) unto the multitude in parables; and without a parable spake he not unto them:* (Matthew 13:34) *That it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth in parables; I will utter things which have been kept secret from the foundation of the world.* (Matthew 13:35). The psalm he is fulfilling is Asaph's, and the pattern of things hidden since the foundation and then opened to a chosen few runs all through the library. Enoch saw the one who does the opening, and was told who he is: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). He was himself the first thing hidden: *And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.* (1 Enoch 48:6). *And the wisdom of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath revealed him to the holy and righteous; For he hath preserved the lot of the righteous, Because they have hated and despised this world of unrighteousness, And have hated all its works and ways in the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits: For in his name they are saved, And according to his good pleasure hath it been in regard to their life.* (1 Enoch 48:7). Solomon speaks the same way as a teacher: *as for wisdom, what she is, and how she came up, I will tell you, and will not hide mysteries from you* (Wisdom of Solomon 6:22), and Ezra is told of the last days when *the truth, which hath been so long without fruit, shall be declared* (2 Esdras 6:28). So when the King speaks in parables to the crowd and opens them to the disciples, he is doing the work Enoch saw the Son of Adam doing, revealing the treasures of what was hidden, and the disciples receive it because, as he had just told them from Isaiah 6, it was given to them to receive. The sower of the good seed in the next verse is this same Son of Adam.
200.note: Internal shorthand (four moves, Red Line #11, wisdom-stream) rewritten; 46:3, 48:6, 48:7 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom 6:22 and 2 Esdras 6:28 kept as the old summary quoted them.

114.title: Names written before the Great One and not blotted out — 1 Enoch 103–104 and confessing or denying him
114.summary_md: *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32). *But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:33). The confessing he promises is a name spoken before the Father, and the library knows the names are already written there. Enoch swears to the righteous what he has read: *That all goodness and joy and glory are prepared for them, And written down for the spirits of those who have died in righteousness, And that manifold good shall be given to you in recompense for your labours, And that your lot is abundantly beyond the lot of the living.* (1 Enoch 103:3). *And the spirits of you who have died in righteousness shall live and rejoice, And their spirits shall not perish, nor their memorial from before the face of the Great One Unto all the generations of the world: wherefore no longer fear their contumely.* (1 Enoch 103:4). And a few lines on: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Names are written before, and the only thing scripture ever says can happen to a written name is that it is blotted out, at Sinai when Moses pleads, in David's psalm, and in the promise to Sardis: *He that overcometh, the same shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels.* (Revelation 3:5). Confess his name before the Father is the same phrase Matthew 10 uses. The one who lives out the confession keeps a name that was always there; the one who denies him under pressure is risking the blotting, which is why the warning is spoken to those whose names are written and not to anyone else.
114.note: The old 103:3 and 103:8 quotes were not the live text (the live 103:8 is a woe); re-quoted 103:3-4 and added 104:1, which carries the 'names written' line; Red Line talk removed; Revelation 3:5 from the index; Exodus 32:33 and Psalm 69:28 named in prose.

189.title: No forgiveness for the hardened heart — Jubilees 15, 1 Enoch 65, Wisdom of Solomon 12
189.summary_md: *And whosoever speaketh a word against the Son of Adam, it shall be forgiven him: but whosoever speaketh against the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), it shall not be forgiven him, neither in this world, neither in the world to come.* (Matthew 12:32). The men he says this to have just watched the Spirit cast out a demon and called it the work of Beelzebub. They saw the thing clearly and named it the devil's, and that is the hardening the library already knew had no road back from it. Enoch was told it about the ones who had learned the Watchers' secrets and would not turn: *And these—they have no place of repentance for ever, because they have shown them what was hidden, and they are the damned: but as for thee, my son, Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits knows that thou art pure, and guiltless of this reproach concerning the secrets.* (1 Enoch 65:11). Jubilees names the same wrath for the ones who set the covenant aside on purpose: *there will be great wrath from Yahuah (the Lord) ... because they have forsaken His covenant and have turned aside from His word* (Jubilees 15:33-34). And the Wisdom of Solomon says why the patience ran out on the Canaanites: he gave them place for repentance, not being ignorant that their malice was bred in them and that their way of thinking would never change (Wisdom of Solomon 12:10). None of these is about a slip of the tongue. They are about a settled refusal, eyes open, that has made up its mind against the correction. That is why the one who fears he has committed this sin almost certainly has not; the fear is a conscience still working, and a hardened heart does not lie awake over it.
189.note: Internal shorthand and the four-costume aside rewritten in plain words; 65:11 quoted in full from the live text; Jubilees kept as the old summary quoted it; Wisdom 12:10 (not in index) given in prose; the pastoral reading kept; title plainer.

12607.title: Whose names are in the book of life — the books of the living (Exodus 32, Daniel 12, Malachi 3, 1 Enoch)
12607.summary_md: Paul names his fellowlabourers at Philippi as those *whose names are in the book of life* (Philippians 4:3), and that book is no late invention but the heavenly register the whole library knows. At Sinai Moses appealed to it: *if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32), and Yahuah (LORD) answered, *Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book* (Exodus 32:33). Daniel learned that deliverance in the last great trouble belongs to *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). Malachi saw it kept for the faithful: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16), who shall be his *in that day when I make up my jewels* (Malachi 3:17). Enoch watched the very same books opened before the throne: *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). He swore by what he had read in them: *Mighty One in dominion, and by His greatness I swear to you. I know a mystery And have read the heavenly tablets, And have seen the holy books, And have found written therein and inscribed regarding them:* (1 Enoch 103:2). And he knew the dark side of the ledger too: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3), the same blotting Yahuah (LORD) spoke of at Sinai. So when Paul says the Philippian partners' names are in the book of life, he is placing them in the one covenant ledger that runs from Moses to Daniel to the throne of the Head of Days, the book of remembrance, the books of the living, in which the righteous are written and kept and not blotted out, gathered as the jewels of Yahuah (LORD).
12607.note: The 104:2 quote ('I have beheld the books of life') is not in Charles; replaced with the live 103:2 ('have seen the holy books'); 47:3 and 108:3 quoted in full from the live text; the rest kept.

37.title: The plant of righteousness and the Branch
37.summary_md: When the Watchers are bound and the earth is cleansed, the first thing commanded to grow in it is a plant: *Destroy all wrong from the face of the earth and let every evil work come to an end: and let the plant of righteousness and truth appear: and it shall prove a blessing; the works of righteousness and truth shall be planted in truth and joy for evermore.* (1 Enoch 10:16). The prophets watch for the same growth and call it the Branch. Isaiah's shoot from the stump of Jesse, the *netser*, becomes in the same chapter the ensign the scattered gather to: *And in that day there shall be a root of Jesse, which shall stand for an ensign of the people; to it shall the Gentiles seek: and his rest shall be glorious.* (Isaiah 11:10). Jeremiah names him outright: *Behold, the days come, saith Yahuah (LORD), that I will raise unto David a righteous Branch, and a King shall reign and prosper, and shall execute judgment and justice in the earth.* (Jeremiah 23:5). Zechariah calls him *my servant the BRANCH* and says *the man whose name is The BRANCH* shall build the temple of Yahuah (LORD) (Zechariah 3:8; 6:12). Then Matthew brings the child of the promise to live in a town whose name carries the word: *And he came and dwelt in a city called Nazareth: that it might be fulfilled which was spoken by the prophets, He shall be called a Nazarene.* (Matthew 2:23). No single prophet says those words; Matthew says the prophets, and Natsareth is Branch-town. The plant Enoch saw appearing after the judgment, the shoot and the Branch the prophets kept promising, and the boy from Natsareth are one and the same, and the books that carry the first witness to it are the ones the Reformation cut from the library.
37.note: Degraded 'register / extras-tier' prose rewritten; 10:16 quoted in full (live, same); Isaiah 11:10, Jeremiah 23:5, Matthew 2:23 added from the index; Zechariah named with its two phrases in prose.

26053.title: The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night
26053.summary_md: *Yahuah (LORD) is thy keeper: Yahuah (LORD) is thy shade upon thy right hand* (Psalm 121:5), and so *The sun shall not smite thee by day, nor the moon by night* (Psalm 121:6). The same shade shields the returning exiles: *neither shall the heat nor sun smite them: for he that hath mercy on them shall lead them, even by the springs of water shall he guide them* (Isaiah 49:10), and brings them at last where no heat can reach: *neither shall the sun light on them, nor any heat* (Revelation 7:16). The lights themselves are no terror to the one he keeps, because Enoch saw what holds them: *And I saw the chambers of the sun and moon, whence they proceed and whither they come again, and their glorious return, and how one is superior to the other, and their stately orbit, and how they do not leave their orbit, and they add nothing to their orbit and they take nothing from it, and they keep faith with each other, in accordance with the oath by which they are bound together.* (1 Enoch 41:5). *And first the sun goes forth and traverses his path according to the commandment of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, and mighty is His name for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 41:6). Sun and moon are bound by an oath and walk by a commandment. The Keeper who gave the commandment is the one standing at thy right hand, and the lights he rules cannot harm what he shades.
26053.note: The abridged 41:5 quote did not match the live wording; 41:5 and 41:6 now quoted in full; the rest kept.

28854.title: Let Every Thing That Hath Breath Praise Yah — the Consummation of the Psalter
28854.summary_md: The whole Psalter ends on a single, total summons: *Let every thing that hath breath praise Yahuah (LORD). Praise ye Yahuah (LORD)* (Psalm 150:6). Every breathing creature — kol haneshamah — is called, and the breath itself is the clue: it was given at creation, *And Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) formed man of the dust of the ground, and breathed into his nostrils the breath of life; and man became a living soul* (Genesis 2:7), and it is held by the One *that giveth breath unto the people upon it, and spirit to them that walk therein* (Isaiah 42:5), who *giveth to all life, and breath, and all things* (Acts 17:25). The gift returns as praise. This widens the keystone's closing vow — *let all flesh bless his holy name for ever and ever* (Psalm 145:21) — to the very edge of creation, and it is sworn by Yahuah himself: *unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear* (Isaiah 45:23), *That at the name of Yahusha (Jesus) every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth* (Philippians 2:10). The restored library hears it already sounding above and ahead: *And I heard the voices of those four presences as they uttered praises before Yahuah (Lord) of glory.* (1 Enoch 40:3); and when the Elect One lifts up his countenance to judge, the whole host summoned before him *On that day shall raise one voice, and bless and glorify and exalt in the spirit of faith, and in the spirit of wisdom, and in the spirit of patience, and in the spirit of mercy, and in the spirit of judgement and of peace, and in the spirit of goodness, and shall all say with one voice: "Blessed is He, and may the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits be blessed for ever and ever."* (1 Enoch 61:11); and the *peculiar people above all peoples* are sanctified *to bless Him who has created all things* (Jubilees 2:21). It consummates in John's vision, where *every creature which is in heaven, and on the earth, and under the earth, and such as are in the sea, and all that are in them* cries *Blessing, and honour, and glory, and power, be unto him that sitteth upon the throne, and unto the Lamb for ever and ever* (Revelation 5:13). This is the telos of the whole Psalter: the gathered two-house people and all that breathes, in one final Hallelujah. Praise ye Yah.
28854.note: Mechanical re-quote kept (40:3, 61:11 live); the sentence leading into 61:11 mended so 'On that day shall raise one voice' has its subject.

191.title: Resurrection from Sheol — the gates of the dead give back what they received — the sign of Yonah in Wisdom of Solomon 16, 1 Enoch 51, Jubilees 23
191.summary_md: They ask for a sign and he gives them one they cannot see yet: *For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the whale’s belly; so shall the Son of Adam be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.* (Matthew 12:40). Three days and three nights in the heart of the earth means Sheol, and coming out of it means Sheol gave him back, and the library had been saying for a long time that Sheol will give back. Solomon says it of Yahuah (God): *thou hast power of life and death: thou leadest to the gates of Sheol, and bringest up again* (Wisdom of Solomon 16:13). Enoch says it of the day the Elect One takes the throne: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1). *And he shall choose the righteous and holy from among them: For the day has drawn nigh that they should be saved.* (1 Enoch 51:2). Jubilees promises the servants that *the Lord will heal His servants, And they shall rise up and see great peace* (Jubilees 23:30). The sign of Yonah is the King announcing that he himself will go down through those gates first and be brought up, the firstfruits of what Enoch saw the earth and Sheol do for everyone entrusted to them. The count is a real count.
