Three days and three nights is what he said, and the Friday evening to Sunday morning the tradition settled on does not hold three nights, which is one more reason to read the week of his death by the calendar of the feasts rather than by the calendar handed down.
191.note: Internal shorthand rewritten; 51:1-2 quoted in full from the live text; Wisdom and Jubilees kept as the old summary quoted them; Matthew from the index; the literal three-days point kept in plain words.

2076.title: The reed to measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein (Ezekiel 40)
2076.summary_md: The chapter opens with a measuring: *And there was given me a reed like unto a rod: and the angel stood, saying, Rise, and measure the temple of Elohim (God), and the altar, and them that worship therein.* (Revelation 11:1). This is Ezekiel's reed: *behold, there was a man, whose appearance was like the appearance of brass, with a line of flax in his hand, and a measuring reed* (Ezekiel 40:3), who charged the prophet to *behold with thine eyes... and declare all that thou seest to the house of Yashar'el (Israel)* (Ezekiel 40:4). It is Zechariah's line too, *behold a man with a measuring line in his hand... To measure Jerusalem* (Zechariah 2:1), and that measuring ended in restoration, Yahuah (LORD) himself a wall of fire and the glory in her midst. The measuring is no demolition. It marks off what belongs to Yahuah (LORD), a *separation between the sanctuary and the profane place* (Ezekiel 42:20). The outer court is left out of it: *But the court which is without the temple leave out, and measure it not; for it is given unto the Gentiles: and the holy city shall they tread under foot forty and two months* (Revelation 11:2). Daniel heard the same treading and the same cry, *to give both the sanctuary and the host to be trodden under foot* (Daniel 8:13), and Isaiah grieved it: *our adversaries have trodden down thy sanctuary* (Isaiah 63:18). But the trampling is measured and brief, forty and two months, a little while, and the temple and the worshippers are kept. Enoch saw where the measuring leads. The old house is taken down and carried off, and then: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). The worshippers counted with the reed are the sheep being gathered into that greater house. To measure the temple is to mark off the regathered Yashar'el (Israel) for the restoration.
2076.note: The 90:17 quote was not Charles's wording; replaced with the live 90:29, which carries the new house with all the sheep in it; the rest kept.

2163.title: Names not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain (Exodus 32, Psalm 69, Daniel 12)
2163.summary_md: *And all that dwell upon the earth shall worship him, whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world.* (Revelation 13:8). The worshippers of the beast are told apart by a book, and it is no new register opened on the day someone believes. It is the book written of old, the one Moses pleaded over at Sinai: *if not, blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32). It is the *book of the living* the psalmist knew, set over against the company of the saved: *let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28). It is the book that carries Daniel's people through the worst trouble: *And at that time shall Michael stand up, the great prince which standeth for the children of thy people: and there shall be a time of trouble, such as never was since there was a nation even to that same time: and at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book.* (Daniel 12:1). One book runs through all of it, the register of Yahuah (LORD)'s own, the names written from the foundation of the world. Enoch saw it opened at the judgment of the shepherds: *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). And earlier, in the Parables, the same books before the same throne: *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). To worship the beast is to be found outside the books of the living. To belong to the Lamb is to have had a name written in his book before the beast ever rose. The Lamb who opens the book is the Lord of the sheep who gathers his own; the writing of the name and the gathering are one act, settled before the foundation of the world, and no confession adds a name that was not there. The patience of the saints rests on that writing. The beast can make war on the body, but it cannot reach the name.
2163.note: The 90:12 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:20 (sealed books opened before the Lord of the sheep) and 47:3 (books of the living); 'the framework's order' said in plain words; the rest kept, Daniel 12:1 in full from the index.

2165.title: The second beast like a lamb, the false prophet and the fire (Deuteronomy 13, 1 Kings 18, Daniel 3)
2165.summary_md: *And I beheld another beast coming up out of the earth; and he had two horns like a lamb, and he spake as a dragon* (Revelation 13:11). The second beast wears the costume of a lamb and speaks with the dragon's voice. He is the false prophet, and the Torah named his kind long before. *If there arise among you a prophet, or a dreamer of dreams, and giveth thee a sign or a wonder* (Deuteronomy 13:1), and the sign comes to pass, yet he draws you after other gods, *thou shalt not hearken*, for *Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) proveth you, to know whether ye love Yahuah Elohaychem (the LORD your God) with all your heart* (Deuteronomy 13:3). A sign that comes true is no proof of a true prophet; it is the proving of your loyalty. So when this beast *doeth great wonders, so that he maketh fire come down from heaven on the earth in the sight of men* (Revelation 13:13) and *deceiveth them that dwell on the earth by the means of those miracles* (Revelation 13:14), he is the sign-worker the Torah taught the people to refuse. And the sign he picks is the very one the true Elohim (God) once owned. At Carmel the test was *the Elohim (God) that answereth by fire, let him be Elohim (God)* (1 Kings 18:24), and Yahuah (LORD) alone answered while the false prophets' altar stayed cold. Now the false prophet apes that fire from heaven to claim a proof that was Yahuah (LORD)'s, and it is a deceiver's costume, not the verdict of heaven. His end is an image and an edict: *as many as would not worship the image of the beast should be killed* (Revelation 13:15), the same decree Nebuchadnezzar made, *whoso falleth not down and worshippeth shall the same hour be cast into the midst of a burning fiery furnace* (Daniel 3:6). But the fire he calls down to deceive does not get the last word. Enoch saw the end appointed for the ones who misled the flock: *And the judgement was held first over the stars, and they were judged and found guilty, and went to the place of condemnation, and they were cast into an abyss, full of fire and flaming, and full of pillars of fire.* (1 Enoch 90:24). *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). The false prophet who calls fire from heaven goes into the fire himself, and the saints who refuse his sign, like the three who would not bow, are kept by the Elohim (God) who is faithful whether he delivers or not.
2165.note: The 90:14 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:24-25 (the stars and the seventy shepherds cast into the fiery abyss); the rest kept with the dashes eased.

1918.title: The tree of life in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God) — Eden restored (Genesis 2)
1918.summary_md: The first letter ends with the oldest promise of all: *He that hath an ear, let him hear what the Spirit saith unto the churches; To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God).* (Revelation 2:7). Paradise is Eden by its Greek name, and the tree is the very tree of Genesis: *And out of the ground made Yahuah Elohim (the LORD God) to grow every tree that is pleasant to the sight, and good for food; the tree of life also in the midst of the garden, and the tree of knowledge of good and evil.* (Genesis 2:9). The tree barred to Adam after the fall is set before the overcomer, the old inheritance opened again rather than a new reward. Ezekiel saw it multiplied into a riverside orchard by the waters from the sanctuary: *all trees for meat, whose leaf shall not fade, neither shall the fruit thereof be consumed... and the fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12). Enoch was shown the same tree, by a mountain that looked like a throne: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). Michael told him who it is kept for and when: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). And the book itself shows the promise kept at the end: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). Genesis bars the tree; Ezekiel and Enoch see it reserved; the letter promises it; the new Jerusalem throws it open. It is one unbroken hope, Eden brought to its end, the curse undone, the tree given freely to the one who keeps the works unto the end.
1918.note: The old 24:11 does not exist live (its words are 25:5); 24:4 and 25:4-5 quoted in full; Revelation 2:7, 22:2 and Genesis 2:9 in full from the index; the draft's broken 'whose fruit Its fruit' sentence mended.

2423.title: The books were opened, and the book of life (Daniel 7 and 12, Malachi 3)
2423.summary_md: *And I saw the dead, small and great, stand before Elohim (God); and the books were opened: and another book was opened, which is the book of life: and the dead were judged out of those things which were written in the books, according to their works.* (Revelation 20:12). Daniel saw the like: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). This is the one reckoning of the dead the seventh trumpet already sounded, *the time of the dead, that they should be judged* (Revelation 11:18), shown here again in full. Daniel was told deliverance comes to *every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1), and that *many of them that sleep in the dust of the earth shall awake, some to everlasting life, and some to shame and everlasting contempt* (Daniel 12:2), the very division that falls at the throne, some found written in the book of life and some cast into the lake of fire. The book of the living the psalmist knew can be blotted out, *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28); names are written and never added, but they can be blotted. Malachi names the same record kept for the faithful: *a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared Yahuah (LORD), and that thought upon his name* (Malachi 3:16). And the works are recorded and repaid, as Isaiah heard: *Behold, it is written before me: I will not keep silence, but will recompense* (Isaiah 65:6). Enoch saw the scene itself, twice. *In those days I saw the Head of Days when He seated himself upon the throne of His glory, And the books of the living were opened before Him: And all His host which is in heaven above and His counsellors stood before Him,* (1 Enoch 47:3). *And I saw till a throne was erected in the pleasant land, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep sat Himself thereon, and the other took the sealed books and opened those books before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:20). And the book of life is named already in the Apocalypse: *the book of life of the Lamb slain from the foundation of the world* (Revelation 13:8), the names written before the world was. The books of works and the book of life are opened together, and *And whosoever was not found written in the book of life was cast into the lake of fire.* (Revelation 20:15).
2423.note: The 90:12 quote was invented; replaced with the live 90:20; 47:3, Revelation 20:12, 20:15 and Daniel 7:10 quoted in full from the index; the rest kept.

2434.title: The tree of life, and the leaves for the healing of the nations — Eden restored (Genesis 2, Ezekiel 47, 1 Enoch 24–25, 2 Esdras 8)
2434.summary_md: The story closes where it opened, in a garden, but the garden has become a city, and the tree once guarded stands open in the street: *In the midst of the street of it, and on either side of the river, was there the tree of life, which bare twelve manner of fruits, and yielded her fruit every month: and the leaves of the tree were for the healing of the nations.* (Revelation 22:2). This is the very tree of Eden, *the tree of life also in the midst of the garden* (Genesis 2:9). It stood in the midst of the garden at the first; it stands in the midst of the street at the last. After the fall the way to it was shut: *lest he put forth his hand, and take also of the tree of life, and eat, and live for ever* (Genesis 3:22), and *Cherubims, and a flaming sword which turned every way* were set *to keep the way of the tree of life* (Genesis 3:24). Now the guard is withdrawn and the tree is given back to the obedient (Revelation 22:14). It is Ezekiel's river-tree fulfilled, the trees by the temple-waters that bore *new fruit according to his months,* whose *fruit thereof shall be for meat, and the leaf thereof for medicine* (Ezekiel 47:12); the monthly fruit and the healing leaf are John's twelve manner of fruits and leaves for the healing of the nations. Enoch saw this tree and could not stop looking at it: *And amongst them was a tree such as I had never yet smelt, neither was any amongst them nor were others like it: it had a fragrance beyond all fragrance, and its leaves and blooms and wood wither not for ever: and its fruit is beautiful, and its fruit resembles the dates of a palm.* (1 Enoch 24:4). He was told when it would be eaten and where it would stand: *And as for this fragrant tree no mortal is permitted to touch it till the great judgement, when He shall take vengeance on all and bring (everything) to its consummation for ever. It shall then be given to the righteous and holy.* (1 Enoch 25:4). *Its fruit shall be for food to the elect: it shall be transplanted to the holy place, to the temple of Yahuah (Lord), the Eternal King.* (1 Enoch 25:5). John is looking at the transplanting done, the tree kept till the great judgment now standing in the holy city for the righteous to eat. And 2 Esdras names the whole vision in one breath: *to you is paradise opened, the tree of life is planted... a city is builded* (2 Esdras 8:52), one hope and not three, Eden become the new Jerusalem. So the promise sworn at the book's opening is kept at its close: *To him that overcometh will I give to eat of the tree of life, which is in the midst of the paradise of Elohim (God)* (Revelation 2:7). The paradise of Elohim (God) is Eden restored; the overcomer eats of the tree at last, and its leaves heal the nations.
2434.note: The old 24:11 does not exist live (its words are 25:5); 24:4 and 25:4-5 quoted in full from the live text; title updated to 1 Enoch 24–25; the rest kept with dashes eased.

1925.title: Sardis: a name that thou livest and art dead — the book of life, names not blotted out (Exodus 32, Daniel 12)
1925.summary_md: To Sardis, the assembly with *a name that thou livest, and art dead* (Revelation 3:1), the slain and living one speaks of the book that decides the living from the dead. The overcomer *shall be clothed in white raiment; and I will not blot out his name out of the book of life, but I will confess his name before my Father, and before his angels* (Revelation 3:5). The book is not new. It is the book Moses pleaded over at the foot of Sinai, *blot me, I pray thee, out of thy book which thou hast written* (Exodus 32:32), and the book whose blotting answers sin, *Whosoever hath sinned against me, him will I blot out of my book* (Exodus 32:33). It is the book Daniel saw run the deliverance: *at that time thy people shall be delivered, every one that shall be found written in the book* (Daniel 12:1). It is the book the psalmist named against the persecutors: *Let them be blotted out of the book of the living, and not be written with the righteous* (Psalm 69:28). Enoch keeps the same picture whole. To the righteous: *I swear unto you, that in heaven the angels remember you for good before the glory of the Great One: and your names are written before the glory of the Great One.* (1 Enoch 104:1). Of the sinners: *And wait ye indeed till sin has passed away, for their names shall be blotted out of the book of life and out of the holy books, and their seed shall be destroyed for ever, and their spirits shall be slain, and they shall cry and make lamentation in a place that is a chaotic wilderness, and in the fire shall they burn; for there is no earth there.* (1 Enoch 108:3). So the warning to Sardis sits inside a promise. The name written can be struck, and therefore *be watchful, and strengthen the things which remain, that are ready to die* (Revelation 3:2); keep the place in the book that defiling the garments would forfeit. And the promise closes with the confessing the Messiah spoke of in the gospel: *Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven.* (Matthew 10:32); *Also I say unto you, Whosoever shall confess me before men, him shall the Son of Adam also confess before the angels of Elohim (God):* (Luke 12:8). The overcomer who held the name on earth is owned by name before the Father and his angels, the Formed Son confessing his own before the Formless.
1925.note: The 104:1-3 quote was not the live wording; 104:1 and 108:3 quoted in full from the live text; the rest kept.

1955.title: The elders cast their crowns, and the myriads before the throne (1 Enoch 40, Nehemiah 9)
1955.summary_md: Round about the throne sit *four and twenty elders... clothed in white raiment; and they had on their heads crowns of gold* (Revelation 4:4); and when the living creatures give glory, *The four and twenty elders fall down before him that sat on the throne, and worship him that liveth for ever and ever, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying,* (Revelation 4:10). They lay their own crowns down before the only One who is worthy. Enoch stood in front of the same worship and could not count it: *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). He had seen the throne they stand before as well: *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). The enthroned elders are part of that host. And Nehemiah's Levites confessed the ground of it all: *thou, even thou, art Yahuah (LORD) alone; thou hast made heaven, the heaven of heavens, with all their host... and the host of heaven worshippeth thee* (Nehemiah 9:6). The host that worships the Maker in the Levites' prayer is the host that gives *glory and honour and thanks to him that sat on the throne* (Revelation 4:9) in John's vision. The elders cast down their crowns because the throne is the Creator's throne, and every crown of gold goes back to the One who made the heads that wear them.
1955.note: The 40:1 quote was in old wording; re-quoted live, with 14:22 added for the ten-thousand-times-ten-thousand before the throne; the rest kept.

1961.title: Ten thousand times ten thousand — the myriads before the throne (Daniel 7, 1 Enoch)
1961.summary_md: Around the throne John hears a host beyond counting take up the praise of the Lamb: *And I beheld, and I heard the voice of many angels round about the throne and the beasts and the elders: and the number of them was ten thousand times ten thousand, and thousands of thousands;* (Revelation 5:11). The count is Daniel's, word for word: *A fiery stream issued and came forth from before him: thousand thousands ministered unto him, and ten thousand times ten thousand stood before him: the judgment was set, and the books were opened.* (Daniel 7:10). Daniel saw that court before the Ancient of days; John sees it round about the throne, lifting its voice to the Lamb who has just taken the book. Enoch counted the same way when he was carried up: *The flaming fire was round about Him, and a great fire stood before Him, and none around could draw nigh Him: ten thousand times ten thousand (stood) before Him, yet He needed no counsellor.* (1 Enoch 14:22). *And after that I saw thousands of thousands and ten thousand times ten thousand, I saw a multitude beyond number and reckoning, who stood before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:1). And he heard what the host's voices were for: *The first voice blesses Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits for ever and ever.* (1 Enoch 40:4). *And the second voice I heard blessing the Elect One and the elect ones who hang upon Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 40:5). The One on the throne blessed, and the Elect One beside him blessed, is exactly the shape of Revelation 5, where the One who sits and the Lamb are praised together. The host's cry is the sevenfold one: *Saying with a loud voice, Worthy is the Lamb that was slain to receive power, and riches, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.* (Revelation 5:12). The court that could not be counted before the Father now lifts its voice to the slain Lamb.
1961.note: The 40:1 quote was in old wording and 14:21 was cited for words that are 14:22; re-quoted 40:1, 14:22, and added 40:4-5 for the two voices; the rest kept.

571.title: The rich man and Lazaros — Sheol with its divisions, and *they have Mosheh and the prophets*
571.summary_md: Lazaros, full of sores and laid at the gate with the dogs licking him, dies and *was carried by the angels into Abraham’s bosom: the rich man also died, and was buried;* (Luke 16:22). *And in hell he lift up his eyes, being in torments, and seeth Abraham afar off, and Lazarus in his bosom.* (Luke 16:23). The dead in this parable remember, the rich man knows he has five brothers; they see, across a gulf; they are still themselves, Lazaros still Lazaros and the rich man still the rich man. And the two places are divided: *And beside all this, between us and you there is a great gulf fixed: so that they which would pass from hence to you cannot; neither can they pass to us, that would come from thence.* (Luke 16:26). Two inherited teachings both stumble here. The one that says the dead sleep without knowing anything has to explain away a conversation. The one that says the torment is the final and eternal state has to ignore that this is Sheol before the resurrection, a holding place and not a verdict. Enoch was shown the holding place and told how it is arranged: *And he answered me and said unto me: ‘These three have been made that the spirits of the dead might be separated. And such a division has been made for the spirits of the righteous, in which there is the bright spring of water.* (1 Enoch 22:9). *And such has been made for sinners when they die and are buried in the earth and judgement has not been executed on them in their lifetime.* (1 Enoch 22:10). *Here their spirits shall be set apart in this great pain till the great day of judgement and punishment and torment of those who curse for ever and retribution for their spirits. There He shall bind them for ever.* (1 Enoch 22:11). Awake, divided, and waiting for the great day: that is what the rich man is doing, and the parable only makes sense if that is where he is. Then the parable turns to the living. The rich man wants a messenger sent to his brothers, and Abraham answers, *they have Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets; let them hear them. If they hear not Mosheh (Moses) and the prophets, neither will they be persuaded, though one rose from the dead* (Luke 16:29, 31). That is the King's standing test against every gospel that sets the Torah aside, and it was proved in the open when another Lazaros was raised at John 11 and the chief priests set about killing him. Five brothers, the leadership of the house of Yahudah (Judah), who would not hear Moses, and so did not believe when one rose.
571.note: Degraded 'framework-honest / FRAMEWORK-MAJOR / member-row' prose rewritten in plain words; 22:9-11 quoted in full from the live text; Luke 16:22, 23, 26 from the index; the old vv.29, 31 quote kept; title plainer.

199.title: The righteous shall shine as the sun in the kingdom of their Father — 1 Enoch 104, 2 Esdras 7, Wisdom of Solomon 3
199.summary_md: When the King explains the tares he ends with what the wheat will look like once the field is cleared: *Then shall the righteous shine forth as the sun in the kingdom of their Father. Who hath ears to hear, let him hear.* (Matthew 13:43). Daniel heard it first: *And they that be wise shall shine as the brightness of the firmament; and they that turn many to righteousness as the stars for ever and ever.* (Daniel 12:3). And the rest of the library says it in the same words. Enoch, to the righteous who have been shamed: *Be hopeful; for aforetime ye were put to shame through ill and affliction; but now ye shall shine as the lights of heaven, ye shall shine and ye shall be seen, and the portals of heaven shall be opened to you.* (1 Enoch 104:2). Ezra is shown the orders of the righteous after death, and *the sixth order, when it is shewed them how their face shall shine as the sun, and how they shall be made like unto the light of the stars, being henceforth incorruptible* (2 Esdras 7:97), and later that *the faces of them which have used abstinence shall shine above the stars* (2 Esdras 7:125). Solomon sets the shining on the day of visitation, in harvest language: *in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble* (Wisdom of Solomon 3:7). Sparks among the stubble is the same picture as the parable, the righteous bright against the burning tares on the day the two are separated. The shining belongs to the wheat that was gathered and came through the sifting with fruit on it, and the King says so by putting the sentence where he puts it, right after the tares are bound and burned.
199.note: Internal shorthand (four moves, FRAMEWORK-MAJOR, Red Line #11) rewritten; 104:2 quoted in full from the live text; Daniel and Matthew from the index; 2 Esdras and Wisdom kept as the old summary quoted them; title cleaned.

203.title: The seed war from Genesis 3 forward, with the devil as the source of death — Wisdom of Solomon 2:24, 1 Enoch 22, Jubilees 4
203.summary_md: *The field is the world; the good seed are the children of the kingdom; but the tares are the children of the wicked one;* (Matthew 13:38). *The enemy that sowed them is the devil; the harvest is the end of the world; and the reapers are the angels.* (Matthew 13:39). Two seeds in one field, and the devil the one who sowed the second. The library had been saying this since the garden. Solomon names the devil as the source of death itself: *through envy of the devil came death into the world: and they that do hold of his side do find it* (Wisdom of Solomon 2:24). The first fruit of that seed was Cain, and Enoch was shown his brother's spirit still crying out: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit.* (1 Enoch 22:5). *Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: ‘This spirit—whose is it, whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?’* (1 Enoch 22:6). *And he answered me saying: ‘This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.’* (1 Enoch 22:7). Abel's suit is against a seed, not only a man. Jubilees tells the murder the way Genesis does, *Qayin (Cain) slew Hevel (Abel) because (God) accepted the sacrifice of Hevel (Abel), and did not accept the offering of Qayin (Cain) ... and his blood cried from the ground to heaven* (Jubilees 4:2), and John names which seed Cain was: *Not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother. And wherefore slew he him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother’s righteous.* (1 John 3:12). So the parable is not a new idea about the world. The serpent in the garden, the envy that brought death in, the Watchers' corruption, the tares in the field, and the harvest where the angels sort them are one story, and Abel's voice has been making suit through all of it until the seed that killed him is gone from among the seed of men.
203.note: Internal shorthand rewritten; 22:5-7 quoted in full from the live text; Matthew and 1 John from the index; Wisdom and Jubilees kept as the old summary quoted them; title cleaned.

27.title: The Son of Adam named before creation
27.summary_md: The Parables of Enoch name the Son of Adam before anything was made. *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). *Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:3). *And for this reason hath he been chosen and hidden before Him, Before the creation of the world and for evermore.* (1 Enoch 48:6). The one who was named first is then seated: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). And at the close of the third Parable his name is made known to the holy ones and they rejoice: *And there was great joy amongst them, And they blessed and glorified and extolled Because the name of that Son of Adam had been revealed unto them.* (1 Enoch 69:26). John says the same of the Word: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* (John 1:1). Micah says it of the ruler out of Bethlehem, *whose goings forth have been from of old, from everlasting* (Micah 5:2). The one with a name before the stars, who was with the Father and went forth from him, is the one who appeared and spoke and walked with the fathers all through the Torah and the prophets. And then the name that was hidden is spoken to Joseph by an angel: *And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name Yahusha (JESUS): for he shall save his people from their sins.* (Matthew 1:21), and set beside it, Immanuel, Elohim (God) with us (Matthew 1:23). Enoch knew the name was there before the gospel ever announced it.
27.note: Degraded 'extras-tier / Red Line #12 / the framework reads' prose rewritten; 48:2-3, 48:6, 62:2 (the old 62:1 citation's thought), 69:26 quoted in full from the live text; John 1:1, Micah 5:2, Matthew 1:21 from the index.

186.title: The Spirit-anointed Elect One — the spirit of wisdom and the spirit of righteousness poured out on the Son in 1 Enoch 49 and 62
186.summary_md: Matthew explains the King's quiet ministry by quoting Isaiah: *Behold my servant, whom I have chosen; my beloved, in whom my soul is well pleased: I will put my spirit upon him, and he shall shew judgment to the Gentiles.* (Matthew 12:18). The prophet's own words are these: *Behold my servant, whom I uphold; mine elect, in whom my soul delighteth; I have put my spirit upon him: he shall bring forth judgment to the Gentiles.* (Isaiah 42:1). Isaiah had already said what that Spirit would be: *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD);* (Isaiah 11:2). Enoch saw the same Spirit on the same chosen one and calls him by Isaiah's word, the Elect One. *For wisdom is poured out like water, And glory faileth not before him for evermore.* (1 Enoch 49:1). *And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 49:3). And when he is seated to judge: *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits seated him on the throne of His glory, And the spirit of righteousness was poured out upon him, And the word of his mouth slays all the sinners, And all the unrighteous are destroyed from before his face.* (1 Enoch 62:2). Isaiah's servant, Enoch's Elect One, and the man the Spirit came down on at the Jordan are one. In this age the anointing shows itself in the way Matthew goes on to describe, a bruised reed he will not break and no voice raised in the streets. At the throne of glory it shows itself as the word of his mouth bringing judgment to victory, which is where Matthew's quotation ends and where Enoch's Parable sits.
186.note: Internal shorthand rewritten; 49:1, 49:3, 62:2 quoted in full (live); Matthew 12:18, Isaiah 42:1 and 11:2 in full from the index.

40.title: The Spirit of Wisdom on the Elect One
40.summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus), when he was baptized, went up straightway out of the water: and, lo, the heavens were opened unto him, and he saw the Spirit of Elohim (God) descending like a dove, and lighting upon him:* (Matthew 3:16). The Spirit that came down at the Jordan was not new to the library. Solomon had described her at length, *holy, one only, manifold, subtil, lively, clear, undefiled* and more, and said where she comes from: *the breath of the power of Yahuah (God), and a pure influence flowing from the glory of the Almighty* (Wisdom of Solomon 7:25). The dove coming down is that breath made visible, going out from the Father and resting on the Son. Enoch saw the resting itself: *And in him dwells the spirit of wisdom, And the spirit which gives insight, And the spirit of understanding and of might, And the spirit of those who have fallen asleep in righteousness.* (1 Enoch 49:3). It is Isaiah's list for the Branch: *And the spirit of Yahuah (LORD) shall rest upon him, the spirit of wisdom and understanding, the spirit of counsel and might, the spirit of knowledge and of the fear of Yahuah (LORD);* (Isaiah 11:2). The Spirit in these books is Yahuah's own breath, flowing from his glory and resting on the one he chose, and that is the Spirit the gospel inherits at the immersion, before anyone had built a grid of three equal persons to put her in.
40.note: Degraded prose rewritten in plain words; 49:3 quoted in full; Isaiah 11:2 and Matthew 3:16 from the index; Wisdom 7 kept as the old summary quoted it.

73.title: Spirits from the giants and the demons partially restrained — 1 Enoch 15-16 and Jubilees 10
73.summary_md: When the two demoniacs at Gergesa cry out, *what have we to do with thee, Yahusha (Jesus), thou Son of Elohim (God)? art thou come hither to torment us before the time?* (Matthew 8:29), they are speaking as creatures who know where they came from and what day is waiting for them. The book of Enoch tells both. The spirits that trouble men are the spirits of the giants, the children the Watchers begot on the daughters of men: *Evil spirits have proceeded from their bodies; because they are born from men and from the holy Watchers is their beginning and primal origin; they shall be evil spirits on earth, and evil spirits shall they be called.* (1 Enoch 15:9). Their work on the earth is named without softening: *And the spirits of the giants afflict, oppress, destroy, attack, do battle, and work destruction on the earth, and cause trouble: they take no food, but nevertheless hunger and thirst, and cause offences.* (1 Enoch 15:11). And they have a day fixed for them, which they know: *From the days of the slaughter and destruction and death of the giants, from the souls of whose flesh the spirits, having gone forth, shall destroy without incurring judgement—thus shall they destroy until the day of the consummation, the great judgement in which the age shall be consummated, over the Watchers and the godless, yea, shall be wholly consummated."* (1 Enoch 16:1). Jubilees carries the story past the flood, when *the unclean demons began to lead astray the children of the sons of Noah; and to make to err and destroy them.* (Jubilees 10:1), and tells how their chief pleaded to keep a portion of them loose: *the chief of the spirits, Mastêmâ, came and said: Yahuah (God), Creator, let some of them remain before me ... for if some of them are not left to me, I shall not be able to execute the power of my will on the sons of men.* (Jubilees 10:8). A tenth part was left him, subject before Satan on the earth, and the rest were bound in the place of condemnation (Jubilees 10:11). So the fear in the demons' mouth at Matthew 8:29 is not a strange outburst. They are the spirits of the giants, left loose for a season, and the one standing in front of them is the Judge of the day Enoch said they would destroy until. They know the time has not yet come, and they know who sets it.
73.note: READ: the gloss cited 15:9 for words that live at 15:11 and carried "architecture" chains; rewritten with every verse quoted in full

433.title: Psalm 110:1 — David's Lord, the Formed at the right hand of the Formless
433.summary_md:
*David himself said by the Ruach HaKodesh (Holy Spirit), Yahuah (the LORD) said to my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand* (Mark 12:36). Yahusha (Jesus) puts the question to the temple crowd and lets it hang: David called the Messiah his Lord, so the son of David is more than David's son. The psalm itself says it plainly: *Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool.* (Psalm 110:1). The first Lord is Yahuah speaking; the second is the one David bows to as his own sovereign. One speaks, the other sits at his right hand. That is the Father, who has no form, speaking to the Son, who is his form made visible, and it is Yahusha's own mouth that hands the people the verse in the days before the cross. Peter preaches the same verse at Pentecost (*Yahuah (the LORD) said unto my Lord,* Acts 2:34), Hebrews opens with it (*sit on my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool,* Hebrews 1:13), and Paul carries the footstool forward to the end of the reign (*for he must reign, till he hath put all enemies under his feet,* 1 Corinthians 15:25).

Enoch saw the same throne and the same two figures. The one who sits was named before anything was made: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). And the Head of Days speaks of him as his own: *On that day Mine Elect One shall sit on the throne of glory And shall try their works, And their places of rest shall be innumerable. And their souls shall grow strong within them when they see Mine elect ones, And those who have called upon My glorious name:* (1 Enoch 45:3). The seat at the right hand is not two gods and it is not one person in two poses. It is the Father and the Son he brought forth, in the relation they have always had, written into the one verse of the Psalms the apostles quote more than any other.
433.note: READ: 45:3 reworded in the live text; the gloss only cited — now quotes 48:2 and 45:3 in full; "architecture" prose replaced

14801.title: Sodom and the Watchers changed the order of nature
14801.summary_md: Naphtali warns his children not to become as Sodom, which changed the order of nature, nor as the Watchers who likewise changed the order of their nature, whom Yahuah (the LORD) cursed at the flood. The Gentiles forsook their Maker and served stocks and stones; the children of Elohim (God) must not. It ain't new — Genesis tells of Sodom and of the sons of Elohim (God) who took wives of the daughters of men, Enoch tells how the Watchers left their own high place and corrupted the earth, and Jude sets both side by side as a warning of the vengeance reserved for them: *And the angels which kept not their first estate, but left their own habitation, he hath reserved in everlasting chains under darkness unto the judgment of the great day.* (Jude 1:6).
14801.note: READ: the mention of 1 Enoch is a true summary of the book (chs 6-16); left the gloss, restored the names in prose, and added Jude 1:6 from the index so the apostles' warning is on the page

102.title: The Animal Apocalypse — shepherds judged, new house built, sheep gathered (1 Enoch 90)
102.summary_md: *But when he saw the multitudes, he was moved with compassion on them, because they fainted, and were scattered abroad, as sheep having no shepherd.* (Matthew 9:36). Ezekiel had already told Yashar'el (Israel) whose fault that was: *Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I am against the shepherds; and I will require my flock at their hand, and cause them to cease from feeding the flock; neither shall the shepherds feed themselves any more; for I will deliver my flock from their mouth, that they may not be meat for them.* (Ezekiel 34:10), and he had promised the one shepherd who would take their place: *And I will set up one shepherd over them, and he shall feed them, even my servant David; he shall feed them, and he shall be their shepherd.* (Ezekiel 34:23). Enoch saw the whole of it in his second dream, where the flock is given over to seventy shepherds who kill more than they were told to. When the Lord of the sheep comes, the record is opened first: *And I saw that man, who wrote the book according to the command of Yahuah (Lord), till he opened that book concerning the destruction which those twelve last shepherds had wrought, and showed that they had destroyed much more than their predecessors, before Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:17). Then the shepherds answer for the flock: *And those seventy shepherds were judged and found guilty, and they were cast into that fiery abyss.* (1 Enoch 90:25). Then the old house is folded up and a new one set in its place: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep brought a new house greater and loftier than that first, and set it up in the place of the first which had been folded up: all its pillars were new, and its ornaments were new and larger than those of the first, the old one which He had taken away, and all the sheep were within it.* (1 Enoch 90:29). And the scattered come home to it: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). So when Yahusha (Jesus) looks at the crowds and sees sheep with no shepherd, he is looking at the flock Ezekiel described and Enoch watched, and he is the shepherd both of them said would come for it.
102.note: READ: the gloss cited 90:16-18 for things that live at 90:17, 90:25, 90:29, 90:33 and referred the reader to an internal file (matthew-9.md §7); rewritten with the verses quoted in full and Ezekiel 34 on the page

400.title: The blood of Hevel (Abel) crying and the mother hen gathering — 1 Enoch 22 and 2 Esdras 1 beside Matthew 23:29-39
400.summary_md: The seventh woe ends with blood. *That upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth, from the blood of righteous Abel unto the blood of Zacharias son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.* (Matthew 23:35). Yahusha (Jesus) reaches back to the first murder and forward to the last one recorded in the Hebrew order of the books, and lays the whole line of slain prophets at the feet of the men who were building the prophets' tombs. The ground had been crying the whole time: *And he said, What hast thou done? the voice of thy brother’s blood crieth unto me from the ground.* (Genesis 4:10). Enoch was shown where that cry goes. In the mountain in the west, among the hollow places where the souls of the dead wait for the day of judgement, one voice goes up louder than the rest: *I saw the spirits of the children of men who were dead, and their voice went forth to heaven and made suit. Then I asked Raphael the angel who was with me, and I said unto him: 'This spirit—whose is it, whose voice goeth forth and maketh suit?' And he answered me saying: 'This is the spirit which went forth from Abel, whom his brother Cain slew, and he makes his suit against him till his seed is destroyed from the face of the earth, and his seed is annihilated from amongst the seed of men.'* (1 Enoch 22:5-7). Abel is still making his suit, and it is a suit against a seed, not against one man. That is why the woe is addressed to *Ye serpents, ye generation of vipers, how can ye escape the damnation of hell?* (Matthew 23:33). The men who killed the prophets and were about to kill the Son are the seed Abel's blood has been pleading against since the field outside Eden, sown in among the people and wearing the priest's robe, and the judgement that falls on them is not a judgement on the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The same chapter of Enoch shows the hollow places divided, the righteous by their spring of water, the sinners kept for the great day, and those who were slain making their disclosure against the ones who slew them, so the damnation of Gehenna the woe names is a holding and a judgement, not the endless torture the pulpit painted over it. Then the voice changes. *O Jerusalem, Jerusalem, thou that killest the prophets, and stonest them which are sent unto thee, how often would I have gathered thy children together, even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings, and ye would not!* (Matthew 23:37). Ezra had heard the Father say the same thing in the same words, that he gathered them as a hen gathers her chickens under her wings, that he sent them prophets whom they took and slew, and that their house is desolate (2 Esdras 1:30-33). The Son speaks with the Father's own voice and the Father's own grief. The judgement on the shepherds is what clears the ground for the gathering, as Ezekiel 34 lays it out, and the lament is not a door shut on the city. It is the Father's heart toward the children of the broken-off, who will yet be brought home out of the nations the way the prophets said they would be.
400.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; old cited 22:7 as the prison of the angels and 22:14 for Abel — Abel is 22:5-7 in the live text; quoted in full; 2 Esdras named in prose (not in the verse pool); title cleaned

397.title: The corrupted priesthood and the proselyte made twofold — Testament of Levi, 1 Enoch 99, Wisdom of Solomon beside Matthew 23:13-22
397.summary_md: The first three woes are aimed at a priesthood. They shut up the kingdom of heaven against men and will not go in themselves, they split hairs over which oath binds and which does not, and in between those two stands the woe that names what the whole system was doing: *Woe unto you, scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! for ye compass sea and land to make one proselyte, and when he is made, ye make him twofold more the child of hell than yourselves.* (Matthew 23:15). The proselyte was told that becoming a Yahudi (Jew) by the rite would save him, and then he was handed a Torah buried under traditions that voided it, so he ended up worse off than the men who made him. Paul fights the same gospel in Galatia a generation later, and it is still being preached today under other names, wherever a system tells a man that joining it is salvation and then teaches him against the commandments. Enoch had already described the men who do this: *Woe to them who pervert the words of uprightness, And transgress the eternal law, And transform themselves into what they were not [into sinners]: They shall be trodden under foot upon the earth.* (1 Enoch 99:2). Perverting the words of uprightness while transgressing the eternal law is the proselyte-maker's trade exactly, and the man he makes is transformed into what he was not. The Testament of Levi had warned the priests themselves that they would deal lawlessly with Yashar'el (Israel) until the veil of the temple was rent, and that the priests of the last times would be idolaters, adulterers, lovers of money, proud and lawless, and the Wisdom of Solomon tells the ministers of the kingdom that they will be judged because they did not judge aright nor keep the law. The test is the same one John gives: whoever says he knows him and does not keep his commandments is a liar. Hold that against any priesthood, in any age, and the woes find their mark. The mark is the system, not the people under it. The King speaking the woes is himself a Yahudi (Jew), so are the apostles, so are the crowds in front of him, and the chapter ends not with their rejection but with his lament over the children he would have gathered.
397.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose with framework labels and internal file references; 99:2 quoted in full (it stands); Testament of Levi / Wisdom 6 / 1 John 2 named in prose because their text is not in the verse pool; title cleaned

401.title: The days of Noach (Noah) and the judgement that took them all away — 1 Enoch 10, 65, 67 and Jubilees 5 beside Matthew 24:37-39
401.summary_md: *But as the days of Noe were, so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be. For as in the days that were before the flood they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, until the day that Noe entered into the ark, And knew not until the flood came, and took them all away; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:37-39). Yahusha (Jesus) does not pick the flood at random. The days of Noah are the days the Watchers had corrupted the earth, and the whole book of Enoch is the record of how that judgement was decided and carried out. The warning to Noah comes first: *'Go to Noah and tell him in my name "Hide thyself!" and reveal to him the end that is approaching: that the whole earth will be destroyed, and a deluge is about to come upon the whole earth, and will destroy all that is on it.* (1 Enoch 10:2). The reason is spelled out to him later by his grandfather: *And He said unto me: "Because of their unrighteousness their judgement has been determined upon and shall not be withheld by Me for ever. Because of the sorceries which they have searched out and learnt, the earth and those who dwell upon it shall be destroyed."* (1 Enoch 65:10), and the ones who taught the sorceries are given their own sentence: *And He will imprison those angels, who have shown unrighteousness, in that burning valley which my grandfather Enoch had formerly shown to me in the west among the mountains of gold and silver and iron and soft metal and tin.* (1 Enoch 67:4). Jubilees describes the same earth: *And lawlessness increased on the earth and all flesh corrupted its way, alike men and cattle and beasts and birds and everything that walks on the earth-all of them corrupted their ways and their orders, and they began to devour each other, and lawlessness increased on the earth and every imagination of the thoughts of all men (was) thus evil continually.* (Jubilees 5:2). Lawlessness abounding is the very sign Yahusha gives for the end of the age a few verses earlier, when the love of many grows cold. So read the taking in the flood's own terms. The flood took away the ones who were not ready; it did not lift them out of trouble. When the Son of Adam comes, the one taken from the field and the one taken from the mill are taken the way the flood took the world of Noah's day, and Luke's disciples ask where, and are told where the body is, there the eagles gather. Noah and his seed were the ones preserved, kept through the judgement and not carried off by it, and Enoch hears the promise over them: *And I will make fast thy seed before me for ever and ever, and I will spread abroad those who dwell with thee: it shall not be unfruitful on the face of the earth, but it shall be blessed and multiply on the earth in the name of Yahuah (Lord).'* (1 Enoch 67:3). Jude says the whole thing in one line, quoting Enoch himself: *And Enoch also, the seventh from Adam, prophesied of these, saying, Behold, Yahuah (Lord) cometh with ten thousands of his saints,* (Jude 1:14).
401.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; old cited 65:11 and 67:1 for words that live at 65:10 and 67:4 in the live text; quoted in full with 10:2, 67:3, Jubilees 5:2, Jude 1:14; title cleaned

395.title: The Elect One at the right hand — the Parables of Enoch beside David's Lord at Matthew 22:41-46
395.summary_md: *Saying, What think ye of Messiah (Christ)? whose son is he? They say unto him, The Son of David. He saith unto them, How then doth David in spirit call him Adonai (Lord), saying, Yahuah (LORD) said unto my Lord, Sit thou on my right hand, till I make thine enemies thy footstool? If David then call him Adonai (Lord), how is he his son?* (Matthew 22:42-45). Nobody in the temple could answer him, and from that day no one dared ask him another question. The question stands on two Lords in one verse. The first is Yahuah, the Father who has no form. The second is the one David bows to, and he sits at the Father's right hand because the Father seats him there. Enoch saw this before David wrote it. He saw an old one with a head of days, and beside him another whose face was like a man's, and asked who he was: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). This Son of Adam is older than David's line, older than the stars: *And at that hour that Son of Adam was named In the presence of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his name before the Head of Days.* (1 Enoch 48:2). And the throne is given, not seized: *And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, And his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath given (them) to him and hath glorified him.* (1 Enoch 51:3); *And Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits placed the Elect One on the throne of glory. And he shall judge all the works of the holy above in the heaven, And in the balance shall their deeds be weighed.* (1 Enoch 61:8). Put the psalm and the Parables side by side and the answer to the temple's riddle is plain. The son of David is greater than David because he was named before the Head of Days before David's house existed, and he is not the Father, because the Father is the one who names him and seats him. He was hidden from the beginning and shown to the elect: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). John says the same thing in his first line: *In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with Elohim (God), and the Word was Elohim (God).* (John 1:1). So the Son is not a creature made at a point in time, and he is not the Father wearing another face, and he is not one of three equals; he is the Father's own form, brought forth from him and seated by him, which is why the whole apostolic witness keeps coming back to this psalm, from Peter at Pentecost to Hebrews to the Revelation.
395.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; 61:8 reworded and 62:7 different in the live text — all five verses quoted in full from the live chapters; title cleaned

225.title: The Elect One on the throne and the keys of the kingdom — 1 Enoch 49, 51, 62 and 69 beside Matthew 16:19
225.summary_md: *And I will give unto thee the keys of the kingdom of heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt bind on earth shall be bound in heaven: and whatsoever thou shalt loose on earth shall be loosed in heaven.* (Matthew 16:19). A steward can only hand out keys that belong to the house he serves, so the question behind the verse is whose house it is and who holds the judgement the keys administer. Enoch answers from the throne room. The Elect One stands before the Father and is given the secrets: *For he is mighty in all the secrets of righteousness, And unrighteousness shall disappear as a shadow, And have no continuance; Because the Elect One standeth before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And his glory is for ever and ever, And his might unto all generations.* (1 Enoch 49:2). He sits on the Father's throne and what he pours out is wisdom, not his own invention: *And the Elect One shall in those days sit on My throne, And his mouth shall pour forth all the secrets of wisdom and counsel: For Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath given (them) to him and hath glorified him.* (1 Enoch 51:3). He was kept hidden and then shown to the elect: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). And the whole of judgement is put into his hands: *And he sat on the throne of his glory, And the sum of judgement was given unto the Son of Adam, And he caused the sinners to pass away and be destroyed from off the face of the earth, And those who have led the world astray.* (1 Enoch 69:27). John heard the same from his own mouth: *For the Father judgeth no man, but hath committed all judgment unto the Son:* (John 5:22), *And hath given him authority to execute judgment also, because he is the Son of Adam.* (John 5:27). That is the throne the keys come down from. Isaiah had shown the pattern already in Shebna and Eliakim, the self-appointed steward put out of the house and the key of David laid on the shoulder of the one the Master chose. The scribes and priests of the second temple were Shebna; the twelve were Eliakim; and what Peter received was a stewardship under the Son's judgement, binding and loosing what the Master of the house had already bound and loosed. Any church that reads the verse as a licence to define doctrine against the Word of the house has mistaken the steward for the owner.
225.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose with an internal short.md reference; 62:7 and 69:27 different in the live text — quoted in full; John 5:22, 27 added from the pool; Isaiah 22 named in prose; title cleaned

411.title: The Elect One vindicated on the throne and the kings and the mighty condemned — 1 Enoch 46, 48, 62 and 63 beside Matthew 26:64
411.summary_md: Bound and under oath before the high priest, Yahusha (Jesus) answers with the two verses the Sanhedrin knew best: *Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, Thou hast said: nevertheless I say unto you, Hereafter shall ye see the Son of Adam sitting on the right hand of power, and coming in the clouds of heaven.* (Matthew 26:64). Sitting at the right hand is David's psalm; coming in the clouds is Daniel's night vision: *I saw in the night visions, and, behold, one like the Son of Adam came with the clouds of heaven, and came to the Ancient of days, and they brought him near before him.* (Daniel 7:13). Daniel says the figure was like a son of Adam, because the one he saw was going to take on flesh; the man in front of Caiaphas is the one Daniel's figure resembled, and he says so with the title and no comparison. Enoch had seen him by name beside the Head of Days: *And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?* (1 Enoch 46:2), and he had been told what this Son of Adam would do to men who sit in judgement seats: *And this Son of Adam whom thou hast seen Shall raise up the kings and the mighty from their seats, [And the strong from their thrones] And shall loosen the reins of the strong, And break the teeth of the sinners.* (1 Enoch 46:4). He was named before anything they ruled over was made: *Yea, before the sun and the signs were created, Before the stars of the heaven were made, His name was named before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits.* (1 Enoch 48:3). So the court that condemned him that night will one day stand in his: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9). Enoch even records what they will say when it is too late: *And splendid in every secret thing is Thy power from generation to generation, And Thy glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Thy secrets and innumerable, And Thy righteousness is beyond reckoning.* (1 Enoch 63:3). Isaiah swore the same oath for the Father, *That unto me every knee shall bow, every tongue shall swear.* (Isaiah 45:23), and Paul puts it on the name of Yahusha: *That at the name of Yahusha (Jesus) every knee should bow, of things in heaven, and things in earth, and things under the earth;* (Philippians 2:10). The ones who will bow are the kings and the mighty, the leadership that persecuted the houses of his congregations, not the Yahudim (Jews) as a people. The King on trial is of the tribe of Yahudah (Judah) himself, and so are the men who followed him out of that courtyard.
411.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; 62:9 and 63:3 different in the live text — all five Enoch verses quoted in full; Daniel 7:13 kept with its "like"; title cleaned

227.title: The gates of Sheol and the dead given back — Wisdom of Solomon, 1 Enoch 51 and 2 Esdras 4 beside Matthew 16:18
227.summary_md: *And I say also unto thee, That thou art Peter, and upon this rock I will build my church; and the gates of hell shall not prevail against it.* (Matthew 16:18). The gates of hell are the gates of Sheol, the grave, the place where the dead are held. The pulpit turned the phrase into the mouth of an everlasting furnace, but the library that Yahusha (Jesus) grew up in uses it for the power of death that came in with the curse. The Wisdom of Solomon says that Elohim (God) made not death, and has no pleasure in the destruction of the living, and that he has power of life and death, leads down to the gates of hell and brings up again. Hosea had the Father say it in his own voice: *I will ransom them from the power of the grave; I will redeem them from death: O death, I will be thy plagues; O grave, I will be thy destruction: repentance shall be hid from mine eyes.* (Hosea 13:14). And Enoch was shown the day the gates give way: *And in those days shall the earth also give back that which has been entrusted to it, And Sheol also shall give back that which it has received, And hell shall give back that which it owes.* (1 Enoch 51:1). Ezra heard the righteous waiting for that day in their chambers: *Did not the souls also of the righteous ask question of these things in their chambers, saying, How long shall I hope on this fashion? when comes the fruit of the floor of our reward?* (2 Esdras 4:35). So the promise to the assembly is a resurrection promise. The grave will take its members the way it takes everyone, and it will not be allowed to keep them, because the one who builds the assembly is the one who walked out of the tomb on the third day and holds the keys: *I am he that liveth, and was dead; and, behold, I am alive for evermore, Amen; and have the keys of hell and of death.* (Revelation 1:18). The assembly shares in his rising at the first resurrection, and Sheol gives back what it owes.
227.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; 51:1 stands and is now quoted in full; Wisdom 1:13 / 16:13 named in prose (not in the pool); Hosea 13:14 and Revelation 1:18 added from the pool

402.title: The gathering of the elect from the four winds — 1 Enoch 57, 61 and 90 beside Matthew 24:27-31
402.summary_md: *For as the lightning cometh out of the east, and shineth even unto the west; so shall also the coming of the Son of Adam be.* (Matthew 24:27). There is nothing secret about it. He comes in the clouds with power and great glory, and then the trumpet sounds: *And he shall send his angels with a great sound of a trumpet, and they shall gather together his elect from the four winds, from one end of heaven to the other.* (Matthew 24:31). Enoch heard that sound from end to end of heaven in the second Parable: *And it came to pass after this that I saw another host of wagons, and men riding thereon, and coming on the winds from the east, and from the west to the south. And the noise of their wagons was heard, and when this turmoil took place the holy ones from heaven remarked it, and the pillars of the earth were moved from their place, and the sound thereof was heard from the one end of heaven to the other, in one day.* (1 Enoch 57:1-2). And he was told that none of the elect will be missed in the gathering, not even the ones the earth had swallowed: *And these measures shall reveal all the secrets of the depths of the earth, And those who have been destroyed by the desert, And those who have been devoured by the beasts, And those who have been devoured by the fish of the sea, That they may return and stay themselves On the day of the Elect One; For none shall be destroyed before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, And none can be destroyed.* (1 Enoch 61:5). In the dream of the sheep the same gathering closes the vision: *And all that had been destroyed and dispersed, and all the beasts of the field, and all the birds of the heaven, assembled in that house, and Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep rejoiced with great joy because they were all good and had returned to His house.* (1 Enoch 90:33). The elect gathered from the four winds are the sheep, the house of Yashar'el (Israel) scattered through every nation, the ones the prophets never stopped promising to bring home: *And he shall set up an ensign for the nations, and shall assemble the outcasts of Yashar'el (Israel), and gather together the dispersed of Yahudah (Judah) from the four corners of the earth.* (Isaiah 11:12); *And say unto them, Thus saith Adonai Yahuah (the Lord GOD); Behold, I will take the children of Yashar'el (Israel) from among the heathen, whither they be gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land:* (Ezekiel 37:21). Moses, Jeremiah, Hosea, Micah, Zephaniah and Zechariah say the same thing in their own places. The gathering at the trumpet is the gathering of the twelve tribes, the paternal seed of the fathers, and not a spiritual category anyone can elect himself into.
402.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; 90:10 was cited for the gathering to the great horn — the gathering home is 90:33 in the live text; 57:1-2 and 61:5 quoted in full; Isaiah 11:12 and Ezekiel 37:21 added from the pool; title cleaned

410.title: The judgment of the kings and the mighty cast down — the Parables of Enoch beside the sheep and the goats at Matthew 25:31-46
410.summary_md: *When the Son of Adam shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him, then shall he sit upon the throne of his glory: And before him shall be gathered all nations: and he shall separate them one from another, as a shepherd divideth his sheep from the goats:* (Matthew 25:31-32). The throne of his glory is Enoch's phrase, and the Parables show who is standing in front of it. *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). The sight of him is what undoes them: *And one portion of them shall look on the other, And they shall be terrified, And they shall be downcast of countenance, And pain shall seize them, When they see that Son of Adam Sitting on the throne of his glory.* (1 Enoch 62:5). They bow too late: *And all the kings and the mighty and the exalted and those who rule the earth Shall fall down before him on their faces, And worship and set their hope upon that Son of Adam, And petition him and supplicate for mercy at his hands.* (1 Enoch 62:9), and they are handed over: *And He will deliver them to the angels for punishment, To execute vengeance on them because they have oppressed His children and His elect* (1 Enoch 62:11). Enoch even records their confession from the darkness: *For we have not believed before Him Nor glorified the name of Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, [nor glorified our Lord] But our hope was in the sceptre of our kingdom, And in our glory.* (1 Enoch 63:7). That is the goats' *Lord, when saw we thee* in another tongue, the recognition that comes after the door is shut. The fire the goats are sent toward was never made for them in the first place: *Then shall he say also unto them on the left hand, Depart from me, ye cursed, into everlasting fire, prepared for the devil and his angels:* (Matthew 25:41). It was prepared for the Watchers and their master, and Jude and Peter say the same. The goats are the unfruitful among the gathered, sifted out before the reign; the kings and the mighty who possess the earth fall at the Day with the tares abroad; and the verdict is final, *And these shall go away into everlasting punishment: but the righteous into life eternal.* (Matthew 25:46). There is no universal rescue hidden in the chapter, and there is no endless torture of the uninformed either. There is a throne, a shepherd who knows his sheep, and a door that closes.
410.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose with an internal thread reference; all five cited verses are different in the live text — 62:3, 62:5, 62:9, 62:11, 63:7 quoted in full from the live chapters; Matthew 25 verses from the pool; title cleaned

418.title: The kings and the mighty condemning the Elect One, and the Elect One vindicated on the throne of his glory — 1 Enoch 62-63 beside Matthew 27
418.summary_md: *When the morning was come, all the chief priests and elders of the people took counsel against Yahusha (Jesus) to put him to death:* (Matthew 27:1). David had seen that council: *The kings of the earth set themselves, and the rulers take counsel together, against Yahuah (LORD), and against his anointed, saying,* (Psalm 2:2). By the afternoon the same men are under the cross: *He saved others; himself he cannot save. If he be the King of Yashar'el (Israel), let him now come down from the cross, and we will believe him. He trusted in Elohim (God); let him deliver him now, if he will have him: for he said, I am the Son of Elohim (God).* (Matthew 27:42-43). Enoch saw the other end of that scene. He saw the day the kings and the mighty are summoned to look at the one they condemned: *And thus Yahuah (Lord) commanded the kings and the mighty and the exalted, and those who dwell on the earth, and said: 'Open your eyes and lift up your horns if ye are able to recognize the Elect One.'* (1 Enoch 62:1); *And there shall stand up in that day all the kings and the mighty, And the exalted and those who hold the earth, And they shall see and recognize How he sits on the throne of his glory, And righteousness is judged before him, And no lying word is spoken before him.* (1 Enoch 62:3). He could have called twelve legions of angels at Gethsemane and did not, because the one who was hidden from the beginning was walking the road the Father laid for him: *For from the beginning the Son of Adam was hidden, And the El Elyon (Most High) preserved him in the presence of His might, And revealed him to the elect.* (1 Enoch 62:7). His cry from the cross is the opening line of Psalm 22, and that psalm does not end forsaken; it ends with the Father hearing and all the ends of the earth turning to him. The Father did not abandon the Son; the Son prayed the psalm the way the Suffering Servant was always going to pray it, through to its end. And the men who mocked will one day beg for a moment's respite: *In those days shall the mighty and the kings who possess the earth implore (Him) to grant them a little respite from His angels of punishment to whom they were delivered, that they might fall down and worship before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits, and confess their sins before Him.* (1 Enoch 63:1), and they will say what they refused to say at Golgotha: *And splendid in every secret thing is Thy power from generation to generation, And Thy glory for ever and ever: Deep are all Thy secrets and innumerable, And Thy righteousness is beyond reckoning.* (1 Enoch 63:3). Paul says every knee will bow at the name of Yahusha, things in heaven, in earth and under the earth. The cross and the throne are the same figure seen from two days.
418.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose with internal thread references; 62:3, 62:7, 63:1, 63:3 different in the live text — quoted in full with 62:1; Psalm 2:2 and Matthew 27 from the pool; title cleaned

372.title: The Lord of the sheep and the gathering — 1 Enoch 40 and 89-90 beside Matthew 18:10-14
372.summary_md: *Take heed that ye despise not one of these little ones; for I say unto you, That in heaven their angels do always behold the face of my Father which is in heaven. For the Son of Adam is come to save that which was lost.* (Matthew 18:10-11). Then comes the shepherd who leaves the ninety and nine on the mountains to go after the one that strayed, and the Father's will that not one of these little ones should perish. Enoch saw the angels who stand before that face. *And he said to me: 'This first is Michael, the merciful and long- suffering: and the second, who is set over all the diseases and all the wounds of the children of men, is Raphael: and the third, who is set over all the powers, is Gabriel: and the fourth, who is set over the repentance unto hope of those who inherit eternal life, is named Phanuel.'* (1 Enoch 40:9). And in the dream of the sheep he saw the Shepherd himself, called by the name Yahuah. When the wolves of Egypt oppressed the flock, the sheep cried to their Lord, and he came down for them: *And a sheep which had been saved from the wolves fled and escaped to the wild asses; and I saw the sheep how they lamented and cried, and besought their Lord with all their might, till that Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep descended at the voice of the sheep from a lofty abode, and came to them and pastured them.* (1 Enoch 89:16). The same Lord raises up a shepherd when the beasts devour the flock, *And the dogs and the foxes and the wild boars began to devour those sheep till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep raised up [another sheep] a ram from their midst, which led them.* (1 Enoch 89:42), and when the sheep forsake his house and are given over, Enoch watches until the day the eyes of the lambs come open: *But behold lambs were borne by those white sheep, and they began to open their eyes and to see, and to cry to the sheep.* (1 Enoch 90:6). At the end the Lord of the sheep acts for them with his own hand: *And I saw till Yahuah (Lord) of the sheep came unto them and took in His hand the staff of His wrath, and smote the earth, and the earth clave asunder, and all the beasts and all the birds of the heaven fell from among those sheep, and were swallowed up in the earth and it covered them.* (1 Enoch 90:18). This is Ezekiel 34 in a dream, the Father against the shepherds who fed themselves and the one Shepherd who comes to seek the lost. The parable in Matthew works at both levels at once: the little one in the assembly who must not be despised, and the lost sheep of the house of Yashar'el (Israel) he said he was sent to. Both belong to the same Lord of the sheep, and the lambs whose eyes open are the ones who hear his voice when he calls, because they are his.
372.note: REWRITE: degraded S1xx prose; 89:42, 89:54, 90:6, 90:18 different in the live text — quoted in full from the live chapters (89:54 replaced by 89:15-16, where the Lord of the sheep comes down at their cry); title cleaned

71.title: The named Son of Adam — 1 Enoch 46 and Matthew 8:20
71.summary_md: *And Yahusha (Jesus) saith unto him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have nests; but the Son of Adam hath not where to lay his head.* (Matthew 8:20). It is the first time in Matthew that he calls himself by that name, and he uses it as a title, not as a way of saying he is only a man. The English Bibles flattened it to *son of man* and the lineage went out of it; *ben adam* is the son of Adam, the seed of the line the promise runs through. Enoch had already seen a figure called by that title standing beside the Ancient of Days: *And there I saw One who had a head of days, And His head was white like wool, And with Him was another being whose countenance had the appearance of a man, And his face was full of graciousness, like one of the holy angels.* (1 Enoch 46:1). He asked who he was: *And I asked the angel who went with me and showed me all the hidden things, concerning that Son of Adam, who he was, and whence he was, (and) why he went with the Head of Days?* (1 Enoch 46:2). And he was told: *And he answered and said unto me: This is the Son of Adam who hath righteousness, With whom dwelleth righteousness, And who revealeth all the treasures of that which is hidden, Because Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits hath chosen him, And whose lot hath the pre-eminence before Yahuah (Lord) of Spirits in uprightness for ever.* (1 Enoch 46:3). Chosen by the Father, given the first place in righteousness for ever, the one who reveals what is hidden, standing at the Father's side before he ever came in flesh: that is the Messiah in heaven before the manger. The one Enoch saw with the Head of Days is the one who told the scribe he had nowhere to lay his head. Daniel saw him too, coming with the clouds like a son of Adam, and said like, because the one he saw was going to take on flesh. Here there is no like. He names himself.
71.note: REWRITE: the old note cited a Red Line and spoke of "the Hebrew library" as a label; 46:1-3 now quoted in full; the same point in plain words

96.title: The named Son of Adam in the Parables of Enoch — named before the stars, hidden, and revealed, beside Matthew 9:6
